Holding back the Lai by hand
items.description: اکھ دی راولپنڈی دے وِچ اکّ اکّ اتھرو نالہ لئی اے In the eyes of Rawalpindi, every single tear has become the Nullah Lai Master Altaf Bahrawana, Punjabi poet It was 6:30am on the first of September in Gawalmandi and Shazia’s mother was making breakfast in the courtyard. Her feet were immersed, her clothes were soaked but she persisted with the fire even though the wood was so damp it barely responded. Shazia, 40, was sitting at the doorway, keeping one eye on the drainage pipe that opened into Nullah Lai. Their house sat on the banks of this tributary of the Soan River that functions more like a stormwater drain for Rawalpindi. Shazia kept her other eye on the tree, which served as a marker for rising water levels as it rained. They and the other families by the banks had been hoping it would not get bad. But sure enough, the water inched up past the mark ( nishani ) to rise over 20 feet, and the nullah started to top its banks and begin pooling into the houses. “ Shazia, bachyan nu utte chuk ke lai ja, ” her mother hollered. Take the children upstairs now. They moved the children to the roof first, then the parents, and then the precious mattresses, charpai and, most importantly, the fridge. Shazia and her family have lived here for six decades, so they know the nullah’s moods, its sounds, and the signs by which it warns them. They are also familiar with the accompanying drumbeat in their veins as adrenaline and anxiety flood their bodies in response to the monsoon. Nullah Lai drains a catchment of about 235 square kilometres, roughly three-fifths of it in Islamabad, before cutting through Rawalpindi’s most crowded neighbourhoods on its way to the Soan River. A funding proposal to the UN’s Adaptation Fund counted 19 floods in the nullah over 59 years and estimated that some 400,000 people in the city suffer every year. The worst came on July 23, 2001, when 620mm fell on the twin cities in roughly half a day. A study of that disaster put the death toll at 74 (64 of them in Rawalpindi), and found that nine in ten surveyed households had lost property, often down to their pots and pans. But the record cannot show what decades of living beside Nullah Lai have taught these women: not simply how to survive a flood, but how to make a life around its return. Master Altaf’s verse, ‘In the eyes of Rawalpindi, every single tear has become the Nullah Lai’ reads like reportage. It is the story of the lives of the women of Gawalmandi and Arya Mohallah, repeated year after year and resurrecting their coping mechanisms each late summer. From the roof, Shazia’s mind turned to a neighbour who was pregnant and alone. She called out but got no answer. So she went down, reached the woman, helped her to safety and stayed with her until the water fell. When it finally did, there was no drinking water and nothing to eat. The wood was soaked, the open-air stove useless, everything covered in muck. The mattresses were left to dry on the roof and the family came downstairs to begin the clean-up on empty stomachs. Eventually, food and water was sent by the youngest daughter from her home. As always, the floodwater brought its own cargo. Snakes are common, and one night Shazia’s mother felt something crawling on her back. She swatted it and found a large centipede. “This is not the first time we have seen this,” Shazia says. “I have been seeing it since I was young.” Then she offers something that sounds less a complaint and more a law of physics: “When the water has to come, it comes. It makes its own way. No one can stop it.” Nullah Lai knows the address Rukhsana, 58, came to Gawalmandi as a bride. She measures the floods against one that predates her own memory, a flood her in-laws said had not been matched in two decades. Across the water in Arya Mohallah, Ambreen, 49, who also moved there after her marriage, counts the floods by year: 2001, then 2010. “And after that, we saw even heavier rains,” she says. Each flood settles on top of the last, bigger than before. Ambreen laughs when she recalls what people tell them: “ Log humain kehte hain …people say we have encroached on the Lai. We tell them we have lived here since the time of our forefathers. We and the Lai go back a long time, our bond old as time. Lai was here before, during the time of our fathers and forefathers but now it seems to have memorized our address year after year, it turns up at our door, as if to pay respect to our elders at their graves.” The nullah has become part of their history. “ Ab hum Lai ki auratein hain,” she says. We are now the women of Lai. Ready before the rain Pre-monsoon prep for the people living around Lai is in place before any official warning is issued. “During the last flood, the deep freezer was too heavy to carry upstairs,” explains Nusrat, who is not spared damage even though she lives a kilometre away. “So this year we women decided to find a solution and raised it on the bricks.” Sewage flows back into kitchen drains and toilets when their exits are flooded. The solution is to keep toilets covered. At the doors, barricades are improvised with wooden planks and sandbags. “We have to create barriers because there isn’t any proper system,” Nusrat says. When the rain is at its heaviest, the women work the drains by hand. “We try to make a path for the water to move out. When we use the wiper, the dirt moves with the water towards the drains. That helps a little.” Houses often stock up on good wipers, mops and toilet-cleaning acid as the season approaches. The women prepare for the possibility that staying home will no longer be safe. Neighbours alert one another when levels turn critical, while families call relatives to higher ground if they need to leave. For Saima, 23, of Arya Mohallah, one precaution proved especially important. “Thank God I had kept a bag with sanitary pads, underwear, a chaddar and a spare shalwar kameez . Otherwise, it would have been very difficult because I had my period the day before. Our house was flooded with 12 feet of water.” Rukhsana cuts straight to the heart of the matter: “Things can be replaced. But a life lost cannot be.” Ambereen’s circle of care extends even further. In every flood, before saving her belongings, she carries her birds and cats to safety. “Now we don’t panic as much,” Shazia says, “because we know what work has to be done.” A solidarity has developed especially between the women. “When floods like this happen, everyone becomes one,” Shazia says. “People check on each other. They ask, ‘Is everything okay? Do you need anything?” Managing life next to a nullah that floods is labour, even if no one calls it that. The women joke that the flood doesn’t wait for a time when the men would be at home. Inevitably it’s the women who are at home when it happens and even when the waters recede. They are the ones cleaning out the diapers, waste, sanitary pads, and rubbish. “I took a shower today, after five days,” says Shazia. “And I saw bruises and marks all over my body. Something hit me here, something else hit me there.” Power and gas supplies take days to return. Ambereen’s household spent four days without electricity after its meter was damaged. In Master Altaf’s verse, the eye is where the flood gathers. In Rukhsana’s answer, it is also where the strength to face it is found. Why the water keeps coming In the opinion of town planner Abida Parveen of Shehersaaz there is no single fix here, least of all widening the drain which can’t solve a problem built into an entire catchment. “Open and permeable land has been replaced by roads, rooftops, concrete surfaces and other impervious areas,” she says. “Even if we widen the channel, we are still dealing with a much larger and faster flow of stormwater entering the system.” Rain that runs off the capital’s roads and rooftops ends up at the doorsteps of Gawalmandi. The channel carries more than rain: about 600 cusecs of sewage flow into it every day, which is why what comes up through Nusrat’s kitchen pipe is never just water but contamination, the possibility of disease, both acute and chronic. That detail is where the story refuses a simple villain. Officials point to encroachments and to garbage and debris dumped into the channel, and they are not entirely wrong: residents of some neighbourhoods along the banks have been photographed dumping waste there in defiance of bans. But Parveen cautions against letting that diagnosis harden into a verdict on the people who live there. “Calling a settlement an encroachment may describe its legal status, but it does not automatically solve the housing problem of the people living there,” she says. “The objective should not be simply to remove people from the nullah. The objective should be to reduce flood risk while ensuring that vulnerable households are not made homeless or pushed into another unsafe settlement.” Danyal Chaudhry, the member of the National Assembly for NA-57, does not dispute that response has outrun prevention. He calls for a shift “from a purely reactive approach — responding after water levels rise — to a preventive approach based on risk mapping, preparedness and timely evacuation.” For him women should not only be treated as beneficiaries of disaster-response programmes; they should also be partners in designing them. “Their experience at the household and community level can significantly improve the effectiveness of official preparedness plans.” While it sounds like the right diagnosis, for now it is also a description of something that has not yet happened. In the women’s own accounts, the early-warning system is a marked tree; the relief operation is a relative arriving with food and water; the evacuation plan is a bag packed by the door. The fear that stays Shazia’s mother no longer sleeps properly when it rains. She lies down, drifts off, and just as sleep begins to take hold, wakes and reaches for the floor to check if it is wet. Nusrat copes differently, “Haha, I have gone crazy, I keep washing the dishes again and again.” For Saima, the fear is tied to the uncertainty of what might happen to the house and the family. “Thunder, the sound of water hitting the pavement grips me with fear…I can’t help but tremble…because the memories come flooding back, the anxiety to face it all once again…it’s like life imprisonment.“ Rukhsana’s answer suggests an anxiety that has found a home in the marrow: “We stay scared and alert. That fear has never really left us.” For these women, eco-anxiety is not an abstract fear of a distant climate future. Where the tears meet the Lai The harder question is whether resilience is simply the name given to the labour people perform when the systems fail them. “There isn’t any proper arrangement to stop it,” says Ambereen. “There isn’t really a solution. If the water rises, it will come inside anyway, no matter what we do.” What they ask for is smaller than an expressway, and harder to argue with. “How can we make ourselves safe when we cannot afford the cost?” she asks. “If the government wants us to move, then give us money or land and let us build somewhere safe.” When the next heavy rain comes, the sequence will begin again in Gawalmandi and Arya Mohallah: the tree, the dash for higher ground, the children first and the mattresses after them, the toilets covered, the bag sent upstairs, the cleaning begun before the smell has settled. “We know this can happen again,” Shazia says. “We have learned how to deal with it because we have been facing it for years. We carry on. Life goes on.” All photos by authors

items.title: Rayan header salvages 1-1 draw between Brazil and Australia
items.description: A last minute header from Brazilian substitute Rayan salvaged a 1-1 draw with Australia in a thrilling international friendly in Townsville on Friday. Rayan headed the ball home in the 95th minute to deny the hosts what would have been only their second win over the South American giants. It was a fitting result from two evenly-matched teams who gave everything in front of a sell-out crowd in the North Queensland city. A superb free kick from Australian youngster Nestory Irankunda had looked enough to give the Socceroos an upset win. With the two sides locked at 0-0 midway through the second half, Irankunda stepped up and drilled his free kick over the defensive wall into the net, leaving Brazil keeper Hugo Souza rooted to the spot. But Brazil came out and dominated against an increasingly defensive Australian outfit and were rewarded seconds before full-time. With both teams looking to rebuild after early exits from this year’s World Cup, it was the Socceroos who seized the early advantage. They dominated possession and territory, attacking with width and finding plenty of space on both sides. Midfielder Connor Metcalfe went close in just the third minute before an Irankunda bullet forced a good save from Souza. Brazil weathered the storm and began to get into the game, looking increasingly dangerous through in-form Barcelona striker Raphinha and Chelsea forward Estevao. Raphinha had a good chance with a header straight to Australian keeper Patrick Beach after 20 minutes before Estevao forced a great save from Beach five minutes later. The Brazil dominance appeared to have paid off in the 46th minute when Estevao scored, but a VAR review saw the goal ruled out due to an earlier foul on Australian captain Harry Soutar. The second half saw much of the same, with Brazil controlling the centre and the Socceroos finding space out wide. The visitors were just edging the match and it seemed only a matter of time before they scored, but they were shocked by Irankunda’s superb free kick. The Socceroos defended furiously and looked to have held out for the win, but a last minute corner saw Rayan’s header just too powerful for Beach to hold out. items.title: Police arrest Niger fugitive over alleged murder of business partner
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has said that it has arrested a fugitive wanted in Niger for allegedly stabbing his compatriot and business partner to death. Kebbi Police Command image maker, SP Bashir Usman, in a statement on Friday, stated that the fugitive, identified as Masaudu Saidu, allegedly used a knife to stab his 38-year-old Nigerian business partner, Masaudu Sani. Bashir added that after allegedly committing the murder, the Nigerian tailor fled Niger and returned to Nigeria, his home country, to evade arrest. The statement further added that following his declaration as a wanted criminal by Niger authorities, the Nigerian Police began a search for him and he was subsequently arrested at Gulma Town in the Argungu Local Government Area of Kebbi State. “Yes, we have arrested a fugitive wanted in Niger Republic for stabbing his business partner to death in Niger Republic. we are currently investigating him,” Usman said. The Police urged Nigerian nationals in other countries to exhibit good character and to desist from denting the image of the country, adding that the law can catch up with any suspect no matter how long one hides. items.title: 2027: You must play according to rules, Jonathan warns politicians
items.description: …says you can’t do anything to win election By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja As campaigns for the 2027 general elections heat up, former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned politicians to play according to the rules, saying it would be wrong for candidates to manoeuvre the system just to win an election. Jonathan’s admonition appears to counter President Bola Tinubu’s earlier remark that “all is fair in politics.” Delivering a goodwill message at a public lecture held to mark the 80th birthday of a former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Kanu Agabi, SAN, ex-President Jonathan, who voluntarily conceded defeat to the opposition party in 2015, maintained that politicians cannot justify every action taken to win an election by simply describing it as politics. According to him, electoral contests must be governed by established rules, and politicians should not treat the quest for victory as justification for misconduct. He said, “In politics, it is a disaster. People do stupid things, also even criminal things, and they will tell you it is politics. It is not politics. Politics has rules. “Politics is like a soccer match. You play according to the rules, and that is why the courts step in to mediate if you go against the rules. Otherwise, you can do anything and win an election and walk away.” The erstwhile president also stressed that the anti-corruption fight in the country requires more than laws and enforcement agencies, emphasising that enduring change would depend on building a society where ethical conduct is valued above wrongdoing. “The challenge before Nigeria is not simply to make laws against corruption. It is to build a culture in which ethical conduct becomes the norm, where public office is treated as a trust, and where institutions are strong enough to uphold accountability. “We cannot continue to claim that private corruption will just keep going around in circles. It cannot go anywhere until we develop that culture, and nobody does wrong willingly,” he added. Recalling an experience in Rwanda, Jonathan said the country’s social values discourage public officials from accepting gifts that could be considered inappropriate. He said the experience demonstrated how deeply rooted social norms can influence public conduct beyond what formal laws prescribe. “I gave this to my aides to give to the people who take care of me. If you give me a hotel room where nobody can see anybody, where it is free, they say it is not the culture of Rwanda to accept the little gift — just a gift,” he said. Meanwhile, he stressed that key institutions in the country, especially the judiciary, have an important role to play in ensuring accountability when rules are violated. “All of us Nigerians have a major role to play if we want to suppress corruption, not just the bodies established by law to discipline and punish those who do it,” he stated, even as he urged politicians to exhibit higher moral standards. The post 2027: You must play according to rules, Jonathan warns politicians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UE et Canada unis face à Trump
items.description: Le Canada pourrait-il devenir le 28 e membre de l'Union européenne et ainsi remplacer le Royaume-Uni, qui l’a quittée en 2020 ? Cette hypothèse est impossible juridiquement, puisque le Canada n'est pas situé sur le continent européen, ce qui est une condition sine qua non d'une adhésion. Le rapprochement, politique, géopolitique et économique entre l'Union européenne et le Canada n’en demeure pas moins spectaculaire. Le Premier ministre canadien, Marc Carney, a assisté au discours sur l'état de l'Union prononcé devant le Parlement européen par la présidente de la commission Ursula von der Leyen le 16 septembre. Ce discours se veut la réplique du traditionnel, mais beaucoup plus suivi, discours sur l'état de l’Union que le président des États-Unis prononce chaque année en janvier. Le lendemain, Marc Carney s'est adressé au Parlement européen où il a été chaleureusement applaudi. 48 heures plus tard, il était reçu par le président Macron dans le territoire français de Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, situé au large du Canada. Ils ont affiché leur complicité et leur solidarité. Le Premier ministre canadien a appelé à une conclusion rapide d'un accord de libre-échange entre l'Union européenne et le Canada. Comment expliquer un rapprochement si appuyé ? En réalité, c’est Donald Trump qui sert d'accélérateur et d'amplificateur de ce phénomène. Le Canada est souvent perçu comme un pays européen, situé sur le continent américain. Il a les mêmes valeurs que les pays européens, le même socle civilisationnel, le même attachement au multilatéralisme et au droit international, et il n'a pas la capacité d'être une puissance impériale comme les États-Unis. Il existe par ailleurs un lien fort unissant le Canada au Royaume-Uni et à la France. Cette proximité se base sur des liens coloniaux anciens, qui ont été dénoués de façon harmonieuse et non conflictuelle. Le Canada et les Européens sont des alliés des États-Unis au sein de l'alliance atlantique, et l'un comme l'autre est désemparé par l'attitude de Donald Trump par rapport aux partenaires traditionnels de Washington. Pour le président états-unien, l'alliance est une source d'obligations automatiques dont il veut se défaire, car il estime que cela entrave la souveraineté de son pays. Par ailleurs, il a affiché ouvertement sa volonté d’annexer le Canada ainsi que le Groenland, qui appartient au Danemark, pays de l’Union européenne. Dans une carte qu'il a publiée récemment, les territoires français des Caraïbes et Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon sont également affichés comme rattachés aux États-Unis. Ces attaques de Washington expliquent l'idée selon laquelle il faudrait front commun pour opposer une résistance à un allié qui pourrait se transformer en prédateur. Le 20 janvier, Marc Carney avait fait un discours remarqué au sommet de Davos, plaidant pour l'alliance des puissances moyennes, afin de résister aux puissances impériales dans lequel il intégrait également la Russie et la Chine. Il a fait même preuve de plus de fermeté que les Européens. Ces derniers ont accepté un accord commercial inégal dans lequel les exportations américaines vers le Vieux Continent ne sont pas taxées, tandis que les exportations européennes vers les États-Unis subissent une taxation de 15 %. À l’opposé, lorsque Donald Trump a décidé de taxer les produits canadiens à hauteur de 50 %, Marc Carney a déclaré qu'il ferait la même chose « au dollar prêt ». C'est extrêmement courageux de sa part dans la mesure où l'économie du Canada est très largement dépendante du marché américain qui reçoit 75 % des exportations canadiennes. Marc Carney veut diversifier son économie et est parvenu à faire baisser ce taux à 70 %. Le Canada et les pays européens espèrent qu’en faisant front commun, ils pèsent plus par rapport à Washington. Cela n’a pas empêché Donald Trump d’annoncer la semaine dernière qu'il avait pris le contrôle total du Groenland. C'est une façon très particulière de présenter les choses. Les États-Unis avaient déjà des bases militaires sur ce territoire et l'accord signé reconnaît toujours la souveraineté pleine et entière du Danemark sur ce territoire. Il prévoit qu'il n'y aura pas de base militaire, russe ou chinoise sur le Groenland, ce qui était de toute façon inconcevable pour Copenhague. Les Européens ont décidé de laisser Trump triompher médiatiquement, l’essentiel étant pour eux le fait que Donald Trump est de plus en plus impopulaire les opinions publiques, tant européenne que canadienne. Les gouvernements font donc contre mauvaise fortune, bon cœur, pensant qu'il est indispensable de garder des liens avec le président américain, même si cela implique certaines déconvenues. L’article UE et Canada unis face à Trump est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Djirèye Clotilde Coly espère du coach « la performance » et une équipe solide
items.description: Pour son premier match à la tête des Lions, Patrick Vieira sera attendu sur le résultat et sur sa capacité à construire une équipe solide. Le ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports, Djirèye Clotilde Coly, qui s’est exprimé dans un entretien avec Le Soleil Digital, estime que le nouveau sélectionneur dispose de la légitimité et de l’expérience nécessaires pour relever ce défi. Ce vendredi, à 13 heures, à Maputo, Patrick Vieira vivra son baptême du feu sur le banc des Lions, face au Mozambique, en qualifications de la Can 2027. Et la tutelle ne cache pas sa confiance. Interrogée par Le Soleil Digital sur les objectifs assignés au nouveau sélectionneur, le ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports, Djirèye Clotilde Coly, salue en l’ancien international français « une figure emblématique du football mondial ».« C’est un sportif d’une grande valeur, qui possède une très solide expérience du haut niveau », souligne-t-elle, mettant en avant le parcours et la légitimité de Patrick Vieira. Ses attentes, elle les résume d’un mot : « la performance ». Ce premier test revêt un caractère particulier, puisque le Sénégal devait initialement recevoir son adversaire à Dakar, avant que l’ordre des rencontres ne soit inversé. Le ministre assure que l’État accompagnera l’équipe nationale tout au long de ce périple : d’abord au Mozambique, puis au Kenya, le 29 septembre, et enfin à Marseille, en France, pour un match amical contre les Comores. Elle indique qu’une réunion a été tenue avec la Fédération sénégalaise de football après la décision d’inverser les matchs, afin de revoir les différents aspects liés à l’organisation de la rencontre. « Tous les aspects logistiques, la délégation, l’accompagnement, tout cela a été revu avec la Fédération », a-t-elle précisé. Pour le ministère, le changement de programme ne modifie donc pas l’objectif : permettre aux Lions d’aborder cette première échéance dans les meilleures conditions. La Fédération garde la main sur le choix du sélectionneur Au-delà du seul résultat face au Mozambique, le ministre attend de Patrick Vieira qu’il pose les bases d’une équipe capable de s’inscrire dans la durée. « Les attentes portent également sur la construction ou la consolidation d’une équipe solide », a-t-elle expliqué, en référence aux nombreuses individualités de haut niveau dont dispose la sélection. Le défi du nouveau sélectionneur sera ainsi de transformer ce potentiel individuel en force collective, dès les premières échéances. Djirèye Clotilde Coly a par ailleurs rappelé que le choix de Patrick Vieira relève de la Fédération sénégalaise de football, conformément à l’autonomie dont elle jouit. Le ministère, précise-t-elle, intervient principalement sur les questions de gouvernance, en veillant notamment au respect des critères de sélection et aux conditions de contractualisation. « C’est elle (la fédération) qui choisit le sélectionneur », a souligné le ministre, le rôle de la tutelle étant de s’assurer que le processus respecte le cadre institutionnel et l’intérêt général. Sur la décision de faire jouer le match aller au Mozambique, le ministre des Sports indique que la Fédération a avancé des arguments techniques que le ministère « accepte ». Elle rappelle toutefois que le stade Léopold Sédar Senghor avait obtenu une homologation temporaire de la Caf et que son plan de mise à niveau se poursuit. Elle appelle surtout la Fédération à davantage d’anticipation, afin d’éviter les changements de dernière minute, qui peuvent avoir, selon elle, des conséquences sportives, organisationnelles et financières. Mais désormais, l’attention se tourne vers le terrain. Dès ce vendredi, Patrick Vieira et les Lions devront réussir leur entrée dans les qualifications de la Can 2027, prévue du 19 juin au 17 juillet au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda. items.title: English, Spanish, Italian, German football leagues call for FIFA reform
items.description: The four main European football leagues — the English Premier League, Spain’s La Liga, Italy’s Serie A and Germany’s Bundesliga — called on Friday for a reform of FIFA. The sport’s governing body has been mired in crisis since the revelation of a plan, since shelved, to create a commercial company FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would be open to private investors. “Fundamental governance reform is essential to restore clear constitutional boundaries within FIFA, including confidence that individual disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference,” the four leagues wrote in a statement sent to AFP. “We are speaking up together, as founding members of European Leagues and the World Leagues Association, because we understand how FIFA’s relentless expansionism affects everyone.” The statement comes just days after FIFA president Gianni Infantino — who has come under fire since the FFE plan to bring private investment into the men’s and women’s World Cups — proposed “a consultation” of the national federations in order to reform the body’s governance. “The FIFA president has now acknowledged the need for reform, but it is not enough for surface-level, process changes to be explored in the aftermath of FFE,” stated the four main European leagues, who went on to describe the project as “one of the biggest abuses of power in FIFA’s history”. The four leagues, however, steered away from putting all the blame on Infantino’s shoulders. “FIFA’s governance problem goes far beyond the role of one individual,” they said. They propose the creation of a permanent body representing national associations, leagues, clubs and players, from across men’s and women’s football. “This new body must be fully informed about new initiatives and have a meaningful role in FIFA’s decision-making process,” they added. “Any major FIFA proposal must begin with a clearly defined rationale, supporting evidence and an independent assessment, published in advance of any decision, covering players, clubs, leagues and supporters, and evaluating the impact on all stakeholders and the development of football.” They also called for the protection of FIFA’s role “as regulator and guardian of the game” from its commercial activities. The four leagues put a call out for candidates for the FIFA presidency who will endorse their principles “within the first 100 days of the next presidential mandate”. For now, Infantino is the sole candidate for the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, with the submission of candidacies open until November 18. UEFA, alongside North American body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), issued a no-holds-barred joint letter against Infantino in August. “Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote. However, Infantino is not without friends — 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body CAF and South America’s CONMEBOL also supportive. items.title: Burkina: les JEPPC remettent le «Made in Burkina» au cœur de la souveraineté
items.description: La deuxième phase de la 3ᵉ édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC) se déroulera du 2 au 16 octobre 2026 sur toute l’étendue du territoire national. Placée sous le hème: «Produisons local, consommons burkinabè», elle entend faire de chaque achat de produit burkinabè un geste en faveur de la souveraineté économique. L’annonce a été faite, ce vendredi 25 septembre à Ouagadougou, au cours d’une conférence de presse présidée par le ministre de la Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, et son homologue de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo. Après une première phase consacrée à l’engagement et à la participation citoyenne, la 3ᵉ édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC) entre dans sa deuxième séquence. Le lancement a été annoncé vendredi 25 septembre 2026 par le ministre de la Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, et son homologue de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo. Le ministre chargé de la justice, Edasso Rodrigues Bayala Prévue du 2 au 16 octobre prochain dans l’ensemble des régions du pays, cette nouvelle phase sera articulée autour du thème: «Produisons local, consommons burkinabè». Le slogan retenu, «Tous pour le Made in Burkina: faisons de chaque achat un acte de souveraineté», donne le ton d’une campagne qui veut rapprocher patriotisme et habitudes de consommation. Pour le ministre de la Justice, le choix du produit acheté peut aussi devenir un choix en faveur de l’économie nationale. «Consommer burkinabè, ce n’est pas seulement acheter un produit: c’est soutenir ceux qui produisent ici, ceux qui transforment ici et contribuer à créer des revenus pour nos jeunes et nos femmes», a déclaré Edasso Rodrigue Bayala. Le ministre chargé de la justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala et son homologue de la communication, Pengdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo lancent officiellement la 3e édition des JEPPC Le ministre entend ainsi placer la consommation locale au cœur de la souveraineté économique. «Chaque fois que nous choisissons un produit burkinabè, nous faisons vivre une chaîne de production nationale et nous renforçons, par notre acte quotidien, notre souveraineté économique», a-t-il ajouté. Du côté du ministère de la Communication, l’accent est mis sur la valorisation des initiatives et des réalisations nationales. Le ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo a, notamment, annoncé la tenue d’une exposition gouvernementale du 2 au 9 octobre au SIAO, conçue comme un espace d’information et d’échanges avec les citoyens. Pour le ministre, cette exposition doit d’abord permettre aux citoyens de mieux connaître l’action publique. «Cette exposition sera une vitrine des acquis et des réalisations du gouvernement, mais aussi un espace où les citoyens pourront s’informer directement sur ce qui est fait pour le pays», a expliqué M. Ouédraogo. Une vue du public L’exposition entend également ouvrir un espace de dialogue avec les populations. «Nous voulons faire de ce rendez-vous un véritable cadre d’écoute, où les préoccupations des citoyens pourront être entendues et où des réponses pourront être apportées aux différentes interrogations», a-t-il souligné. Au-delà des cérémonies officielles, cette deuxième phase des JEPPC veut ainsi inscrire le patriotisme dans les gestes du quotidien. Acheter burkinabè, produire burkinabè et mieux faire connaître les initiatives nationales sont appelés à devenir autant de manifestations concrètes de l’engagement citoyen. Du 2 au 16 octobre, le pari sera donc de transformer le patriotisme affiché en réflexes économiques quotidiens, avec le Made in Burkina comme l’un des principaux marqueurs de cette nouvelle séquence des JEPPC. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burkina: les JEPPC remettent le «Made in Burkina» au cœur de la souveraineté est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: No new denominations beyond GH¢200 under Heritage Series – BoG
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has clarified that the upcoming Heritage Series will not introduce any new banknote denomination above the existing GH¢200 note. Director and Head of Currency Management at the BoG, Dominic Owusu, said the upgrade would apply only to the banknotes currently in circulation, from GH¢1 to GH¢200. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show, Mr Owusu said the central bank was not introducing a GH¢500 note or any other higher denomination as part of the Heritage Series. He explained that the existing banknotes covered by the upgrade are GH¢1, GH¢2, GH¢5, GH¢10, GH¢20, GH¢50, GH¢100 and GH¢200. “Bank of Ghana is not bringing any higher denominations today after our announcement,” he added. Mr Owusu urged the public to rely on information officially released by the Bank of Ghana and cautioned against claims circulating on social media about the introduction of higher denominations. “So let’s guard against social media issues talking about higher denominations other than 200. And let’s make sure that we limit our information to what Bank of Ghana puts out there,” he said. He stressed that the Heritage Series was an upgrade of the existing banknotes and did not constitute an expansion of the range of denominations currently available. He reiterated that the Bank of Ghana had no plans to introduce a denomination higher than GH¢200 under the new series. “We are not doing any higher denominations,” he said. The clarification comes as the Bank of Ghana prepares to introduce the Heritage Series as part of efforts to modernise the country’s banknotes and strengthen their security and durability. According to the Bank of Ghana, the new banknotes are intended to preserve the cedi’s national identity while ensuring that the currency remains secure, trusted, durable and fit for the future. The new series is expected to be officially launched on November 3, at the Bank Square in Accra, as part of efforts to modernise Ghana’s currency and respond to developments in banknote technology and security The Bank of Ghana says the introduction of the Heritage Series is not simply about replacing or changing the country’s existing banknotes, but forms part of a broader responsibility to protect the integrity of the national currency.

items.title: La Goulette rend hommage à Claudia Cardinale à la belle étoile
items.description: Un an après la disparition de Claudia Cardinale, l’actrice italienne native de Tunisie, surnommée «la plus belle Italienne de Tunis», l’ambassade d’Italie et l’Institut culturel italien de Tunis, en collaboration avec Cinématdour (un projet de cinéma itinérant), organisent, le dimanche 27 septembre 2026, une projection gratuite en plein air du film ‘‘L'Île du pardon’’ du réalisateur tunisien Ridha Béhi. Le choix de La Goulette confère à cet hommage une dimension qui dépasse le simple cadre cinématographique. Née à Tunis en 1938 au sein d’une famille italienne d’origine sicilienne, Claudia Cardinale a grandi dans cette ville portuaire et dans sa «Petite Sicile» , un quartier où, durant des décennies, ont coexisté Tunisiens, Italiens, Maltais, Français et communautés de confessions diverses. En mai 2022, lors de l’un de ses derniers séjours en Tunisie, une rue et une grande fresque murale — devant laquelle aura lieu la projection de dimanche — lui avaient été dédiées à La Goulette même. «Je me sens encore un peu tunisienne» , avait déclaré l’actrice lors de cette visite, évoquant la Tunisie de sa famille comme une terre de «partage, de joie et d’échange» . Elle avait également souligné l’importance de préserver le passé commun aux deux rives de la Méditerranée, rappelant que la Tunisie avait été une terre d’accueil pour des générations d’Italiens. Ce lien rend d’autant plus significatif le choix du film ‘‘L'Île du pardon’’ . Sorti en 2022 et figurant parmi les derniers films interprétés par Claudia Cardinale, ce long métrage de Ridha Béhi se déroule dans la Tunisie des années 1950 et raconte, à travers l’histoire d’une famille italienne chrétienne, la coexistence entre différentes communautés, cultures et religions. Tourné à Djerba, ce long métrage, dans lequel Claudia Cardinale incarne magistralement Agostina, a été présenté en compétition internationale au Festival international du film du Caire. La projection à La Goulette revêt ainsi la forme d’un retour aux sources : une actrice devenue une icône du cinéma italien et international est mise à l’honneur dans le quartier tunisien où s’est forgée son identité méditerranéenne, à travers un film tunisien abordant précisément les thèmes de la mémoire, du vivre-ensemble et de la rencontre des cultures. La collaboration avec Cinémadtour renforce cette dimension. Le cinéma quitte la salle pour retrouver l’espace urbain, face au visage de Cardinale peint sur un immeuble de l’ancienne «Petite Sicile» , dans un lieu qui demeure l’un des symboles les plus visibles de l’entrelacement historique et culturel entre l’Italie et la Tunisie. Outre Cinémadtour, l’initiative compte parmi ses partenaires le Bari International Film & TV Festival ainsi que l'association tunisienne Ciné-Sud Patrimoine. L’article La Goulette rend hommage à Claudia Cardinale à la belle étoile est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Moscou condamne les sanctions européennes contre Xenia Fedorova et promet une réponse à la «censure politique» de Bruxelles
items.description: Moscou a fermement condamne, le 25 septembre, les sanctions europeennes visant Xenia Fedorova et annonce qu'une reponse serait apportee. Dans un commentaire officiel, la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, a qualifie la decision de nouvel « acte de censure politique » et denonce une nouvelle manifestation de la politique antirusse de Bruxelles. Cette reaction intervient au lendemain de l'inscription de l'ancienne directrice de RT France sur la liste des sanctions de l'Union europeenne. Bruxelles lui reproche de participer a la diffusion en France et dans l'UE de discours qualifies de pro-russes dans le contexte du conflit en Ukraine. La diplomatie russe rejette cette justification. Maria Zakharova estime que les mesures adoptees contre Xenia Fedorova visent egalement a donner davantage de legitimite a la recente procedure francaise d'expulsion visant la journaliste. La porte-parole du ministere a notamment rappele que Xenia Fedorova ne travaille plus depuis plusieurs annees pour des medias russes. Elle collabore desormais avec plusieurs medias francais, notamment CNews, Europe 1 et le JDD. Selon Maria Zakharova, les mesures prises a son encontre sont liees aux positions qu'elle continue d'exprimer publiquement sur les evenements en France et sur plusieurs dossiers internationaux. Moscou invoque la liberte de la presse Pour la diplomatie russe, l'affaire depasse desormais le seul cas de Xenia Fedorova et pose directement la question de la liberte d'expression en Europe. Le ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres estime que les mesures prises contre la journaliste sont contraires aux engagements internationaux de la France et de l'Union europeenne en matiere de liberte de la presse et d'acces a l'information. Moscou a ainsi appele le Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies aux droits de l'homme, l'UNESCO et l'OSCE a examiner les actions de Paris et de Bruxelles et a evaluer leur respect de ces engagements. La Russie a egalement prevenu que cette decision ne resterait pas sans reponse. « Les attaques russophobes des pays concernes […] recevront une reponse appropriee », a declare Maria Zakharova. Le Kremlin denonce une « pression manifeste sur les medias » Le Kremlin a, de son cote, appuye la position exprimee par la diplomatie russe. Dmitri Peskov, porte-parole de la presidence, a estime le 25 septembre qu'il ne s'agissait « pas de la premiere sanction illegale de ce type ». « C'est une pression manifeste sur les medias. C'est une persecution des representants des medias. C'est la suppression de toute opinion dissidente dans le pays », a-t-il declare devant des journalistes. Dmitri Peskov a egalement estime que les mesures visant Xenia Fedorova illustrent la maniere dont les autorites francaises traitent les voix qui s'ecartent de la ligne dominante. Sa reaction prolonge ainsi celle du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, qui place l'affaire au cœur du debat sur la liberte de la presse, la liberte d'expression et le traitement des opinions divergentes en Europe.

items.title: Police train 45 personnel ahead of Traffitech-GH rollout on October 1
items.description: The Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service has trained 45 police personnel and public sector stakeholders in the Volta Region ahead of the operationalisation of the Traffitech-GH project on October 1. According to a post shared on Facebook by the Service, the training, held on Thursday, September 24, at the Stevens Hotel Conference Room in Ho, focused on the operation of the automated traffic enforcement system and recent changes to Ghana’s road traffic laws. The programme, organised in collaboration with the Police Service’s private sector partner, was the fifth and final session in a nationwide series of enforcement training programmes. Participants included MTTD personnel from Ho and representatives of the Judicial Service, National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), National Insurance Commission (NIC) and Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA). They were taken through the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) and the Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1153), with particular attention to automated road traffic offences and fines under Regulation 242. The training also covered the operation and implementation of Traffitech-GH, including the process for contesting automated traffic offences. Selected members of the Volta Region back office team received practical training in the use of the in-vehicle fixed camera and the handheld or tripod Lasercam4 speed camera. The Police Service said the Volta Region back office has also been established at the Regional MTTD Office in Ho and equipped with the updated Traffitech-GH software ahead of the October 1 rollout.

items.title: PTI decides to postpone Sept 27 Islamabad long march
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The PTI leadership decided on Friday to postpone its planned long march towards Islamabad, originally scheduled for Sept 27, by more than a week. The party had been preparing for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. Speaking to Dawn , a senior PTI leader, who requested anonymity, said the march will now leave from Peshawar on Oct 4. He added that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi would formally announce the postponement soon. “There was a proposal to exhaust the federal government and law enforcement agencies, as they have already closed down the federal capital and a number of routes,” he said. The leader claimed that the PTI had already achieved what it wanted to do via the march. “They have closed down roads and are spending hundreds of millions on law enforcement,” he noted. Asked if the PTI intended to march alongside the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), which had postponed its own protest march against the petroleum levy on the request of the premier, the leader said that the decision had nothing to do with them. “We are capable of arranging the march on our own,” he said. The development comes a day after a PTI leader had hinted at the possibility of postponing its protest march if the federal government agreed to hold elections within six to eight months, release Imran and other political prisoners, and investigate the May 9 and November 26 crackdowns on the opposition party. Advocate Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that the protest could be postponed if these three assurances were given by the government. Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram, however, had denied any such proposal was being discussed at any party forum, saying only Imran could take a decision even if such a proposal was on the table. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation have been in full swing in light of the potential long march and other protests in Islamabad. Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months. The Punjab government has also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jam­med on Sept 27. Meanwhile, the federal government on Thursday approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5. “The deployed troops may respond appropriately in self-defence to any threats or violent activities encountered in the course of their duties as per rules/regulations in vogue,” the notification stated.

items.title: Asanko Gold expands agric support programme to 80 farmers in Ashanti Region
items.description: Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd has expanded its Community Agricultural Support Programme (CASP) to reach 80 smallholder farmers in the Ashanti Region. The beneficiaries are drawn from 12 communities in the Amansie West and Amansie South districts. The second phase of the programme aims to improve agricultural productivity, strengthen food security, and help farmers cope with rising input costs, changing rainfall patterns, and limited access to agricultural extension services. Isaac Kwakye, Asanko’s Social Responsibility Manager, said the initiative was designed to strengthen agriculture and support livelihoods in the company’s host communities. He explained that providing farmers with inputs, training, and technical support would help improve farming practices and increase food production. “We thought it wise that if we can help our farmers improve agricultural practices, if we can support them with farming inputs, it will go a long way in augmenting their farm produce, which in the end will bring more food to the area,” Mr Kwakye said. He added that beneficiaries from the first phase would continue to receive agricultural extension services to help them sustain and build on the progress made, while new farmers are brought onto the programme under Phase Two. Justice Fenteng, General Manager of Asanko, noted that agriculture remains an important source of food and income for households in the company’s host communities. He said farmers continue to face high input costs, weed-control difficulties, changing rainfall patterns, and inadequate access to technical support. Under Phase Two, each participating farmer cultivating at least one acre will receive weed-control inputs, Wellington boots, a raincoat, a cutlass, and a knapsack sprayer. Mr Fenteng said the items were selected to support farmers in key activities including land preparation, weed management, and safer working conditions. He stressed that the intervention was not only about distributing inputs but also about equipping farmers with the knowledge to use them effectively. Beneficiaries will receive practical training in improved and climate-resilient farming methods, covering farm planning, weed management, responsible use of inputs, safe handling of equipment, and approaches to adapting farming practices to changing rainfall patterns and other weather conditions. Illegal mining driving youth away from agriculture Esther Afoakwa, Assistant Director of Agriculture for the Amansie South District, said illegal mining was contributing to declining interest in agriculture among young people in the district. She noted that farming was increasingly being left to older people as some young people turned to mining activities for income. “The state of agriculture in the district currently, due to illegal mining activities, we are finding some challenges because the youth are not into agriculture. It is only the aged who are into agriculture,” she said. Ms Afoakwa welcomed the intervention, saying the support would help farmers improve their activities and strengthen household livelihoods. A beneficiary from one of the participating communities expressed appreciation for the initiative. “We are grateful to Asanko for the support. It will help us improve our farming activities, and we hope the company will continue to support farmers in our communities,” the beneficiary said.

items.title: DR Congo running short of health workers as Ebola outbreak intensifies, WHO says
items.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo faces a severe shortage of healthcare professionals to staff specialised treatment centres. The World Health Organisation issued this warning as the nation battles the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic in recorded history. Spreading Across Provinces And Populations The epidemic has expanded across seven provinces throughout the country. Government figures record a total of 7,773 confirmed cases and 3,759 deaths. Recent weeks show declining numbers in certain regions. Cases dropped by twenty-six per cent in Ituri province and fifteen per cent in Haut-Uele between August 31 and September 20. Transmission patterns remain unpredictable. The outbreak stays largely out of control across a wide geographic footprint. Marie Roseline Belizaire addressed the regional disparities. “While cases and deaths are declining in some provinces, they continue to rise in others,” Belizaire said. “The outbreak is still not under control and remains spread across a wide geographic area.” Surging Rates In North Kivu The eastern province of North Kivu experienced a sharp spike. Cases surged seventy-three per cent over three weeks. Catherine Smallwood noted that cases and deaths eventually began declining in North Kivu following weeks of increases. Health authorities add new treatment beds daily. Facilities still lack sufficient staff and operational partners. Compounding Crises On The Ground Multiple compounding factors accelerate viral transmission. Armed insecurity, widespread population displacement, massive movement, and ongoing health worker strikes create extreme operational hurdles. The current trajectory threatens to eclipse past historical crises. The World Health Organisation reports that this epidemic is on track to surpass the 2014 through 2016 West Africa outbreak. That previous disaster remains the deadliest on record, with over 11,000 fatalities primarily concentrated in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Severe Human Resource Bottlenecks Staffing shortages cripple medical responses in active zones. Catherine Smallwood emphasised the core issue. “The human resources gap is one of the biggest gaps,” Smallwood said. Anne Ancia outlined the massive staffing requirements for medical infrastructure. A single Ebola treatment centre needs approximately 300 professionals. This workforce includes general practitioners, nurses, hygienists, and anaesthetists. “Estamos construyendo centros de tratamiento, pero no siempre tenemos los recursos humanos necesarios para operarlos,” Ancia said. “Those health workers must be paid.” Wage Disputes And Payroll Verification Front-line workers previously launched strikes over unpaid wages. These job actions severely damaged patient access to care. Health Minister Roger Kamba explained administrative delays in July. The government launched a verification process for payroll lists after discovering ghost workers and unauthorised names added to response rosters. Frontline workers reported that officials promised to clear salary arrears. Many staff members received only partial payments while others received nothing at all. Devastating Vulnerability Among Young Children Children under the age of five face disproportionately high mortality risks. Marie Roseline Belizaire stated that young children endure a case fatality rate exceeding sixty per cent. Adult fatalities hover around fortyper centt. Clinical detection among infants presents unique diagnostic hurdles. Catherine Smallwood explained the clinical complexities. Smallwood noted that detecting cases among children under five is exceptionally difficult because young patients cannot accurately articulate their symptoms, and disease presentation often remains confusing. Navigating The Humanitarian Imperative Resolving these intersecting crises requires coordinated financial transparency, robust security guarantees for aid workers, and sustained international backing to protect vulnerable populations while medical teams race to contain the contagion.

items.title: Futsal: le Maroc conserve sa 6e place mondiale chez les hommes, recule à la 26e chez les dames
items.description: Le Maroc conserve sa place de leader africain incontesté dans les classements mondiaux de football en salle (futsal) de la FIFA, publiés vendredi, se maintenant à la 6e position chez les hommes, même s'il recule au 26e rang chez les femmes. Dans la catégorie masculine, le Royaume conserve sa 6e place avec un gain de 10,77 points et reste largement en tête du classement africain, suivi de très loin de l’Égypte, 41e (-1) et de la Libye, 52e (+1). Chez les dames, la sélection marocaine occupe désormais la 26e position, après avoir perdu deux places et 14,36 points, tout en conservant son leadership continental loin devant la Tanzanie, 73e (+1) et le Sénégal, 81e (+1). Au niveau mondial, le Brésil est toujours aux commandes des deux classements, devant le Portugal (2e chez les hommes, 3e chez les dames) et l’Espagne (3e chez les hommes, 2e chez les femmes), tandis que le Top 10 est resté inchangé dans les deux catégories depuis mai 2026. La Croatie signe la plus forte progression chez les femmes, avec trois places gagnées pour atteindre le 32e rang, alors que la Zambie réalise le meilleur bond chez les hommes, avec quatre places gagnées, au 82e rang. Le Vietnam enregistre, pour sa part, la plus forte progression en points chez les hommes (+19,5) et se hisse au 20e rang. La prochaine mise à jour des classements mondiaux de futsal masculin et féminin est prévue le 11 décembre 2026, selon la FIFA. The post Futsal: le Maroc conserve sa 6e place mondiale chez les hommes, recule à la 26e chez les dames appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Scrap dealers declare nationwide strike from Oct. 1, alleging irregularities
items.description: The National Association of Scrap and Waste Dealers Employers of Nigeria (NASWDEN) has directed its members to embark on strike from Oct. 1, over alleged irregularities in the scrap metal industry. Its National President, Mr Abdulfatah Adisa-Ogunwale, gave the directive in a statement made available to newsmen by the NASWDEN Deputy National President, Alhaji Aminu Hassan-Soja, on Friday in Kano. The statement said the decision followed what the association described as persistent anomalies, irregularities and grievances affecting scrap-metal dealers and their businesses. “The industrial action is aimed at suspending the supply of scrap metals to iron-smelting companies producing iron rods and other steel products from non-ferrous and scrap metals. “The industrial action is scheduled to commence on Oct. 1, and will run until Oct. 15. “The action will continue indefinitely beyond that date, if no satisfactory Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) is reached with the affected iron and steel companies,” it said. The statement cited areas of concern to include unannounced reduction in scrap metal prices. “In some instances, dealers could lose approximately N3 million to N6 million on a single truckload as a result of sudden price reductions,” it said. Others, according to the statement, are alleged deductions by some companies under what they refer to as “Extra Dust”. “Deductions ranging from one per cent to five per cent are imposed on some transactions, which it considers as an additional financial burden and an unfair practice against its members,” it said. The statement also alleged involvement of foreigners in the scrap business. “The association further expressed concern over what it described as the increasing involvement of foreigners in the scrap-metal business. “Some foreigners are allegedly taking over portions of the business by establishing dumpsites and scrap-collection centres across different parts of the country, thereby creating difficulties for indigenous Nigerian scrap dealers,” it claimed. The association also alleged that some iron companies purchase scrap metals from unregistered or uncertified agents and dealers. “The association is concerned that such practices could encourage the circulation of vandalised public and private property within the scrap-metal market,” it warned. The association, therefore, called for greater regulation and verification of scrap dealers, agents and collection centres to ensure that materials entering the steel industry were obtained through legitimate channels. It appealed to relevant government agencies, stakeholders in the iron and steel sector and the general public to take note of the planned industrial action and support efforts toward resolving the issues through constructive engagement. items.title: 2027: I’ll ensure N-Delta feel impact of oil wealth – Obi
items.description: By Ochuko Akuopha PRESIDENTIAL candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in the 2027 general election, Mr Peter Obi, has promised to ensure that the Niger Delta region feels the impact of the wealth it generates for the country if elected President. He said the era in which the oil-rich region contributed enormously to the nation’s wealth without corresponding development must end. Obi spoke in Asaba, Delta State, during the inauguration of the NDC campaign headquarters in the state. Lamenting the neglect of the Niger Delta despite its strategic contribution to Nigeria’s economy, He said: “One thing that I can assure you is that the days you don’t see the impact of your wealth are gone. Niger Delta must see the impact of the wealth it is creating for the nation,” Obi said. Obi who also decried the deplorable state of the East-West Road and all federal roads in the oil rich region noted that “you cannot pass anywhere in the the Niger Delta, yet they are producing the wealth the country share every month. “We will ensure that that this will change and it will change by the way we manage the resources; it will change because we are going to be transparent. We will tell you where every penny is going to.” The NDC candidate also promised to prioritise the development of Nigeria’s healthcare system, saying that “We will fix it and make it work,” He promised that he would ensure that political office holders in the seek medical treatment in Nigeria. “We will ensure that those of them who are in power must seek medical care here. Anybody that will go abroad will be for referral,” Obi said, promising to spend all his holidays in Nigeria if elected President. Gubernatorial candidate of the NDC in Delta State, Chris Iyovwaye and Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the party, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege said the people of the state were prepared to vote for Peter Obi at the forthcoming polls. items.title: GBA condemns attempted arrest of Manhyia South MP at Accra High Court
items.description: The Ghana Bar Association (GBA) has condemned an attempt by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) to arrest Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah at the premises of the Accra High Court, where he had gone to represent a client as a lawyer. The Association has also raised concerns over the alleged assault of another lawyer, Mr Enoch Anhwere Afoakwa, during the incident on 23 September 2026. In a statement dated September 24, the GBA said it had reviewed videos of the attempted arrest and observed what it described as an assault on Mr Afoakwa by a woman who was subsequently identified by EOCO as one of its officers. “The Ghana Bar has noted with grave concern the attempt by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) to arrest the Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah on the premises of the Accra High Court Complex, where he had gone to represent a client in his capacity as a lawyer, on September 23,” the statement said. PRESS STATEMENT (11) Download The Bar Association acknowledged that no individual is above the law but said enforcement agencies must ensure that investigations and arrests involving lawyers are carried out in accordance with constitutional and professional safeguards, particularly when a lawyer is performing official duties on behalf of a client. The Association warned that failure to respect those safeguards could have broader consequences for the legal profession, including creating a perception of intimidation and discouraging lawyers from carrying out their professional responsibilities. “Attempts to circumvent these safeguards create the perception of intimidation and may have a chilling effect on the legal profession as a whole,” it said. According to the GBA, lawyers have a fundamental role in the administration of justice and in protecting the rights of citizens. It therefore cautioned that actions that interfere with lawyers’ ability to represent clients could undermine public confidence in the justice system. The Association referred to remarks made by its President at the 2025 Annual GBA Conference in Wa, where she expressed concern about incidents involving lawyers in the course of their work. “Lawyers should be at liberty to defend clients of their choice without being heckled. Such unruly acts may stifle the provision of pro bono cases by well-meaning lawyers,” she added. GBA recalls earlier BNI incident The Association also referred to comments made by its president during the GBA’s Virtual Mid-Year Conference on 5 June concerning an earlier incident involving former Vice-President of the Bar, Justice Minka Premo, and a young female lawyer. According to the GBA President, the two lawyers had gone to the Bureau of National Investigations (BNI) to defend a client but were subsequently arrested and detained overnight. “This worrying incident has left in its trail serious unanswered questions: If these persons were under the security radar prior to their visit to BNI, why had they not been invited earlier?” she asked. The Ghana Bar Association called on EOCO and other relevant state institutions to ensure that their activities are conducted in accordance with due process, fairness, and respect for the rights of all persons involved. “The rule of law demands not only that justice be done, but that it be seen to be done. The independence of the legal profession is a cornerstone of every democratic society and must be at all times,” the statement added.

items.title: Éthiopie : le président dénonce des «ingérences» tandis que les combats s’intensifient autour du Tigré
items.description: Le president ethiopien Taye Atske Selassie s'est exprime le 23 septembre devant l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies, alors que les tensions s'intensifient dans le nord de son pays. Le chef de l'etat a denonce le role d'« acteurs exterieurs » dans la destabilisation de la region et affirme que l'ethiopie avait fait preuve d'une « immense retenue » malgre les ingerences dans ses affaires interieures. « Notre message aux forces de destruction et de chaos est clair et net. Nous les exhortons a respecter le droit sacre des populations de la Corne de l'Afrique a vivre dans la paix et la prosperite », a declare Taye Atske Selassie, tout en reaffirmant l'ambition de l'ethiopie de devenir l'un des principaux moteurs de developpement du continent. Dans sa premiere declaration depuis le debut des hostilites, l'armee ethiopienne a affirme avoir repousse des attaques menees par les forces tigreennes et leurs allies dans la region de l'Amhara, voisine du Tigre, a rapporte la presse ethiopienne le 24 septembre. L'armee affirme avoir inflige de lourdes pertes a ses adversaires et saisi des armes, sans fournir davantage de precisions. Aucune source independante n'a, pour l'heure, ete en mesure de verifier ces affirmations. De son cote, le FLPT n'avait pas encore reagi officiellement a ces declarations. Une source humanitaire citee par l'AFP a egalement affirme, le 24 septembre, que les forces tigreennes avaient eu recours a l'artillerie lourde lors d'une offensive visant a s'emparer de la ville de Yallo, a proximite de la frontiere du Tigre. Cite par l'AFP, le vice-president du FLPT, Amanuel Assefa, a declare : « Nous sommes desormais en situation de guerre ouverte. » Internet perturbe et achats de panique dans le Tigre La connectivite a internet a ete fortement perturbee ce 25 septembre dans le nord de l'ethiopie, sur fond d'intensification des combats entre l'armee federale et les forces tigreennes. NetBlocks, organisation specialisee dans la surveillance de la connectivite numerique, a indique que ses donnees faisaient apparaître une perturbation d'internet a l'echelle infranationale dans le nord du pays. Plusieurs medias ont egalement fait etat de difficultes a etablir des communications, y compris telephoniques, avec Mekele, capitale du Tigre, ainsi qu'avec la ville de Shire. Ces perturbations font craindre le retour de coupures prolongees d'internet et des reseaux mobiles, comme celles qu'avait connues la region durant le conflit de 2020-2022. Par ailleurs, des habitants du Tigre ont commence a constituer des reserves de nourriture et d'autres produits de premiere necessite, provoquant des achats de panique par crainte de perturbations des communications, des services bancaires, de l'electricite et des approvisionnements. La nouvelle escalade entre le gouvernement ethiopien et le FLPT a debute le 22 septembre par des affrontements le long de la frontiere entre le Tigre et l'Afar, avant de gagner d'autres zones de l'Amhara. Le lendemain, les forces tigreennes ont pris le controle des aeroports de Mekele, d'Axoum et de Shire, tandis que les combats se propageaient aux regions voisines. Les Nations unies, l'Union europeenne et l'Union africaine ont appele a une desescalade immediate et a la reprise du dialogue afin d'eviter un nouvel embrasement. Le conflit de 2020-2022 avait fait environ 600 000 morts selon une estimation citee par l'Union africaine et entraîne le deplacement d'environ un million de personnes.

items.title: Obi debt claim: Anambra govt presents N363m salary arrears records
items.description: Anambra State Government has released documents detailing N363.38 million in salary arrears owed to workers and pensioners of two defunct state agencies, amid former governor Peter Obi’s insistence that he left the state without debt. The documents, shared on social media by Anambra State New Media, a platform affiliated with the state government, form part of its response to Obi’s claim that he did not leave outstanding debts at the end of his eight-year administration. The records include a memo dated May 22, 2025, signed by a former head of service, and a terms-of-settlement agreement between the state government and the Amalgamated Union of Public Corporations, Civil Service, Technical and Recreational Services Employees (AUPCTRE). According to the memo, the state government scheduled a second tranche of N363.381 million for payment in 2026 as part of an agreement to settle outstanding salary arrears involving the defunct Anambra State Water Corporation (ANSWC) and Anambra State Environmental Protection Agency (ANSEPA). “The second payment in the sum of Three Hundred and Sixty-Three Million, Three Hundred and Eighty-One Thousand Naira only (₦363,381,000.00) will be made in 2026,” the document reads. The memo, which referenced Article 7 of the terms of settlement, said the payment was part of the government’s commitment to fulfilling the agreement and addressing the hardship faced by affected workers and pensioners. The beneficiaries include next of kin, staff and pensioners of the two defunct agencies. The document also proposed that the payment be processed through the state government payroll system using a dedicated account. It sought approval for the release of the funds to the beneficiaries, listing the vote charge as 61104001/23020105/10000003 and indicating a balance of N500 million. The terms of settlement cited in the memo were signed by the state government and AUPCTRE on February 6, 2024. The Soludo administration maintains that the N363.381 million represents part of the salary arrears inherited from Obi’s administration, which it said left the entitlements of workers and pensioners of the two agencies unpaid. According to the government, the first tranche of the settlement has already been paid, while the second payment was provided for under the 2024 agreement. However, the documents do not independently establish when the underlying arrears were incurred or whether they originated during Obi’s tenure as governor. Renewed dispute between Obi and the Anambra government followed an earlier claim by Anambra State Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Law Mefor, that Obi left $123.77 million in debt when he handed over power. Mefor said the funds were obtained for projects covering malaria control, education, healthcare, erosion management, community development and value-chain development. Obi, however, insists that his administration did not leave Anambra State burdened with debt. items.title: Fédération burkinabè de handball : 35 entraineurs obtiennent la Licence D IHF
items.description: La Fédération burkinabè de handball a clôturé, vendredi 25 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une session de formation de cinq jours consacrée à l’obtention de la Licence D de la Fédération internationale de handball (IHF). Au terme des travaux, les 35 candidats ont tous été déclarés admis. Une réussite qui ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour la formation des jeunes handballeurs au Burkina Faso. La session de formation des entraineurs en Licence D IHF a connu son épilogue, le vendredi 25 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, avec un taux de réussite de 100 %. Organisée par la Fédération burkinabè de handball, avec l’accompagnement du Fonds d’appui au sport et à la presse privée (Wassa Bondo), elle a réuni 35 stagiaires autour des fondamentaux de l’encadrement technique. Pendant cinq jours, les participants ont alterné enseignements théoriques et séances pratiques sous la conduite de l’expert béninois de l’IHF, Dr Kocou Basile Nouatin, avec l’appui du sélectionneur national, Simplice Somé. Les modules ont notamment porté sur l’entrainement des jeunes, la pédagogie, la technique individuelle et les bases du jeu collectif. A la cérémonie de clôture, le formateur a salué l’engagement et les progrès des stagiaires. « J’ai pu observer votre engagement, votre soif d’apprendre et votre passion pour le handball », a-t-il souligné, estimant que les acquis de cette formation constituent un socle pour leur parcours d’éducateurs. Dr Kocou Basile Nouatin a invité les nouveaux diplômés à mettre leurs connaissances au service des jeunes joueurs et joueuses, particulièrement dans les écoles et les clubs. Il les a également exhortés à poursuivre leur apprentissage et à cultiver les valeurs d’intégrité, de discipline et de passion. Représentant les stagiaires, Olivier Tuina a exprimé sa reconnaissance à la Fédération et au Fonds Wassa Bondo pour leur soutien financier. Il a relevé que, sans cette subvention, plusieurs participants, souvent confrontés à des conditions de travail difficiles et à l’absence de rémunération, n’auraient pas pu prendre part à la formation. Il a par ailleurs salué la qualité des enseignements et le partage d’expériences entre techniciens, avant d’appeler à la poursuite de l’accompagnement pour favoriser la professionnalisation du handball burkinabè. Pour sa part, la directrice générale du Fonds Wassa Bondo, Ida Ouédraogo née Paré, s’est réjouie des résultats obtenus. « Nous avions 35 candidats. Nous avons 35 admis », a-t-elle déclaré, rappelant que la qualité des athlètes dépend aussi de celle de leur encadrement. Elle a souhaité que les connaissances acquises soient rapidement mises en pratique sur le terrain, au bénéfice des sportifs. Le président de la Fédération burkinabè de handball, Boubacar Sanfo, a remercié les partenaires et l’expert pour leur contribution. Il a annoncé la poursuite du programme de formation, avec la perspective de la Licence B, afin d’élargir le nombre d’entraîneurs qualifiés et de renforcer la présence du handball sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Cette session marque ainsi une nouvelle étape dans le renforcement des capacités des encadreurs et la structuration du handball burkinabè à la base. Pengdwendé Achille OUEDRAOGO

items.title: Richmond Amoateng Foundation drives youth development and community unity in Juaben
items.description: The Richmond Amoateng Foundation is supporting youth development and community cohesion in Juaben through a range of initiatives focused on education, sports, social support and diaspora engagement. Working with local leaders, including H/W Kusi and Samuel Aikins, the Foundation has organised programmes aimed at bringing residents together while creating opportunities for young people in the community. One of its flagship initiatives is the annual December in Juaben festival, which brings together families, residents and members of the diaspora to celebrate their shared heritage and strengthen community ties. As part of the Christmas celebrations, the Foundation also organised a feeding programme that provided meals for 5,000 children. The initiative was aimed at supporting children and families in the community during the festive season. Using sport to unite young people The Foundation has also used sports as a platform for youth engagement and community development. During the Easter period, it organised a football tournament involving teams from various communities. The tournament provided an opportunity for young people to interact while promoting teamwork, friendship and community unity. Beyond sports, the Foundation has placed emphasis on education and academic development. It organised a breakfast meeting for past BECE candidates, using the occasion to motivate students to remain focused on their education and work towards improved academic outcomes. Strengthening diaspora links The Foundation has also sought to deepen the involvement of the Juaben diaspora in the development of the community. Representatives travelled to the United Kingdom to engage with the Juaben Association on ways the diaspora and other stakeholders could contribute to youth development in Juaben. The discussions focused on identifying practical opportunities to support young people, who the Foundation considers central to the community’s future. The Foundation said its programmes are guided by a commitment to youth development, education, sports, social welfare, community cohesion and stronger partnerships with the Juaben diaspora. About the Richmond Amoateng Foundation The Richmond Amoateng Foundation is focused on bringing the people of Juaben together and supporting community development through programmes in education, sports, social welfare and diaspora engagement.
