items.title: The Americans Having the Most Sex
items.description: In the popular imagination, religious faith and a thriving sex life don’t tend to go together. Movies, books, and TV shows depict religious couples as sexually inhibited or dysfunctional. For example, in Caro Claire Burke’s best-selling novel, Yesteryear —soon to be a movie starring Anne Hathaway—a Scripture-quoting tradwife puts up a good front for Instagram but is privately miserable with her husband, who not only is passive but also struggles to perform in the bedroom. But the data tell a different story. According to our new report , published today by the Institute for Family Studies, no group of Americans seems to be having more sex—and more satisfying sex—than married men and women who regularly attend a place of worship. (This group is made up mostly of Christians, but also includes Jews and Muslims.) In fact, we find that the only Americans who have avoided the country’s “sex recession” —in which fewer and fewer men and women are having regular sex—are husbands and wives who attend religious services at least twice a month. In the 1990s, 64 percent of married people aged 20–54, both churchgoing and secular, had sex at least once a week, according to the General Social Survey. Now only 48 percent of secular couples (who never or rarely attend church) have sex weekly compared with 62 percent of their religious peers. In America today, the faithful are having more sex. Could this just be about wives in patriarchal religious communities who feel obligated to perform for their husband, but in ways that leave them sexually unsatisfied and deeply unhappy? Again, the data suggest otherwise. Both religious husbands and wives aged 20–54 are more likely to describe their sex life as “excellent” or “very good” than their secular peers, according to the 2026 IFS Religion and Family Survey. Forty-nine percent of churchgoing wives report being sexually satisfied, compared with just 38 percent of secular wives. The survey also finds that churchgoing spouses are more likely to be “very” or “extremely” happy in their marriage. In our report, “The Devout Difference: Religion, Marital Quality, and Sex Among Americans,” written with the family scholars Richard Dell’Isola and Jane Lankes Smith, we conclude that the “cultural trope of the sexually prudish, frustrated religious American does not fit the data.” We hypothesize that when marriage and sex are endowed with a sense of sacredness—and the family-friendly values found in faith—they are both more likely to be satisfying. That’s partly because virtues such as forgiveness and fidelity smooth out the bumps in married life and reduce the odds that your marriage will hit those bumps in the first place. It’s also because religious rituals such as prayer—especially shared prayer—do more than foster emotional intimacy: They help make the stresses of family life more manageable, which may help explain why the believers in our study who pray daily have 1.29 times higher odds of sexual satisfaction than those who do not regularly pray. [ From the September 2026 issue: The great romance slump ] The sociologist Sam Perry, an expert on religion and sex, thinks that most of these findings flow from the tie between marital quality and religious faith. As he told us over email, the sexual advantages that the religious enjoy are, in all probability, “mostly downstream of relational harmony.” Research generally finds that faith leads to happier marriages, he noted, especially for couples who share a common faith. “So religious couples who are attending together are likely more in sync religiously and consequently happier and better able to enjoy one another,” he wrote. The religious advantage regarding sex may also have to do with the fact that religious Americans are more likely to embrace an ethic of sexual generosity. Religious couples seem more willing than secular couples to acknowledge what popular culture often denies: that men and women can have different sexual appetites, and that men typically want sex more frequently than women do. Indeed, husbands are more than three times more likely than wives to initiate sex in contemporary marriages. Rather than treating that gap as a grievance, the faithful may lean into it: Husbands honor their wife’s moments of uninterest, wives honor their husband’s desire, and both sides are willing to compromise. In the 2024 book Get Married , one of us (Brad Wilcox) found that wives in religious marriages are more likely than others to say that it is “mostly” or “definitely” true that their husband is considerate when they do not want sex, and found that husbands in such marriages are more likely to say that their wife is responsive when they initiate. But if qualities such as generosity and forgiveness explain why religious couples are withstanding the sex recession, they don’t explain why secular couples are succumbing to it, and experiencing much less intimacy than their predecessors. We suspect that one factor is that secular women are more likely than churchgoing women to fall prey to the negative messaging about men and marriage that floods social-media algorithms. The social psychologist Jonathan Haidt has observed that young female liberals are “more anxious and depressed than other groups”—especially religious conservatives—because of their “heavier use of social media and their participation in online communities” dominated by catastrophizing thinking. Amplified by social media over the past 15 years, these currents may also have strained the lives not just of young liberals but of secular couples in their prime, all the way into the bedroom. [ Read: What a century-old sex manual got right ] Another challenge facing secular couples is that they live in what the writer Derek Thompson has called “the anti-social century,” in which neighborliness, friendships, and community life are all in shorter supply. This matters because husbands and wives with high levels of support from friends and family are “at least 23 percentage points more likely to report that they are very happy” in their marriage, according to one study . In contrast with secular couples, religious couples are more likely to be embedded in real-world communities that lend social and normative support to marriage and family life. These include regular worship and small men’s and women’s groups that encourage them to be better spouses and parents. Engaging in real communities with real people also means that religious couples are less subject to the trends of our era that can leave people feeling lonely, unmoored, and unhappy. Religion frequently gets a bad rap in our public conversation about sex. One recent New York Times op-ed , for instance, argued that conservative Christian women are pushed to “submit to their husbands, sexually and otherwise” in churches marked by “misogyny and hypocrisy.” Of course, some religious women are in coercive or unsatisfying marriages. But blanket commentary like this leaves the public with the impression that religion is an obstacle to a happy marriage and a good sex life. Yet in an atomized, individualistic age, faith has turned out to be one of the few institutions still nurturing one of the most powerful expressions of human intimacy.

items.description: Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz has questioned the absence of Video Assistant Referee (VAR) technology in Africa following Ghana’s 2-0 defeat by Côte d’Ivoire in their opening 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match. Ghana began their qualifying campaign with a disappointing loss in Bouaké, with the hosts scoring twice to claim all three points. Queiroz was unhappy with the penalty decision that went against his side in the second half and used his post-match press conference to question why VAR is not available in AFCON qualifying matches. The referee awarded Côte d’Ivoire a penalty in the 58th minute after Malick Yalcouyé went down inside the box following a challenge from Ghana midfielder Abdul Fatawu Issahaku. Franck Kessié converted the spot-kick to double the hosts’ advantage. “Today it’s us, tomorrow it will be Ivory Coast,” Queiroz stated. “So why don’t we have VAR in the Africa Cup of Nations competition? Which example do we want to give to the world? Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers for Africa Cup of Nations, we don’t have VAR to help the referee to make the game fair. “Why don’t we have VAR in Africa? What is the reason we don’t have VAR in the Africa Cup of Nations? I am tired of this situation where referees don’t do a good job” Sitting at the bottom of Group C following the setback, the Black Stars will now shift their focus to their game against The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium on Tuesday, September 29.

items.title: Oborevwori welcomes FG’s emergency rescue of Benin-Asaba Road
items.description: Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has welcomed the Federal Government’s decision to commence emergency repairs on the Benin-Asaba Road, describing the intervention as a major step towards restoring the critical economic corridor. Oborevwori, who spoke through the Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, at the “Operation Rescue Benin-Asaba Road” exercise in Benin City on Thursday, said the deplorable condition of the highway had subjected motorists, commuters and businesses to prolonged hardship. Aniagwu said the road was particularly important to Delta and Edo states, describing it as a major artery linking communities, commercial centres and the South-South and South-East regions. He attributed its deterioration largely to the failure of the concessionaire to meet the objectives of the concession agreement. “We are therefore delighted that the Federal Government has today deemed it fit to give life back to this important road corridor, which connects not only the commercial centres of the South-East but also the burgeoning business centres in Delta and Edo states,” he said. He commended President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi, for the intervention and urged the Federal Government and contractors to expedite the work. “We look forward to seeing the work commence in earnest and to having this important road restored to a standard that will ease the movement of people and goods, revive commercial activities and improve the economic fortunes of our people,” Aniagwu said. The commissioner also highlighted Delta’s collaboration with the Federal Government on federal roads, citing the state’s intervention on the Warri-Sapele Road, where it constructed the section from the U-turn at the Spare Parts Market to Ohore Junction with concrete rigid pavement. He said Delta would continue to support efforts to address critical infrastructure challenges and commended Umahi for the intervention on the First Niger Bridge, expressing optimism about its reopening after major rehabilitation works. Speaking at the event, Umahi said the emergency rehabilitation was not awarded as a conventional contract but involved the deployment of equipment hired from contractors operating along the corridor, including Hi-Tech, CCECC and CBC. He said the temporary intervention was expected to restore the road within four weeks, while President Tinubu had directed the redesign of the entire 136-kilometre Benin-Asaba dual carriageway with reinforced concrete pavement for long-term reconstruction. Umahi said the Federal Government had offered the concessionaire three options to continue with the project, but the options failed, prompting the ministry to intervene in the public interest. He also alleged that the concessionaire lacked the engineering and financial capacity to execute the project and had breached provisions of the concession agreement. According to him, the emergency works would commence from the Edo axis, with particular attention to the Benin Bypass, while supervising engineers would be deployed to different sections to monitor the work and ensure compliance with standards. Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, thanked President Tinubu for ordering the intervention and urged those handling the project to ensure quality, adherence to specifications and timely completion. The Benin-Asaba Road, a major transportation corridor linking the South-South and South-East with other parts of the country, has suffered failed sections and severe gridlock in recent months, disrupting the movement of people and goods. The emergency intervention is expected to provide immediate relief to motorists while the planned redesign and long-term reconstruction of the corridor proceeds. items.title: Safe NCD care needs leadership, investment and patient involvement – PharmAccess
items.description: PharmAccess has outlined four key conditions it says are necessary to make patient safety and quality care a daily reality for people living with non-communicable diseases (NCDs). The SafeCare Director of PharmAccess Ghana, Bonifacia Benefo Agyei, identified visible leadership, sustained investment, effective measurement and active patient participation as critical to improving the safety of NCD care. She made the call at a Ghana Health Service event in Accra to commemorate the 2026 World Patient Safety Day, which focused on safe care for non-communicable diseases under the theme “Safe care for life!” According to the World Health Organisation, one in 10 patients is harmed while receiving healthcare globally, with around half of that harm considered preventable. People living with NCDs face particular risks because they often require continuous and complex care across different health facilities and over long periods. NCDs, including cardiovascular diseases, cancers, and diabetes, account for about 74% of deaths globally, according to the WHO. Ms Benefo Agyei said the risks faced by people living with chronic conditions could not be addressed through isolated interventions. She illustrated the point with the example of a woman diagnosed with hypertension in her 40s who may have to live with the condition for another 30 to 40 years. Such a patient could interact with hundreds of clinicians, receive numerous prescriptions and referrals, and repeatedly move between healthcare facilities, she noted. In many cases, she said, patients are left to carry their medical histories in their memory because their folders or medical information do not move with them. “The safety of such a woman is not in a single event. It is the sum of every consultation, every prescription, every hand-off,” she said. Four interventions to strengthen NCD care Ms Benefo Agyei said PharmAccess is using four interventions to address some of the points where NCD care can break down. Through SafeCare, the organisation supports healthcare facilities to assess their services against internationally recognised standards, identify gaps and translate the findings into measurable improvements. The programme works with the Ghana Health Service, the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG), and private providers to ensure that quality improvement is embedded within Ghanaian institutions and led by local teams. Globally, SafeCare has assessed thousands of facilities, with 74% demonstrating measurable quality improvement, according to PharmAccess. The systems supported through the methodology currently serve approximately 9.6 million patient visits each month. PharmAccess is also working to advance value-based care, a model that links payments to patient outcomes rather than simply the number of procedures performed. Working with the National Health Insurance Authority and CHAG, the organisation is evaluating the approach for hypertension and diabetes, taking into account clinical outcomes, quality of life, patient experience, and financial protection. A third intervention is NkwaPlus, a digital health platform developed with technology partner Afrifanom and currently being piloted with selected facilities and patient groups. The platform allows patients to share health information from home with their care teams, supporting continuous monitoring and earlier intervention. Ms Benefo Agyei said this could help ensure that emerging risks are identified before they develop into emergencies, particularly in chronic care, where patients spend much of their time outside health facilities. The fourth intervention is the Medical Credit Fund, which provides loans and technical assistance to healthcare providers to enable them to address identified quality gaps. She said this was important because identifying a safety risk through an assessment was of limited value if a facility lacked the resources to fix it. The Medical Credit Fund has so far supported more than 2,100 healthcare providers and disbursed more than 12,000 loans, with a reported 95% repayment rate. About 30% of its lending supports women-led health enterprises. Ms Benefo Agyei said the four interventions were designed to complement each other. “Standards identify the problem, financing fixes it, digital tools catch it early, and payment reform rewards the outcome. It is the combination that makes patients safer,” she said. Four conditions for safer care Beyond these interventions, Ms Benefo Agyei said four conditions must be met if patient safety is to become part of everyday healthcare delivery. She said leadership must be visible, with patient safety treated as a priority at every level of the health system. “Patient safety must be a standing item at every level, from the ministry to the ward,” she said. She also called for sustained investment, saying commitment to patient safety must be reflected in budgets, staffing, and operational plans. On measurement and accountability, she said assessments, peer reviews, incident reports, and patient feedback should lead to concrete action. “Assessments, peer reviews, incident reports and patient feedback matter only when each one ends in a named person, a date, and a change, and staff must be able to report harm without fear,” she said. The fourth condition, she said, was making patients active partners in their own care. People living with chronic conditions, she noted, must be supported to understand their conditions, treatment, and the steps they can take to manage their health safely. The WHO’s 2026 campaign similarly emphasises the need for people living with NCDs to be partners in safe care, while highlighting continuity of care, stronger health systems, and meaningful patient engagement. Ms Benefo Agyei urged stakeholders to agree on a short list of practical actions, with each assigned a responsible lead, timeline, budget and measurable outcome. She said that by the next World Patient Safety Day, the health sector should be able to identify which actions had been funded and implemented and demonstrate how they had improved safety for patients. On behalf of PharmAccess and its Country Director, Dr Maxwell Antwi, she reaffirmed the organisation’s readiness to provide technical support and help mobilise resources with partners. “The strongest expression of our commitment will not be spoken here today,” she said. “It will be what changes in our facilities tomorrow.”

Université Norbert Zongo : Yamnékré Marguerite Ouédraogo décroche son doctorat en sciences de l'éducation avec la mention très honorable.
items.description: Yamnékré Marguerite Ouédraogo a soutenu, dans l'après-midi du mercredi 23 septembre 2026, sa thèse de doctorat unique en sciences de l'éducation, spécialité mesure et évaluation, à l'université Norbert Zongo de Koudougou. Ses travaux portent sur l'évaluation comparative de l'efficacité de la pédagogie du texte et du bilinguisme de transfert dans les écoles bilingues de la région de Oubri. Au cours de sa recherche, la désormais docteure s'est intéressée aux effets de deux approches utilisées dans l'éducation bilingue : la pédagogie du texte et le bilinguisme de transfert. L'objectif était de mettre en évidence les apports respectifs de ces deux méthodes dans le développement des compétences des apprenants. Président du jury, le professeur François Sawadogo a souligné l'intérêt du travail réalisé par l'impétrante. Selon lui, la recherche a permis de faire ressortir des différences dans les résultats obtenus en fonction de l'approche utilisée. « Elle a comparé deux approches d'usage des langues dans l'éducation bilingue et a montré l'apport différencié de chacune d'elles », a-t-il expliqué. Le président du jury a notamment précisé que les résultats de la recherche incitent à envisager une combinaison des deux méthodes afin d'en optimiser l'efficacité. À l'issue de la soutenance, le jury a reconnu la qualité du travail présenté par Yamnékré Marguerite Ouédraogo et lui a décerné la mention « Très honorable ». Pour son directeur de thèse, le docteur Oumar Lingani, cette distinction traduit la reconnaissance unanime de la valeur scientifique du travail accompli. Il a toutefois invité la nouvelle docteure à ne pas considérer ce résultat comme une fin en soi, mais à œuvrer pour la valorisation de ses recherches. « Il faut souligner la pertinence et l'importance du travail fourni par l'étudiante, qui mérite objectivement d'être porté à la connaissance des autorités compétentes pour une exploitation adéquate », a-t-il indiqué. La nouvelle docteure entend d'ailleurs donner une suite pratique à ses travaux. Elle a annoncé son intention de valoriser les résultats de sa recherche, notamment par la publication d'articles scientifiques et leur mise à disposition des enseignants, des encadreurs et des décideurs. Selon les résultats présentés par l'impétrante, les apprenants issus du bilinguisme simultané ont obtenu de meilleures performances en expression écrite que ceux du bilinguisme de transfert. En revanche, ces derniers se sont davantage distingués en compréhension écrite. La chercheuse a également mentionné certaines difficultés rencontrées lors de ses enquêtes, notamment la réticence de quelques enseignants. Elle reconnaît par ailleurs, comme limite à son étude, la non-prise en compte de certains paramètres contextuels dans l'analyse des données. « Forte de ces compétences acquises, je m'emploierai à mettre ces résultats à la disposition des enseignants et des encadreurs afin qu'ils contribuent à l'amélioration des compétences bilitératiques des apprenants », a déclaré Yamnékré Marguerite Ouédraogo. Elle a enfin exprimé sa reconnaissance au président et aux membres du jury, l'examinateur, le docteur Gninneyo Sylvestre-Pierre Niya, et aux deux rapporteurs, le docteur Ibrahima Traoré et le docteur Wendkûuni Désiré Poudiougo, ainsi qu'à son directeur de thèse, le docteur Oumar Lingani, pour leur accompagnement tout au long de la réalisation de ce travail. Prince Omar Lefaso.net

items.title: Pope warns a ‘paradise of machines’ could undermine humanity as he opens France trip
items.description: Pope Leo XIV warned Friday that a “paradise of machines” risked undermining humanity as he opened a trip to France by posing fundamental questions about what it means to be human in the age of artificial intelligence, nuclear arms race and other threats to life itself. Leo raised existential concerns about scientific progress, life and human rights during his opening speech to President Emmanuel Macron and diplomats at the Élysée Palace. Given the wars plaguing Europe and the Middle East, he reaffirmed the Vatican’s opposition to nuclear weapons and said the nuclear deterrence doctrine was “mistaken” since it was just fueling a new arms race. “Peace is not a balance of power; rather, it is built day by day through dialogue and justice,” he said. Leo, whose paternal ancestors were French, arrived in Paris at the start of four intense days in France, where the Catholic Church has lost ground on influencing ethical issues given the strict approach to secularism that is enshrined in the French Constitution. Church bells tolled across France when Leo’s charter flight landed at Paris’ Orly airport, and upward of a million people are expected to turn out to see him. The welcome has underscored the surprising level of interest in Leo’s visit, the first official state visit by a pope in 18 years. Macron said Leo’s visit brings “a source of hope” to many French people. “France stands on the side of peace, effective multilateralism, respect for international law and the United Nations Charter … because every life has equal value, and all peoples must be defended,” he said. Later Friday, Leo was to visit UNESCO headquarters, celebrate vespers at the newly reopened Notre-Dame cathedral and then preside over a massive youth vigil at the Paris stadium Friday night. A capstone visit as Macron’s term ends For Macron, who is barred from seeking a third term in May elections, hosting the American pope is something of a capstone, after Pope Francis refused repeatedly to make a proper state visit to France during his 12-year pontificate. “For a president of the republic as Macron, who is at the end of his mandate, it can be important to be aside the pope and to capture a part of his popularity. It’s not new,” said Charles Mercier, director of history and sociology of Catholicism studies at Paris EPHE university. With seven months left in his term, Macron’s approval ratings are near record lows, driven by anger over the rising cost of living and criticism of France’s growing debt and deficit and deteriorating public services. Smiling broadly as Leo spoke French, Macron thanked the pope for visiting, saying: “You are here with us for an extended visit, giving us your time, and that is moving.” The Rev. Aristide Ahidote, from Ivory Coast, was among those who planned to attend the pope’s vespers service in Notre-Dame. “God has given us a pope with vigor and strength,” he said. While acknowledging the French church has declined in popularity, “it still has small remnants and these small remnants have been edifying for me.” Leo appeals to loftier questions about life Leo has been keen to emphasize Europe’s Christian roots and try to push the church’s message about the value and dignity of human life in a country where the right to abortion was enshrined in the constitution in 2024, and where lawmakers recently gave final approval to a bill allowing adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal medication. The French Catholic hierarchy strongly opposed the measures, in keeping with Catholic teaching that human life must be protected and defended from conception until natural death. In his speech to Macron and other government and diplomatic authorities, Leo called for France especially to remember that the right to life is the “indispensable foundation of every other human right.” He recalled France’s “deep Christian roots” and the recognition of human rights in warning about scientific progress and artificial intelligence. “If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a ‘paradise of machines’ invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment and the capacity to acknowledge the moral good,” he said. From the very start of his pontificate, Leo has identified artificial intelligence as one of the greatest challenges facing humanity. He dedicated his first encyclical to the topic, “Magnificent Humanity,” calling for robust regulation and for AI developers to work for the common good rather than profit. Leo also appealed to AI developers and political leaders responsible for regulating them to slow down, an appeal that several top AI companies seem to have taken to heart in recently. Speaking to reporters en route to Paris, Leo said he was pleased that his message was being heard and said he hoped the dialogue that the Vatican had initiated with tech companies would continue. “And I think from their perspective, many of them, they’re very much open to looking for ways of making sure that AI does not displace or ultimately destroy humanity, but rather than be a tool for human beings,” he said. “Good things are beginning at least.”

Pakistan secure another Asian Games medal as Noor, Ashab reach squash semis
items.description: Pakistan secured another medal at the Asian Games on Friday after Noor Zaman and Mohammad Ashab Irfan won their respective singles matches to reach the semi-finals of the squash competition. Third-seeded Noor defeated Hong Kong’s Chi Hin Henry Leung, while fifth-seeded Ashab overcame India’s Veer Chotrani at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena to put Pakistan into the medal rounds of the event. Noor, Pakistan’s top-ranked player in the draw, was pushed by Leung but held his nerve to secure a place in the last four. Ashab also produced a strong performance against the fourth-seeded Indian, recovering from losing the opening game to win 3-1. Ashab prevailed 6-11, 11-8, 11-6, 11-6 to avenge Pakistan’s defeat to India in the men’s team final at the previous Asian Games. The victories mean Pakistan are assured of at least a bronze medal in the men’s singles competition, with the losing semi-finalists awarded bronze. It is the first time since 2002 that two players for Pakistan have made it to the Asian Games semi-finals The two Pakistanis had reached the quarter-finals without dropping a game, with Noor defeating Kuwait’s Ammar Altamimi 11-4, 11-9, 11-4 and Ashab overcoming Saudi Arabia’s Mohammad Al Alnafsan 11-9, 11-3, 11-5 in the last 16 on Thursday. Noor and Ashab will now contest their respective semi-finals on Saturday, with a place in Sunday’s final at stake.

However, when Renard was asked about the comments from his Ghana counterpart, the Côte d’Ivoire coach chose not to engage in the debate. “As for the controversy launched by the Ghanaian coach, I’m not going to respond to him,” he stated. The result leaves Côte d’Ivoire top of Group C after the opening round of matches, while Ghana will have to regroup ahead of their next fixture. items.title: Explainer-What has turned the Afghan Taliban and Pakistan from partners to foes?
items.description: By Asif Shahzad ISLAMABAD, Sept 24 (Reuters) - Pakistan's air force struck 10 locations in Afghanistan on Thursday, its second round of strikes in four days after three months of relative quiet along the two countries' 2,600-km (1,600-mile) border. Islamabad said it struck militant hideouts in retaliation for drones launched from Afghanistan. items.title: 2027: For me as governor, opposing Tinubu means implosion – Otti
items.description: Abia State Governor Alex Otti has said opposing President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid while serving as a governor and member of the National Economic Council could lead to an “implosion”, explaining why he has to support the President despite belonging to the Labour Party. Otti stated this during an exclusive interview aired on Arise Television on Friday, following questions about whether his support for Tinubu’s re-election amounted to a “comfortable arrangement” between him, a Labour Party governor, and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The governor said he was not in a position to oppose Tinubu’s candidacy, given his role in the government and involvement in federal policy decisions. “It works the way you have said. It’s a statement of fact. I am not in a position to oppose his candidacy,” Otti said. He, however, distinguished between his position as a member of the National Economic Council and the Labour Party’s choice of a presidential candidate for the 2027 election. When asked whether he was supporting Tinubu for re-election, Otti recalled that he had previously stated that he had a presidential candidate for the Labour Party. After the interviewer identified Tinubu as the candidate, the governor rejected the suggestion. “No, that’s not what I said,” he said. Asked whether he was referring to a Labour Party presidential candidate, Otti replied, “Yes.” The interviewer subsequently pressed him on whether he was supporting Tinubu. “What do you expect me to say? To say I’m not supporting him?” Otti responded. The Abia governor said Tinubu had the right to contest the 2027 presidential election, adding that his membership of the National Economic Council meant he was involved in decisions and policies of the Federal Government. “I had also said that as a governor in this republic, that a lot of the things that are being, in fact, I’m part of all the things that have been done as a member of National Economic Council. So, we should distinguish that. “When somebody now says, ‘Oh, you are supporting or you’re not,’ I have to support him,” he said. Otti explained that he preferred to express disagreements with government policies during official meetings rather than publicly oppose the President. He warned that openly opposing Tinubu while remaining part of the government could create internal divisions and undermine its operations. “And sometimes people don’t understand opposition. When you say opposition, and you are part of a government, then what you are driving towards is implosion. “So if I do have a problem with anything, I’ll sit down in one of our meetings and I’ll make my point. So I’m not going to oppose his candidacy,” he added. The governor also said some of Tinubu’s policies aligned with his own views, citing the removal of the petrol subsidy as an example. According to Otti, the subsidy had become unsustainable, adding that people were not necessarily required to agree with his position. “Quite frankly, there are a lot of things that we have talked about now, that he has implemented, that resonate with me and my thinking. “People don’t have to agree with me, but from where I sit, I know that for instance, the fuel subsidy was even unsustainable,” Otti said. items.title: Images IA : quand une illustration devient trompeuse
items.description: Les images generees par intelligence artificielle permettent aujourd'hui d'illustrer presque tous les sujets. Mais lorsqu'elles sont utilisees pour representer un evenement reel, elles peuvent tromper le public et deformer sa perception des faits. Recemment, une page d'information a illustre l'interception d'un camion rempli de betail a Kenieba avec une image generee par IA, au lieu des images reelles de la saisie. Un autre exemple plus trompeur, le 22 août 2026, une forte pluie s'est abattue sur Tombouctou. Selon plusieurs sources locales, 68 millimetres de precipitations ont ete enregistres. Les intemperies ont provoque des degâts materiels dans plusieurs zones de la ville, avec notamment des maisons endommagees et certaines completement effondrees. Aucune perte en vie humaine n'a ete signalee dans les premieres informations disponibles. Dans ce contexte, une page a diffuse une image presentee comme montrant Tombouctou apres les fortes pluies. L'image montre notamment des habitations fortement endommagees ainsi qu'une mosquee qui ressemble a Djingareyber. a premiere vue, rien ne semble forcement alerter un internaute. L'image paraît realiste et correspond au type de degâts que peuvent provoquer de fortes pluies. Pourtant, apres verification, la rue visible sur l'image n'existe pas. Et selon notre correspondant a Tombouctou, Seyni Faye, le quartier de Djingareyber n'a pas ete touche par les inondations. Une image generee par intelligence artificielle La verification montre que cette image a ete generee par intelligence artificielle. Elle ne constitue donc pas une photographie prise a Tombouctou apres les pluies du 22 août. Le probleme n'est donc pas seulement que l'image soit artificielle. C'est surtout le contexte dans lequel elle est utilisee. Une image generee par IA peut parfaitement servir a illustrer un sujet. Elle devient problematique lorsqu'elle est presentee, volontairement ou non, comme la photographie d'un evenement reel. Dans le cas present, associer cette image aux inondations de Tombouctou peut conduire le public a croire qu'elle montre les degâts reellement constates sur place, alors qu'elle fabrique une scene qui n'existe pas. Une image trompeuse peut ainsi deformer la perception d'un evenement reel, renforcer une fausse representation des faits et contribuer a la diffusion d'une fausse information. Une image realiste n'est pas forcement une preuve Les outils d'intelligence artificielle permettent aujourd'hui de produire des images extremement realistes . Mais leur realisme ne garantit ni leur authenticite ni leur contexte. C'est l'un des principaux reflexes a developper en education aux medias, « ne pas confondre ce qui semble vrai avec ce qui est verifie. » Une image publiee sur Facebook, WhatsApp, TikTok ou un autre reseau social doit donc etre consideree comme une information a verifier, et non comme une preuve en elle-meme. Lire aussi : Pourquoi les rumeurs circulent elles si vite sur WhatsApp ? L’article Images IA : quand une illustration devient trompeuse est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Yacine Bammou devient ambassadeur de son ancien club en France
items.description: Yacine Bammou, âgé de 35 ans, fait son retour à l’AS Boulogne-Billancourt, son ancien club français. Après avoir décidé de ne pas poursuivre sa carrière au plus haut niveau, l’attaquant entame une nouvelle mission au sein de la formation française en tant qu’ambassadeur. Yacine Bammou retrouve un club qui a marqué ses débuts. L’ancien attaquant des Lions de l’Atlas revient à l’AS Boulogne-Billancourt, où il avait évolué entre 2010 et 2012, pour occuper désormais un rôle qui dépasse le cadre sportif. Le club français, qui évolue en Régional 2 et accorde une place importante à la formation, a annoncé le retour de Bammou en tant qu’ambassadeur. Sa mission consistera notamment à accompagner les joueurs et à leur transmettre son expérience du football professionnel, ainsi que les exigences nécessaires pour évoluer au plus haut niveau. Une carrière riche en expériences Le parcours de Yacine Bammou est marqué par une trajectoire atypique. Avant de devenir footballeur professionnel, le Marocain avait notamment travaillé comme vendeur dans une boutique du Paris Saint-Germain. Il a ensuite réussi à atteindre la Ligue 1 française, avant de poursuivre sa carrière en Turquie et au Maroc. Bammou a également porté le maillot de la sélection nationale marocaine à sept reprises, inscrivant un but. Au total, l’ancien attaquant a disputé plus de 350 rencontres professionnelles, pour 67 buts. Sa dernière expérience s’est déroulée sous les couleurs de l’Union Touarga, après notamment un passage par Dunkerque en Ligue 2 française. Transmettre son expérience aux jeunes Avec cette nouvelle fonction, Yacine Bammou entend désormais mettre son expérience au service des joueurs de l’AS Boulogne-Billancourt. Son retour est également un clin d’œil à ses débuts dans le football, plus d’une décennie après son premier passage au sein du club. Visiblement heureux de retrouver son ancien environnement, Bammou a également adressé un message aux supporters du club : « Je suis de retour au club, et je vous retrouve tous les dimanches au stade Gallu. Nous sommes ensemble, allez l’ASB ! » Après avoir connu la Ligue 1, la sélection marocaine et plusieurs expériences à l’étranger, l’ancien international entame ainsi un nouveau chapitre de sa carrière, cette fois dans un rôle tourné vers la transmission et l’accompagnement des jeunes joueurs. items.title: Aéronautique | Aksa Composites s’implante en Tunisie
items.description: La société turque Aksa Composites, filiale du groupe Akkök, vient d’officialiser son implantation en Tunisie avec la signature, jeudi 24 septembre 2026, de son bail industriel au Technopole de Borj Cédria, au sud de Tunis. «La Tunisie confirme son attractivité dans les industries aéronautiques et les matériaux avancés», commente le Groupement des industries tunisiennes aéronautiques et spatiales (Gitas) dans un communiqué. Le projet représente un investissement initial annoncé de 5 millions de dollars et constitue la première implantation d’Aksa Composites sur le continent africain. L’entreprise prévoit de développer en Tunisie des activités liées à la fabrication de composants et matériaux composites destinés notamment au secteur aéronautique. Le Gitas à la manœuvre Cette implantation est aussi le résultat d’un travail engagé en amont par l’écosystème aéronautique tunisien et, notamment, par le Gitas, sous l’impulsion de sa présidente Stefania Sonia Dallali, qui a joué un rôle important dans l’identification et la mise en relation avec l’investisseur turc. Les premiers contacts avec Aksa Composites remontent au Hamburg Aviation Forum 2025, où des échanges ont été initiés avec le Gitas. Ils ont ensuite donné lieu à plusieurs discussions, rencontres et démarches visant à faire connaître à l’entreprise les capacités industrielles tunisiennes, son tissu de sous-traitants, ses compétences et son intégration dans les chaînes de valeur aéronautiques internationales. «Cette dynamique illustre l’une des missions fondamentales du Gitas : rapprocher les industriels internationaux de l’écosystème tunisien et favoriser l’émergence de nouvelles opportunités d’investissement et de coopération dans l’aéronautique et le spatial» , souligne le groupement professionnel dans son communiqué. Mme Dallali a souligné la portée de l’arrivée d’Aksa Composites en Tunisie. Pour le Gitas, le choix de la Tunisie par un acteur turc spécialisé dans les matériaux composites avancés constitue une nouvelle illustration de la confiance acquise par la filière aéronautique tunisienne au cours des dernières décennies. Avec un tissu industriel de plus de 80 entreprises et une forte orientation export, la filière tunisienne s’est progressivement intégrée aux chaînes de valeur internationales. La qualité des compétences, la proximité de l’Europe, la flexibilité industrielle et l’existence d’un écosystème de fournisseurs constituent autant d’atouts mis en avant pour attirer de nouveaux investissements. Stefania Sonia Dallali entourée des représentants de la société turque. Fipa assure l’accompagnement institutionnel La présidente du Gitas a également rappelé l’importance du développement des partenariats internationaux de la filière, notamment avec les organisations professionnelles française et allemande de l’aéronautique. Le rôle du Gitas s’inscrit dans une dynamique complémentaire avec celui de la Fipa-Tunisia. L’agence de promotion de l’investissement extérieur a accompagné le projet dans ses différentes étapes et a notamment participé aux échanges portant sur le choix du site, les conditions d’implantation et les démarches nécessaires à la concrétisation de l’investissement. Une rencontre organisée par la Fipa le 19 mai 2026 avait notamment permis de confirmer le projet et de poursuivre les discussions autour de son implantation en Tunisie. La signature du bail industriel à Borj Cédria vient ainsi concrétiser un processus auquel ont contribué plusieurs acteurs de l’écosystème tunisien : Gitas, Fipa, le Technopole de Borj Cédria ainsi que les partenaires institutionnels et professionnels tunisiens et turcs. Un investissement à forte valeur ajoutée À travers cette implantation, Aksa Composites entend développer une activité industrielle orientée vers les matériaux composites et les applications aéronautiques. Le groupe dispose déjà d’une expertise internationale dans les matériaux composites et dans différentes opérations industrielles destinées notamment aux secteurs aéronautique et à haute performance. Il a également développé des collaborations avec plusieurs grands acteurs internationaux de l’industrie aéronautique. Selon les informations communiquées, le futur site de Borj Cédria devrait constituer le point de départ d’un développement industriel appelé à évoluer progressivement en Tunisie. Des sources sectorielles évoquent un démarrage opérationnel envisagé à l’horizon 2028 et la création à terme de plusieurs dizaines d’emplois directs. Au-delà du montant de l’investissement, l’enjeu réside donc également dans le transfert de technologies, le développement des compétences locales et le renforcement de la place de la Tunisie dans les chaînes de valeur internationales des matériaux avancés et de l’aéronautique. joué par le Gitas dans la dynamique industrielle et par la FIPA dans l’accompagnement de l’investissement. items.title: Publicité : Meta applique la TVA au Maroc dès octobre
items.description: Les annonceurs marocains utilisant les services publicitaires de Meta devront composer avec une nouvelle règle de facturation à partir du 1er octobre 2026. Une TVA de 20 % sera appliquée selon les informations fiscales renseignées dans leurs comptes publicitaires. Les dépenses publicitaires effectuées sur Facebook et Instagram vont évoluer pour certains annonceurs au Maroc. Meta a informé ses clients d’un changement de traitement fiscal qui entrera en vigueur le 1er octobre 2026, avec l’application d’une TVA au taux actuellement fixé à 20 %. Le dispositif concerne notamment les comptes publicitaires pour lesquels le Maroc est indiqué comme pays de vente et dont le numéro d’identification fiscale (TIN) n’est pas renseigné. Dans cette configuration, la TVA sera ajoutée au coût des achats publicitaires effectués auprès de Meta. Les annonceurs peuvent toutefois renseigner leur identifiant fiscal depuis les paramètres de paiement de leur compte. Le numéro apparaîtra alors sur les reçus correspondant aux dépenses publicitaires. Dans ce cas, Meta indique que la TVA ne sera pas directement ajoutée aux achats publicitaires lorsque les conditions fiscales prévues sont remplies. La charge fiscale n’est cependant pas nécessairement supprimée. Pour les annonceurs concernés, le traitement repose sur le mécanisme de l’autoliquidation, ou « reverse charge », prévu par la réglementation marocaine. Ils restent ainsi responsables du calcul et du paiement de la TVA selon les règles applicables à leur situation fiscale. Ce changement concerne donc directement les entreprises et professionnels qui utilisent les plateformes de Meta pour leurs campagnes commerciales au Maroc. La présence ou non des informations fiscales dans le compte publicitaire devient notamment déterminante dans le traitement de la taxe. Le fonctionnement des seuils de facturation ne sera, lui, pas modifié. Meta précise que la TVA, lorsqu’elle est appliquée, s’ajoute au montant des dépenses publicitaires mais ne permet pas d’atteindre plus rapidement le seuil de facturation défini pour le compte. Le montant effectivement prélevé peut néanmoins dépasser ce seuil en raison de la taxe. Un traitement spécifique est également prévu pour les comptes alimentés à l’avance. En cas de paiement prépayé, la TVA est calculée au taux en vigueur au moment du financement du compte. Au taux actuel de 20 %, elle est donc intégrée au montant pris en compte pour déterminer le solde effectivement disponible pour les campagnes publicitaires. L’évolution annoncée par Meta intervient dans le cadre de la réforme engagée par le Maroc pour soumettre à la TVA les services numériques fournis par des entreprises non résidentes. La Direction générale des impôts a lancé en mai 2026 la plateforme électronique « Taxation on Digital Services », destinée aux fournisseurs étrangers de services à distance. Le dispositif concerne les prestataires non établis au Maroc qui fournissent électroniquement des services à des clients dont le siège, l’établissement ou le domicile fiscal se trouve dans le Royaume et qui ne sont pas eux-mêmes assujettis à la TVA. Le cadre réglementaire a notamment été précisé par le décret n° 2.25.862 du 27 novembre 2025, qui complète le dispositif d’application de la TVA et fixe les modalités d’enregistrement des fournisseurs non résidents, de déclaration de leur chiffre d’affaires réalisé au Maroc et de paiement de la taxe. L’entrée en application de ces règles commence désormais à se traduire dans les services proposés par les grandes plateformes internationales. Avant Meta, d’autres acteurs du numérique ont adapté leur facturation au marché marocain. TikTok a ainsi officiellement indiqué que ses services publicitaires fournis à des clients au Maroc sont soumis à une TVA de 20 % lorsque ceux-ci ne communiquent pas un identifiant marocain valide. La plateforme précise également que les clients disposant des informations fiscales requises peuvent relever du mécanisme d’autoliquidation prévu par la législation marocaine. De son côté, OpenAI applique depuis le 1er août 2026 une TVA de 20 % à certains services fournis à des clients marocains non assujettis, notamment les abonnements ChatGPT et certains services API. The post Publicité : Meta applique la TVA au Maroc dès octobre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘Bus would be better’ — Nigerians react over car used to pick Super Eagles players from airport
items.description: Nigerians on social media have reacted after a 2008 Toyota Avalon was reportedly used to pick up Super Eagles players from the airport ahead of their 2026 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON, qualifying clash against Madagascar in Uyo. The vehicle attracted attention after images and videos of the players being conveyed from the airport circulated on social media, with some fans criticising the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, over what they described as an inappropriate mode of transportation for the national team. One X user, @Adikastakes, wrote: “The Super Eagles were picked from the Airport with 2008 Toyota Avalon, NFF remains a massive disgrace. I just hope Eric Chelle and the players work a miracle and qualify for AFCON starting from defeating Madagascar.” Another user, @IghoBryan, wrote: “If them use bus e better pass this car These players guide pass all these shit wey NFF dey do ….these players personally dey drive Bentley, lambos and all but see car lmaoo.” @oyewi75457 also criticised the arrangement, writing: “NFF will never miss an opportunity to embarrass us. How are you picking up the Super Eagles with a 2008 Avalon in 2026?” Another user, @mosswan1, compared the vehicle with the cars available to some of the players abroad, writing: “Just imagine say Saka leave England come deh pass through this thing… All this players there lowest car for there garage go buy this car 4 times.” However, some Nigerians defended the choice of vehicle, arguing that transportation from the airport should not be a major issue compared with the team’s performance and other challenges facing Nigerian football. “The car used to carry them from the airport is the least of our problems right now, we don’t even have proper stadiums na car we dey talk about,” @Olique7 wrote. Similarly, @mom_boy76677 said there was nothing inherently wrong with the vehicle, arguing that the focus should be on the team’s performance. “There’s nothing wrong with the car, is the same car a normal businessman would book as uber from the airport, it has nothing to do with commitment. The car is not their preparation, is just a mobility,” the user wrote. The Super Eagles are preparing for a crucial AFCON qualifying fixture against Madagascar in Uyo as they seek to strengthen their position in the qualifying race. The team is being led by coach Eric Chelle, who is expected to guide the squad through the remaining qualifying fixtures. The reaction over the airport vehicle comes amid wider scrutiny of the NFF and the Super Eagles following Nigeria’s failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. With the AFCON qualifiers now providing another opportunity for the national team to deliver success, attention will turn to the players’ performance on the pitch when they face Madagascar. items.title: Gestion des ressources : de nouvelles mesures au Burkina
items.description: © Internet Le Conseil des ministres burkinabè a adopté, jeudi 24 septembre 2026, plusieurs mesures relatives à la gestion des ressources mobilisées pour le développement. La création d’une structure consacrée à l’entretien du patrimoine public et l’adoption de nouvelles règles applicables aux organisations non gouvernementales figurent parmi les principales décisions. La gestion des ressources occupe ainsi une place importante dans les textes adoptés à Ouagadougou. Réuni sous la présidence du capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Conseil des ministres a notamment précisé le cadre de partenariat entre l’État, les ONG et les associations de développement. La création de Faso Sanya, nouvel établissement public à caractère administratif, constitue l’une des principales mesures à portée économique. La structure sera chargée de la maintenance préventive et corrective des bâtiments publics, notamment dans les domaines du nettoyage, de la plomberie, de l’électricité, de la climatisation et de la rénovation. À travers cette structure, le gouvernement entend professionnaliser la maintenance du patrimoine immobilier public, mutualiser les ressources et améliorer la prise en charge des infrastructures. Faso Sanya travaillera avec la Maison des Compétences Burkina Suudu Bawdè afin de mobiliser des coopératives regroupant des ouvriers qualifiés. Cette organisation pourrait ouvrir de nouvelles possibilités aux artisans, aux coopératives et aux petites structures spécialisées dans les services techniques. Elle doit également permettre à l’État de mieux préserver son patrimoine immobilier et de planifier les interventions d’entretien. Le Conseil des ministres a également adopté deux décrets précisant les conditions d’obtention du statut d’ONG ainsi que les modalités de collaboration entre l’État et les organisations associatives. Ces textes s’inscrivent dans l’application de la loi du 17 juillet 2025 portant liberté d’association. Les ONG intervenant au Burkina Faso devront désormais consacrer au moins 80 % de leur budget global aux investissements directs. Selon le gouvernement, cette disposition instaure une clé de répartition commune destinée à orienter une plus grande part des ressources vers les programmes et les populations bénéficiaires. Un accord-cadre sera exigé des associations de droit burkinabè, tandis que les organisations étrangères seront régies par une convention de siège. Les nouvelles dispositions prévoient également une évaluation administrative, financière et technique des activités. Une période transitoire de deux ans est accordée aux organisations concernées pour se conformer à ces exigences. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: Why Macklemore Was Kicked Off the Ed Sheeran Tour
items.description: Among the many reckonings sparked after the rapper Macklemore was booted from Ed Sheeran’s tour earlier this month, one of the more amusing ones has been about taste. Macklemore, who’d gotten ejected after saying “Free Palestine” onstage, is widely seen as a goofy mascot of Millennial cringe. Sheeran, who put out a statement declining to share his personal views on “this devastating conflict” and then continued his tour, is a folk-pop singer beloved at children’s birthday parties. Now some pro-Palestine music fans are joking that “Thrift Shop,” Macklemore’s saxophone-skronked 2012 hit, isn’t as annoying as they’d thought. As for Sheeran, his bland songwriting is serving as a rhetorical piñata. “This crisis is the worst thing that has happened to Ed Sheeran fans since their head injury,” sniped a comedian on Saturday Night Live UK . Political allegiances and artistic quality don’t actually correlate, but it does make sense that music’s most consequential confrontation over Israel and Palestine has been driven by two of the least cool people in all of popular culture. Precisely because they’re perceived to have little edge or relevance, Sheeran and Macklemore offered a perfect test case for questions about whether popular music is expected to change the world or distract from it, rebel against the system or serve the man—and who exactly sets those expectations. The situation began earlier this month when the 43-year-old Macklemore gave speeches centered on the phrase “Free Palestine” while opening for Sheeran at two shows in New Jersey. “I want those words to be loud and clear, so the people from Gaza all the way to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten them,” he said. He also played “Hind’s Hall,” a 2024 track that accuses Israel of genocide and voices support for pro-Palestinian campus protesters in the U.S. Imagery of those protests and the destruction in Gaza played on screens behind him. Groups such as the Anti-Defamation League and StopAntisemitism quickly issued criticism calling Macklemore bigoted and—to quote a petition from the Israeli-American Council—“biased.” In a lengthy post, the musician Pink wrote that Macklemore had caused her to feel fear “as a Jewish mom.” Much of the outcry connected Macklemore’s performance to an incident in 2014 in which he caused offense by wearing a costume that looked an awful lot like a Jewish caricature. At the time, the rapper apologized and said he’d disguised himself with random props without realizing the implications of how he looked. The backlash then was loud but died down relatively quickly, and the ADL said that it “accepted Macklemore at his word.” This time, the billionaire Robert Kraft, who co-owns Gillette Stadium, in Massachusetts, called Sheeran to say that he wouldn’t allow Macklemore to play his venue and that neither would a number of other stadium owners. On September 14, the rapper was dropped from the billing. Shortly after that, all of the tour’s other opening acts, plus Sheeran’s backing band, quit in protest. (Sheeran’s tour is still ongoing, though he is now the only performing act.) Sheeran, one of the most popular musicians on Earth, has argued throughout this saga that refereeing controversy simply isn’t part of his job. “Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum,” he wrote in his initial statement last week. “I have always used my platform and music to bring people from all backgrounds and cultures together and this won’t ever change.” On Saturday, after days of public outcry against him, he opened his first show since Macklemore’s departure by offering some thoughts on Israel and Palestine and apologizing for “mistakes” he’d made. But he reasserted, again, that he tries to stay out of politics as much as possible. Sheeran has lots of company in the annals of musicians who have professed that their commitment to unity precludes them from taking a stand. Last year, Pharrell said that he “despises” politics because “when you pick a side, you are inadvertently supporting division.” Dolly Parton famously maintained bipartisan appeal by avoiding wading into most touchy issues. Billy Joel once described the role of musicians as “more like court jesters than court philosophers.” Ever since the Chicks drew conservative fury by criticizing George W. Bush in 2003, mainstream artists have understood that some portion of their audience prefers that they—to quote Fox News’s Laura Ingraham—“shut up and sing.” That point of view has always been a bit at odds with the fact that many of history’s most beloved songs have been forged by struggle and sloganeering. But part of what makes Sheeran both successful and uncool has long been his knack for cleaving musical traditions of their social context. His slickly grooving songs tend to evoke artists who had a clear point of view—a Bob Dylan cadence here, a Stevie Wonder melody there—even as his lyrics stick to the generic or autobiographical. He is a proudly mathematically minded musician (check his album titles) who openly talks about chart positions and sales figures. He has calculated, no doubt correctly, that a market exists for music that hides itself away from the world’s problems. But the thing about the word political is that its definition is always changing. What’s uncontroversial in one moment may be a divisive topic the next. And some issues that seem like ballot-box concerns can quickly snowball into moral emergencies. The free-speech questions related to Israel and Palestine have become so hot that they’re burning through his firewall—because it’s become clear even to him that silence is a form of taking a side. Tensions have been building to this moment ever since Hamas’s October 7 attacks killed more than 1,200 Israelis, hundreds of whom were civilians attending the Nova music festival. Even as Israel’s counteroffensive in Gaza—which has claimed at least 73,000 lives, according to the Hamas-run Health Ministry—sparked so much outcry that it upended the domestic politics of Israel’s international allies, musicians have felt stymied in their own efforts at protest on the matter. The R&B singer Kehlani, an outspoken supporter of the Palestinian cause, lost gigs at Cornell and in New York City’s Central Park after pro-Israel groups and politicians raised objections. The rap acts Kneecap (from Ireland) and Bob Vylan (from the U.K.) faced criminal investigations in the U.K. and visa problems in the U.S. following onstage comments regarding Gaza. (More on those in a minute.) Given the bloody history of anti-Semitism, those controversies have largely centered on the question of what divides legitimate activism from hate speech and incitement to violence. A Kehlani music video flashes the phrase Long live the Intifada , which many Palestinians hear as a cry for liberation and many Jews say endorses mass murder. After Kneecap’s pro-Palestine statements at 2025 Coachella drew media attention, footage surfaced of an earlier concert in which a member of the group yelled “Up Hamas, up Hezbollah.” (The band said it condemns “all attacks on civilians, always.”) At the Glastonbury music festival, Vylan’s front man chanted “Death, death to the IDF!” (which the group later said was not a call for violence but rather “for the dismantling of a violent military machine”). Watching those episodes, other musicians have taken care to modulate their approach. Earlier this year, I covered a concert in Los Angeles, called Artists for Aid , that brought together 20 pop, R&B, and rock artists to raise money for victims of conflict in Gaza and Sudan. The event was serene and uplifting, sometimes to the point of somnolence; speakers and singers did not even say Israel onstage. The organizer, the singer Mustafa, told me that the event had been carefully designed to avoid criticism. Even so, the show was hard to pull off: Though he’d held two similarly mellow installments of Artists for Aid in New Jersey and London, Mustafa told me he’d been turned down by at least half a dozen venues in L.A. Those places gave no explanation for saying no, but he was sure their refusals were related to Gaza. “Hind’s Hall” is, rather astonishingly, the most significant protest song related to Israel that’s been released by an American musician since October 7, and its lyrics take on the question of why musicians haven’t been louder about Gaza. “You can ban TikTok, take us out the algorithm,” Macklemore raps in “Hind’s Hall,” citing the theory that social-media regulations are targeting activists. Another line—“If I was on a label, you could drop me today”—suggests that artists who criticize Israel risk losing industry support. (Macklemore has long released music independently.) To anyone who knows Macklemore mainly from “Thrift Shop,” a novelty hit in which he seemed to satirize hip-hop’s rags-to-riches tropes by boasting about “flannel zebra jammies,” his political salience may seem surprising. But the truth is that he’s always been an earnest—eye-wateringly so—contributor to the tradition of “conscious” hip-hop that approaches the medium as a tool for social change. His 2012 hit “Same Love” made the case for acceptance of same-sex marriage before it was legal in the United States. After October 7, he posted that Hamas’s murder and kidnapping of Israelis was “horrific” but that “killing innocent humans in retaliation as collective punishment is not the answer.” Weeks later, he spoke at a pro-Palestine rally. Sheeran had to have known Macklemore’s politics when he booked him; perhaps he just figured that whatever he said wouldn’t prove to be very controversial. And indeed, Macklemore’s performance almost seemed designed to test what exactly can be said on the world’s largest stages. He didn’t use particularly inflammatory slogans. He went out of his way to specify whom he wasn’t attacking: “To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters, criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is criticism of you,” he said. “My message is for peace, love, for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.” But the answer came back swiftly and conclusively: Even a couched protest, on this subject, is going to cause a furor. Some of Macklemore’s critics emphasized the need to protect the audience from discomfort. Pink objected to the fact that “he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them.” The ADL wrote, “Imagine being a Jewish or Israeli fan who came with family or friends to enjoy the show, only to be confronted with this hostility from the stage.” Macklemore, in a statement, said that Sheeran had told him that “a lot of people he spoke with” view the words Free Palestine and the image of the Palestinian flag as “hurtful.” A StopAntisemitism tweet said, “Fans deserve apologies and refunds. Unacceptable.” Those statements carry the implication that Macklemore broke a contract between performers and the public. But audiences aren’t a monolith (a lot of the stadium seemed to be cheering in videos of Macklemore’s comments). And audiences, as it turns out, aren’t who decide what’s permissible—behind-the-scenes power brokers are. According to Sheeran, the choice to drop Macklemore was made by venue owners and Messina Touring, the promotion company for many of the most prominent tours in America. Kraft acknowledged his role in a statement that accused the rapper of “sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas.” By that logic, Macklemore was banned based not only on what he said but on what he didn’t say: a breathtaking assertion of a venue owner’s prerogative to dictate on-stage expression. “Israel does not have a more loyal friend than Robert Kraft,” Benjamin Netanyahu said in 2019 when presenting him with a $1 million prize, and Kraft’s involvement in the seemingly trivial matter of what a tour opener says between songs suggests larger geopolitical stakes at play. Voters in both major political parties are less convinced than ever about America’s continuing support of the Israeli government. The Palestinian cause—and related policies such as ending military aid to Israel and unwinding the two-tiered legal system that governs Gaza and the West Bank—has proved persuasive to the general public in the past few years. Defenders of the status quo have reason to try to prevent that case from being amplified. The irony is that the tactics in this case are so blatantly repressive that they’re spreading Macklemore’s message—and the pro-Palestinian movement’s concerns about institutional deplatforming—far more broadly than would have otherwise happened. Macklemore’s words had been aimed at a ticketed crowd, but they quickly reached the national news. With even his backing band quitting the tour, Sheeran’s avowals of being beyond politics came to look, to many, like he’d clearly acquiesced to an act of censorship. Announcing a “Free Palestine” tour today, Macklemore wrote, “When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention.” By Saturday’s show in Philadelphia, Sheeran had recalibrated. He opened the concert with a speech in which he said the question of Israel and Palestine now transcended politics: “This is a humanitarian issue and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore.” After condemning the October 7 attack for compounding “centuries of Jewish pain,” he added, “What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate.” And he had a word, it seemed, for Kraft: “I am deeply worried about the idea that venues should pre-approve content of performers. This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.” He’s right on that last point—but the repression he refers to is of a piece with the kind of censorship that’s touched all corners of American culture in recent years. The Trump White House has issued threats to broadcasters predicated on the idea of restoring neutrality to the airwaves. Paramount Skydance has signaled a willingness to accept government input on programming decisions in the name of fighting bias. Cultural institutions have been forced to rework and ditch all manner of diversity-related programming in order to counteract supposed liberal propaganda. What’s become obvious is that calls for a less “political” public sphere do, inevitably, serve a political agenda. At his latest show, Sheeran’s foray into political speechifying had him in tears, and he closed by offering an apology to families who “didn’t buy a ticket to hear that first bit of the show.” But he also said that it was the best concert he’d ever played, and that the backlash he feared he might face from his own fans never materialized. It’s as if he was realizing, in real time, that it wasn’t his audience who’d wanted him to stay quiet all these years—and that there might be unity to be found in going beyond the platitudes of a pop song to say what he really thinks.

items.title: Cameroun/ Électricité : l’ARSEL et la Banque mondiale s’accordent sur les priorités d’investissement
items.description: © DR Le mardi 22 septembre 2026, l'Agence de régulation du secteur de l'electricité a reçu une équipe de la Banque mondiale à son siège. Objectif : préparer un nouveau programme d'investissement pour améliorer la performance du système électrique camerounais, avec trois axes prioritaires retenus. La performance du système électrique au cœur des échanges. Le mardi 22 septembre 2026, au siège de l'ARSEL, l'Agence de Régulation du Secteur de l'Électricité a tenu une séance de concertation avec une équipe de la Banque mondiale, dans le cadre de la préparation d'un nouveau programme d'investissement dans le secteur de l'énergie. Au cœur des échanges, les projets susceptibles de contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance du système électrique, notamment l'étude du coût du service et la tarification de l'électricité, la gestion dynamique de la demande (« demand response ») pour mieux équilibrer l'offre et la demande, et le relèvement du facteur de puissance afin d'optimiser l'utilisation des capacités disponibles. Les discussions ont également porté sur la réduction des pertes dans le réseau de distribution, l'amélioration des outils de prévision de la demande et le renforcement des capacités de planification et de régulation. À l'issue de la rencontre, trois axes ont été retenus comme prioritaires pour la première phase : coût du service et tarification, gestion de la demande et relèvement du facteur de puissance. Une concertation qui traduit la volonté commune de renforcer la performance, l'efficacité et la durabilité du secteur de l'électricité au Cameroun. Cet article Cameroun/ Électricité : l'ARSEL et la Banque mondiale s'accordent sur les priorités d'investissement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Journée mondiale du gorille : le WWF et le MINFOF sensibilisent les élèves de Salapoumbé
items.description: © DR À l'occasion de la Journée mondiale du gorille célébrée le 24 septembre, le WWF - Programme Jengi TNS, en partenariat avec le Ministère des Forêts et de la Faune, a organisé une journée de sensibilisation à Salapoumbé, dans la région de l'Est, à l'intention des élèves. Protéger le gorille pour préserver la forêt. À l'occasion de la Journée mondiale du gorille, célébrée le 24 septembre, le WWF - Programme Jengi TNS, en partenariat avec le MINFOF, a organisé une journée de sensibilisation auprès des élèves de Salapoumbé, dans la région de l'Est. Au programme, des échanges pédagogiques sur l'importance des gorilles, espèce emblématique du bassin du Congo, et sur la nécessité de protéger leur habitat, de plus en plus menacé par le braconnage et la déforestation. Les activités se sont poursuivies par des séances de plantation d'arbres avec les élèves, geste symbolique et concret en faveur de la restauration des écosystèmes. À travers ces actions, le WWF et le MINFOF entendent encourager les jeunes à mieux comprendre, protéger et préserver la biodiversité qui les entoure, et à devenir des ambassadeurs de la conservation au sein de leurs communautés. Une initiative qui s'inscrit dans les efforts de conservation du paysage transfrontalier Tri-National de la Sangha. items.title: Teacher unions declare nationwide strike over unpaid promotion arrears and delayed negotiations
items.description: The three teacher unions — the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG), have declared a nationwide industrial action effective Friday, September 25, 2026, following the government’s failure to resolve outstanding issues concerning the payment of promotion allowances and arrears owed to teachers. The unions had given the government until midday on Thursday, September 24, 2026, to address the concerns. The unions say the decision follows what they describe as prolonged delays, unfulfilled commitments and growing frustration over conditions affecting teachers. “In light of the above circumstances and given the delays, unfulfilled promises on the part of the duty bearers and the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC), as well as threats by the rank-and-file of our members, we, the teacher unions, do stand with our members and hereby declare a nationwide industrial action (Strike), effective today, Friday, 25th September 2026,” the statement said. In a joint statement dated September 25, the unions cited three major concerns, including the delay in negotiating a new Collective Agreement, the failure to automatically place newly promoted teachers on the appropriate salary scales, and the non-implementation of the Deprived Area Allowance. According to the unions, the existing Collective Agreement has expired, while negotiations for a new agreement, which they say should have been completed by June 2026, remain outstanding. They said the matter has been raised with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) several times, but has yet to be resolved. The teacher unions are also demanding the automatic placement of teachers who successfully passed the promotion examinations in December 2025 and February 2026 onto their respective salary scales, including payment of arrears effective January 2026. They said the failure to implement the arrangement has created tension and anger among their members. On the Deprived Area Allowance, the unions referenced provisions in the 2024 Collective Agreement requiring the Ministry of Education and the Ghana Education Service (GES) to review the Deprived Area Report for implementation, after which the unions and the FWSC would negotiate the applicable figures. They, however, said this process has not been completed. The unions further expressed concern about what they described as a failure to honour a directive on incentives for teachers working in deprived and hard-to-reach areas. They said the outstanding issues have resulted in “widespread disaffection, anger, and disillusionment” among their members.

items.title: Forum de l’International Pact Patriotic Organisation: Le ROJALNU salue la dynamique politique engagée par le président du Faso
items.description: A la faveur du Forum de l’International Pact Patriotic Organisation tenu à l’office des Nations Unies à Naìrobi le lundi 21 septembre 2026, le président mondial du Réseau des Organisations des Jeunes Leaders Africains des Nations Unies (ROJALNU), le Burkinabè Abraham Zida Bila, a appelé à une mobilisation internationale en faveur d’un « Pacte Patriotique International » fondé sur la souveraineté des nations, le droit au développement et la paix. Nairobi, la capitale kenyane a accueilli le lundi 21 septembre le Forum de l’International Pact Patriotic Organisation . Rencontre au cours de laquelle le président mondial du Réseau des Organisations des Jeunes Leaders Africains des Nations Unies (ROJALNU), le Burkinabè Abraham Zida Bila a, dans un discours solennel appelé à une mobilisation internationale en faveur d’un « Pacte Patriotique International » fondé sur la souveraineté des nations, le droit au développement et la paix. Abraham Zida Bila défend ainsi un pacte qui, selon lui, devrait servir de cadre de solidarité entre les nations et favoriser des relations fondées sur des intérêts mutuellement bénéfiques. Il a estimé que les relations internationales doivent évoluer vers davantage d’équité et de respect entre les peuples. « Le développement ne doit pas être une faveur accordée aux uns et refusée aux autres. Le développement est un droit. La souveraineté est un droit. La dignité est un droit. Et la paix est un droit universel », a-t-il déclaré. Evoquant la situation du Burkina Faso et la dynamique politique engagée sous le leadership du capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le président mondial du ROJALNU a informé que cette dynamique dépasse les frontières du Burkina Faso et porte un message à la jeunesse africaine : celui de la possibilité pour les peuples de « prendre leur destin en main ». Il a cité la coopération entre le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger au sein de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES), qu’il présente comme une illustration de la nécessité pour les États de renforcer leur solidarité et de mutualiser leurs capacités. M. Bila a annoncé l’organisation à Ouagadougou, en décembre prochain, d’un Colloque mondial de la jeunesse. Cette rencontre réunira des jeunes, des organisations de la société civile, des intellectuels, des leaders et des acteurs du développement autour des questions de souveraineté, de développement et de paix. Yves OUEDRAOGO

items.description: (New-York, le 25 septembre 2026) Le ministre des Affaires étrangères, le Camarade Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORE s'est entretenu avec son homologue de la République Gabonaise dans les locaux des Nations Unies à New-York, le jeudi 24 septembre 2026. A cette audience, le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè et S.E. Madame Marie-Edith Tassyla-Ye-Doumbeneny, ont salué la qualité des relations historiques entre la République Gabonaise et le Burkina Faso, des relations humaines et fraternelles caractérisées par une forte communauté deux pays installée de part et d’autre. Ils ont exprimé leur disponibilité à œuvrer à la consolidation des liens entre les deux pays, avec en ligne de mire la tenue en novembre prochain de la grande Commission mixte de coopération Burkina Faso-République Gabonaise. Cette Commission mixte permettra de renforcer et d'actualiser les instruments juridiques pour davantage dynamiser l'axe Ouagadougou-Libreville et en faire un modèle de coopération Sud-Sud. Il faut également noter que le Camarade ministre des Affaires étrangères a accordé une audience à la ministre d’Etat chargée du Développement international du Royaume Uni, S.E. Madame Kirsty McNEILL. Celle-ci est venue solliciter le soutien du Burkina Faso pour les candidatures britanniques aux postes internationaux. Le ministre TRAORE a indiqué que le Burkina Faso va examiner attentivement cette requête, tout en soulignant que la coopération entre Ouagadougou et Londres a besoin d'être renforcée.
