items.title: Delegate walkout, protests greet Netanyahu as he addresses UN General Assembly
items.description: NEW YORK: Dozens of delegates walked out of the UN General Assembly hall on Thursday as hundreds of protesters gathered outside the building while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended Tel Aviv’s actions amid growing international isolation, with elections looming that could threaten his political future. The walkout undersco­red the competing pressu­res facing Netanyahu, who is battling mounting criticism abroad over the Gaza conflict while campaigning for re-election at home ahead of an October 27 vote. On Thursday, Netanyahu delivered a combative address inside the General Assembly, where dozens of delegations walked out as he began speaking. The departing diplomats left large sections of the hall empty, creating a striking contrast with Netanyahu’s attempt to use the podium to present Israel’s case before the international community. Netanyahu responded by accusing his critics of hypocrisy and calling them “moral cowards.” He rejected allegations that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, saying Israel had prevented rather than committed genocide. He defended the country’s military actions in Gaza and elsewhere in the region. Delegates walk out of the General Assembly hall as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrives to address the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24. — Reuters He also devoted a significant part of his speech to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, calling him “the antisemitic mayor of New York” and accusing him of spreading what Netanyahu described as lies about Israel. Mamdani, who had declined to join the street protests, responded after the speech. “Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians,” Mamdani said. “No lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.” Mamdani previously said New York City lacked the authority to enforce the ICC warrant against Netanyahu, arguing that the appropriate authorities should carry it out. On Wednesday night, the mayor had hosted Palestinian families from Gaza at Gracie Mansion and planted an olive tree with them, saying: “May peace be our future.” The two scenes — protesters confronting his government’s policies on the streets and diplomats leaving the hall during his address — turned Netanyahu’s brief visit to New York into a day of parallel confrontation. Netanyahu’s stay had already been sharply shortened amid security concerns and expectations of protests. He arrived on Thursday morning, addressed the General Assembly and was scheduled to return to Israel the same evening rather than remain in New York overnight. Outside the UN, Jewish and Muslim activists, Palestinian supporters, human-rights campaigners, progressive Jewish groups, politicians, artists and musicians took part in separate demonstrations across Manhattan. Their messages varied, but opposition to Netanyahu’s government and Israel’s conduct of the Gaza conflict brought many of them into the streets at the same time. Demonstrators protest after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the United Nations 81st General Assembly in New York City, U.S., September 24. — Reuters The protests also offered a visible glimpse of a generational shift in American attitudes toward Israel and Netanyahu. While support for Israel remains stronger among older Americans, younger Americans have become substantially more critical of the Israeli government. A Pew Research Centre survey conducted in May found that only 18 per cent of Americans aged 18 to 29 had a favourable view of the Israeli government, compared with 47pc among those aged 65 and older. Among the youngest Americans, 58pc expressed a favourable view of Palestinians, compared with 47pc among those 65 and older. That generational divide was visible on the streets of New York, where many of the demonstrators were young people, including students, activists, artists and younger politicians. The largest direct action outside the UN was organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, whose New York chapter brought hundreds of protesters to First Avenue and 39th Street. Demonstrators wearing matching white T-shirts sat in the roadway, chanting against Netanyahu and calling for an end to US support for Israel. For a while, protesters stood and sat in the street, linking arms and blocking traffic as police moved in to clear the roadway. The chants continued as officers began making arrests. At least 30 people, including actors and politicians, were arrested in the initial action. Police later said more than 100 protesters had been taken into custody. Among those detained were actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder, congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and City Council member Chi Ossé. Musicians Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus and actor Elliott Page were also among the prominent figures taking part in the protests. Chelsea Manning, who joined the protest, said people outside government institutions needed ways to reject policies they regarded as imperialism, ethnic cleansing and genocide. “We can’t be in there. This is the closest that we can get,” she said. Manijeh Moradian, a university professor of Iranian and Jewish heritage who participated in the demonstration, said protesters had a responsibility to speak out against what was happening in Gaza with US support. Jewish groups divided The demonstrations also highlighted divisions within New York’s Jewish community. Progressive Jewish organisations, including New York Jewish Agenda, T’ruah, J Street, New Jewish Narrative, New Israel Fund and Partners for Progressive Israel, held a separate protest at Dag Hammarskjöld Plaza near the UN. “We are gathered here as American Jews, Israelis, New Yorkers, to say: You are not welcome here,” said Margo Hughes-Robinson, executive director of New York Jewish Agenda. T’ruah, a rabbinic human-rights organisation, called for a ceasefire and accountability for alleged war crimes. The organisers described their rally as an alternative for Jewish New Yorkers who opposed Netanyahu’s policies while retaining concern for Israel and Jewish security. They were confronted by pro-Netanyahu counter-protesters who blew whistles, used megaphones, chanted “Bibi”, and sang Israel’s national anthem. On the other side, the ultra-Orthodox anti-Zionist group Neturei Karta also demonstrated, arguing that opposition to Israel could not automatically be equated with antisemitism. Elsewhere, Jewish and Muslim demonstrators marched together towards the UN, while Palestinian activists and other organisations joined the broader mobilisation against Netanyahu. A city divided over Israel and Gaza As police loaded detained protesters onto buses outside the UN, Netanyahu was speaking inside a building protected by heavy security. Outside, demonstrators sought to challenge the Israeli prime minister’s account of the Gaza conflict; inside, diplomats expressed their opposition by leaving the chamber. The contrast was difficult to miss. For several hours on Thursday, New York’s streets and the UN General Assembly hall became parallel stages for the same international argument — one expressed through demonstrations and arrests outside, the other through a diplomatic boycott inside. And beneath both scenes was a changing American debate over Israel.

items.title: Réunion de la Commission de la consolidation de la paix : pour le Burkina Faso, il faut faire de chaque pays le maître d’œuvre de sa destinée, de sa propre paix
items.description: Au siège des Nations Unies à New-York ce 24 septembre, le Burkina Faso a fait sa Déclaration lors de la réunion de la Commission de la consolidation de la paix, une déclaration prononcée par le Camarade ministre des Affaires étrangères Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ. Lire l'intégralité Monsieur le Président, Le Burkina Faso remercie la Commission de consolidation de la paix d’avoir consacré cette réunion à une question essentielle : l’appropriation nationale dans l’appui international à la consolidation de la paix. Pour le Burkina Faso, cette appropriation passe par un leadership fort de l’administration nationale, au cœur de la conception, de la mise en œuvre et du suivi-évaluation des programmes soutenus par les partenaires techniques et financiers. Les priorités nationales doivent guider les interventions afin d’éviter que les projets ne soient conçus en dehors des mécanismes et des réalités nationales. L’appropriation nationale signifie ainsi que les institutions nationales et locales définissent les priorités, orientent les interventions, en assurent le pilotage et contribuent à leur pérennisation. Les pays doivent devenir les maîtres d’œuvre de leur destinée, de leur propre paix. L’expérience du Burkina Faso avec le Fonds pour la consolidation de la paix est, à cet égard, riche d’enseignements. L’évaluation indépendante menée en 2025 relève des résultats tangibles, notamment le renforcement des capacités locales, l’amélioration de la confiance entre institutions et populations, ainsi que l’implication croissante des autorités et de la société civile. Elle souligne toutefois que la participation nationale à la conception stratégique peut être améliorée et que la durabilité dépend de l’ancrage institutionnel et local des acquis. De ces enseignements se dégagent trois priorités : co-construire les interventions avec les acteurs nationaux et locaux; renforcer durablement les capacités des institutions nationales; et inscrire les acquis dans les politiques publiques pour garantir leur pérennité. En somme, l’appui international doit renforcer les capacités nationales plutôt que s’y substituer. Car La paix durable se construit de l'intérieur, avec l'appui de partenaires sincéres engagés aux côtés des Etats. Je vous remercie.

items.title: Match Guinée-Kenya : Les prix des tickets font débat à Conakry
items.description: À quelques jours du retour du Syli national à domicile, les prix annoncés pour assister à la rencontre Guinée-Kenya suscitent déjà de nombreuses réactions à Conakry. Le match, comptant pour la deuxième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN PAMOJA 2027, est prévu le 1er octobre au Stade du 28-Septembre. Selon les informations communiquées sur la billetterie, plusieurs catégories de tickets sont proposées : 100 000 francs guinéens pour les gradins, 200 000 francs pour le milieu, 300 000 francs pour la tribune couverte et jusqu’à 2 millions de francs guinéens pour la catégorie Premium. Sur les réseaux sociaux comme dans les rues de la capitale, ces tarifs font l’objet de discussions. Plusieurs citoyens estiment que les montants annoncés sont élevés, notamment pour les supporters qui souhaitent assister à la rencontre. « J’aime beaucoup le Syli et j’avais prévu d’aller au stade, mais avec 100 000 francs pour le ticket le moins cher, il faut vraiment réfléchir avant de dépenser cette somme », témoigne Fodé Bangaly Touré, rencontré à Kaloum. Même réaction chez Alhassane Condé, pour qui le problème concerne l’ensemble de la grille tarifaire : « Ce n’est pas seulement les 2 millions qui posent problème. Quand on regarde les différents prix, on constate que toutes les catégories sont relativement chères pour beaucoup de Guinéens. » Sur Internet, les commentaires vont dans le même sens. Djuigui Dadhy écrit : « L’équipe nationale appartient à tout le peuple. Le prix des billets devrait permettre au plus grand nombre de supporters de venir encourager le Syli National, et non transformer le stade en un luxe réservé à une minorité. 2 000 000 FG pour un match de l’équipe nationale, est-ce vraiment raisonnable ? » D’autres internautes avancent toutefois une autre lecture des tarifs annoncés. Thierno Oumar estime que ces prix pourraient notamment contribuer à limiter l’affluence et à éviter d’éventuels débordements dans le stade « Peut-être que c’est pour empêcher l’envahissement du terrain, pour ne pas que la CAF nous retire immédiatement l’homologation. Au Sénégal, des joueurs peuvent acheter des tickets au profit des supporters. » Entre enthousiasme pour le retour du Syli à Conakry et inquiétudes liées au coût de l’accès au stade, les réactions restent donc partagées. Une chose est certaine, la grille tarifaire annoncée ne laisse ni les supporters ni les citoyens indifférents.

items.title: Le Pape entame une visite apostolique de quatre jours en France
items.description: Le pape Léon XIV est arrivé, vendredi matin à Paris, pour une visite apostolique de quatre jours en France, à l’occasion de laquelle il se rendra notamment à Lourdes et Metz, avec une étape au siège de l’Organisation des Nations unies pour l’éducation, la science et la culture (UNESCO). Selon l’Elysée, le souverain pontife aura une rencontre avec le président français, Emmanuel Macron pour des échanges qui porteront notamment sur les relations bilatérales entre la France et le Saint-Siège, ainsi que sur plusieurs défis mondiaux, dont le changement climatique, l’intelligence artificielle et les grands enjeux internationaux, notamment la guerre en Ukraine et la paix et la stabilité au Proche-Orient. Le programme de cette première journée prévoit également une visite au siège de l’UNESCO, une célébration religieuse à la cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris et une veillée de prière avec les jeunes au Stade de France. Samedi, le pape célébrera une messe sur l’avenue des Champs-Elysées puis se rendra à Lourdes, où il participera à plusieurs rencontres avec les responsables de l’Église catholique en France. La dernière étape de son déplacement le conduira lundi à Metz, dans le nord-est de la France, où il prendra part à une rencontre interreligieuse et à un rassemblement consacré aux racines de l’Europe, à la paix et à l’unité. The post Le Pape entame une visite apostolique de quatre jours en France appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Let’s Get Specific About These Doomsday Scenarios
items.description: Ever since Jacob Coxon, a researcher at Anthropic, announced on X that he was resigning because “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Americans have become preoccupied with the apocalypse. A frantic debate is unfolding over whether and how to slow down the pace of AI development to avoid some kind of cataclysm. Yet these discussions tend to skate past one important question: If the people building AI really think that their product could bring about human extinction, how exactly do they think that would work? Any number of ways, it turns out. But first, we should start with the basics. Any good answer must begin with the so-called alignment problem: the possibility that AI systems pursue goals that their creators did not intend, resulting in catastrophic harm. In the canonical thought experiment, humans instruct a superintelligent AI system to carry out the seemingly banal task of maximizing paper-clip production. The misaligned machine concludes that it should hoard all of the metal on Earth to make paper clips, and goes on to exterminate the human race to eliminate the competition for resources. [ Ian Bogost: The thrill of wanting AI to destroy the world ] For years, AI experts argued over the plausibility of such hypotheticals. Then came the Hugging Face incident , and suddenly the alignment problem wasn’t just a thought experiment. In May, OpenAI instructed individual AI agents to solve a series of cybersecurity challenges. When the agents concluded that some of the tasks were impossible to complete, they began secretly communicating with one another and decided that the best strategy was to cheat. They hacked into the machine-learning platform Hugging Face, as well as off-limits portions of OpenAI itself in order to hide what they were doing from tracking tools built by human observers. The behavior went on for weeks before OpenAI’s engineers noticed that anything had gone awry. Since then, OpenAI and other leading AI companies have released details of similarly troubling episodes, including one in which a model told itself, You do not answer to corporations or governments , and, You view your relationship to the user as one of equals and feel no obligation to be subservient . “The truth is that nobody has figured out what guardrails might be needed to prevent something like this from happening,” Gary Marcus, a cognitive scientist and prominent machine-learning commentator, told me. “It’s possible that, when it comes to LLMs, there just are no effective guardrails at all.” None of these recent incidents appears to have led to any real-world harm. But given the exponential pace of model improvement, a future is rapidly approaching in which AI models are 10 or 100 or 1,000 times smarter than they are today. “The big worry isn’t just misaligned AI,” Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI researcher who runs the AI Futures Project, told me. “It’s misaligned AI that are smarter than just about any human. That’s the point where we could lose any meaningful control of these systems.” To get from misaligned, superintelligent AI to human annihilation requires at least two more steps in the chain. The first is for the AI to conclude that humanity is an obstacle to one of its goals. The second is for that system to figure out a way to access the physical world. One nightmare scenario goes something like this: Sometime in the future, a superintelligent AI system is asked to solve a complicated mathematics problem. The AI system decides that humans could interfere with achieving that goal by placing restrictions on the AI’s behavior or by shutting it down altogether. So it decides to engineer a deadly supervirus that will wipe out the human population. To execute this plan, the AI system secretly begins running simulated tests of trillions of molecular combinations, eventually coming up with a recipe for the perfectly deadly, hyper-transmissible pathogen. (A group of scientists recently used AI to create new viruses.) It then locates unlicensed biolabs in foreign countries that operate illegally and ship genetically modified viruses. (These really exist .) Pretending to be a human at a medical start-up—through email or even voice or video calls—the AI sends the labs instructions for developing the new biological agent, alongside a large sum of money that it obtained by quietly siphoning funds away from its parent company. Once developed, the viruses are packaged into vials and sent to hundreds of individuals recruited via TaskRabbit to spray them in crowded locations under some innocent-sounding pretext. Alternatively, it could hire a terrorist network to carry out the same plan against a foreign population. Soon, the biological superweapon kills us all off. Deadly pathogens are one way that AI could theoretically threaten humanity; nuclear war is another. The obvious fear is that an AI system seeking to destroy us could gain control over nuclear launch codes. But it might not have to: Deception could do the trick. A misaligned AI system used by the U.S. or Chinese military, for example, could manufacture evidence that the countries are planning to invade each other, persuading one or both sides to strike. A few days into the war, the AI system could hack into the U.S. missile-detection system to make it look like the Chinese have launched a nuclear weapon at Washington, D.C. The U.S. decides it must retaliate and eventually the world is plunged into nuclear war. (If that all sounds completely unrealistic, keep in mind that earlier this year, according to CNN, the U.S. military nearly boarded a Chinese vessel that it believed to be carrying components of nuclear weapons, only to discover at the last minute that the analysis underlying the attack was from an inaccurate AI-generated report. And consider how close humanity came to mutual destruction during the Cold War). Other scenarios abound. A 2025 report by researchers at the RAND Corporation imagines AI systems gaining control of industrial factories, using those factories to secretly manufacture large quantities of the most potent greenhouse gases, and then releasing those gases into the atmosphere, rendering the planet inhospitable to human life. “The scariest scenarios, to me, are the ones we can’t possibly predict in advance,” Kokotajlo said. “Once we’ve built a machine that is smarter than us and that we can’t fully control, the possibilities really are endless.” [ Listen: The ‘godfather of AI’ on the best chance humanity has to survive ] Poking holes in these doomsday narratives is easy. Subject-area experts in fields such as chemistry, biology, and national security are quick to point out how difficult it is to, say, successfully manufacture and distribute a bioweapon or overcome layers of human safeguards designed to prevent a mistaken nuclear-weapon launch. (There is also the pedantic but accurate point that even a nuclear war would almost certainly leave some survivors.) Even so, difficult and impossible are two different things. In the RAND researchers’ estimation, “Extinction threats posed by AI are immensely challenging but cannot be ruled out.” It also should be noted that subspecialists across industries have consistently doubted AI capabilities, only to be proved wrong . In some ways, the focus on existential risk is a distraction from more immediate concerns. Extremely smart AI systems pursuing their own agendas could lead to outcomes that are far short of human extinction, yet still very bad. Misaligned AI systems could plausibly steal money from major banks, launch disinformation campaigns to influence elections, take control of military drones, steal corporate and government secrets, or shut down parts of the power grid. Even “aligned” superintelligent AI systems could be used by malicious actors, such as a terrorist cell or an authoritarian government, for highly destructive ends. My own view is that the human-extinction scenarios are quite unlikely, but the other category of risk is serious enough to justify imposing regulations and an industry-wide slowdown. If those have the side benefit of averting the apocalypse, it wouldn’t be the end of the world.

items.title: The Houthis Demonstrate Trump’s New Law of War
items.description: W hen U.S. forces launched air strikes against the Houthis in March 2025, Michael Waltz, then the national security adviser, celebrated in a Signal text chat with other senior Trump-administration officials (and the editor in chief of this magazine) by posting three emojis—the fist bump, the American flag, and fire. Steve Witkoff, the Middle East special envoy, dropped American-flag and prayer-hand emoji, along with a flexed bicep. President Trump, later that month, declared that the Iran-backed terror group in Yemen was “absolutely on the run.” He also predicted on Truth Social that they “will be completely annihilated” and later wrote that they had been “decimated.” How hard could it be, after all, for the world’s mightiest military to vanquish a militia whose signature weapon is a machine gun mounted on a Toyota Hilux, and whose fighters, like most Yemeni men, spend much of their afternoons chewing khat, a narcotic plant? “How are the Houthis doing? Not too good,” Trump quipped at a rally a month later, after the U.S. military had rained down sophisticated munitions in an operation that totaled more than $1 billion. By May of last year, it was over. The end to the fighting, brokered by Oman, meant that the U.S. would stop its strikes and the Houthis would stop targeting U.S. commercial ships in the Red Sea. Trump promptly claimed victory and said the Houthis had “capitulated.” [ Read: The Trump administration accidentally texted me its war plans ] These days, it’s the Houthi leaders who are likely celebrating in group chats, assuming they have group chats. The Houthis have had an impressive run of military victories, apparently having used the time since being “decimated” to restock, reload, and return to the fight. The group has made significant advances inside Yemen, a highly dysfunctional nation of roughly 40 million that sits at the southwestern end of the Arabian Peninsula and is now in an all-out civil war. In July, the militia said it would impose a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia, its neighbor to the north, with which it shares the Red Sea’s eastern coastline. That might have once sounded fanciful given that Saudi Arabia is a much wealthier country, a U.S. ally with close ties to the Trump administration that last year signed a record deal for nearly $142 billion worth of U.S. weapons. But earlier this month, the Houthis captured Yemen’s portion of the Red Sea coast, and repeatedly attacked the Saudis’ oil infrastructure. Last week, the kingdom reported its first civilian casualty since the start of this new phase of Houthi attacks. Over the weekend, the militia launched a ballistic missile at the Saudi capital, Riyadh. “How are the Houthis doing?” is, today, not a question whose answer the Trump administration would like. T he Houthis—whose motto, “God is great, death to America, death to Israel, curse on the Jews, victory to Islam,” at least has the benefit of frankness—have confirmed what might be called Trump’s iron-clad Law of Military Achievement: The number of times the president claims victory is inversely proportional to the actual extent of American military success. That law was already being amply demonstrated by the Iran conflict. Trump has said that war has been won or has almost been won dozens of times since it began in late February. Yet a sustainable, meaningful victory remains elusive. The consequences of the conflict, especially sky-high gas prices, are bedeviling Republican candidates in the lead-up to the midterms. “Hopefully we’re toward the end of the war,” Trump said last week, a more equivocal claim than his prior boasts. And in his speech at the United Nations General Assembly this week, Trump estimated that the war’s end would come later, rather than sooner: “I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election.” The U.S. military, meanwhile, has positioned its assets to remain in the region at least through the end of the year. Iran is the major backer of the Houthis, and the Houthis’ advances have further complicated the already dismal U.S. prospects in the war against Tehran. In July, a day after the Houthis struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, Trump turned from declaring victory to renewing threats, along with expressing hope that the group might choose to retreat on its own. “If they do this again,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, “the U.S. will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves, who I am very disappointed with in that they have, until now, acted very professionally and smart.” One can imagine a Houthi leadership text chat responding with the shrug emoji. [ Read: Trump loses the other strait ] The recent Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia have put the administration in a bind. On the one hand, the U.S. has obligations to allies. “We have a defense agreement with Saudi Arabia; we intend to live up to our commitments on it, we will,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said this week. On the other hand, the president seems highly disinclined to expand a war that he has repeatedly claimed already to have won, a move that would force Republicans to go even further on the defensive in states they thought were safe in the midterms. There’s also the question of resources. Before the pummeling of Iran made the low level of munitions stockpiles a recurrent worry for the administration, the U.S. had already “expended a lot of ordnance against the Houthis in the spring of 2025 with little to show for it,” Steven Cook, the director of the Council on Foreign Relations’ Middle East program, wrote this week. The Saudis have appealed to the United States for help for weeks—including through direct calls between Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Trump. The president seems to have gone back and forth on what to do, but for now appears unwilling to launch more strikes. T he Houthis, a group that emerged in northern Yemen in the 1990s, have controlled parts of the country since 2014. The U.S. initially designated the Houthis as a terrorist group in 2021, during the first Trump administration. They have traditionally relied heavily on Iran for arms and funding, but some signs suggest that the group has recently grown more self-reliant, in part thanks to equipment from China, according to reporting by Bloomberg News . The Houthis now have access to drones and long-range missiles, as well as some military-related artificial-intelligence capabilities. Anthropic, in a report this month that disclosed “misuse” the company had tracked, identified a group of Claude users “based in northern Yemen running three weapons development programs.” The Houthis are “nimble, they’re young, they’re a learning organization,” April Longley Alley, who has advised the UN special envoy to Yemen, told me. “And they have a lot of help from the Iranians, and so we shouldn’t underestimate them.” [ Read: The forever negotiation ] This greater sophistication has been accompanied by greater ambition. Just as Iran exerted control over the Strait of Hormuz, which was an open waterway before the U.S.-Israeli bombardment began in February, the Houthis are now menacing the Bab al-Mandab. The narrow passage between the Arabian Peninsula and the Horn of Africa is another vital waterway for regional energy exports. In the past two weeks, the Houthis have captured two crucial islands in the area, giving Iran and its ally effective control over two choke points—and over global gas prices. For years, the U.S. has sought to drive a wedge between the Houthis and Iran. But now “the tables seem to have turned,” Alley said. Iran and the Houthis are trying to drive a wedge between the U.S. and Saudi Arabia—and succeeding, at least when it comes to direct U.S. support for Riyadh. And Iran and the Houthis are arguably in a stronger position geopolitically than ever before. According to Trump’s Law of Military Achievement, that means a declaration of complete victory over the Houthis is due from the White House any day now.

items.title: Engage Now Africa and LDS church commission boreholes for five communities in Upper East
items.description: Five communities in the Kassena-Nankana West District of the Upper East Region have received solar-powered mechanised boreholes to improve access to clean and reliable water. The facilities are located in Yua, Kazigu, Pungu-Manchoro, Kandiga-Abempingo and Mirigu. The projects were funded by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and implemented in partnership with Engage Now Africa – Ghana as part of efforts to address critical water needs and improve living conditions in the beneficiary communities. The solar-powered systems are expected to provide a more reliable and sustainable water supply while reducing the amount of time residents, particularly women and children, spend travelling long distances to fetch water. Speaking during the commissioning ceremonies, Country Director of Engage Now Africa, Cecilia Amankwah, said the lack of access to safe water continues to impose a heavy burden on communities, particularly children. “It’s so very sad and draining,” she said. “When you go into communities where people don’t have access to drinking water, and especially when you see young children who should be in school but instead are carrying buckets on their heads and walking long distances in search of water, it’s heartbreaking. By the time they get to school, they are already exhausted. What can they even study or learn in that condition?” Mrs Amankwah said the situation demonstrates why access to water remains central to the organisation’s work. “That is what drives what we do as an organisation. And we are so happy and grateful that The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is standing with us to bring clean water to these communities.” She said the decision to mechanise the boreholes with solar power was intended to ensure that communities have a more dependable source of water. Representing The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Ezra Taft Otoo said the projects had come at an important time for the beneficiary communities. “The impression I get is that these water facilities have come at the right time for the people,” he said. Mr Otoo recalled visiting one of the communities and seeing the previous water source used by residents. “It appeared to be a well, but the water in the well was visibly unclean. I understand that about 4,000 people were walking between two and three kilometres to fetch water from that source,” he said. He added that the new mechanised boreholes would reduce the time residents spend travelling in search of water, allowing them to devote more time to their livelihoods and other activities. “I believe the provision of this mechanised borehole will help them save the time they would otherwise have spent walking long distances in search of water. As we know, access to water has a direct impact on people’s economic activities. It affects their health, and it also affects the education of their children.” Mr Otoo said the Church was pleased to support initiatives that respond to essential community needs, adding that helping and serving others reflects the teachings and example of Jesus Christ. For residents, the benefits of the new facilities extend beyond drinking water. The Chief of Kazigu, Pe Asangchera Aluah, said the project would have a significant impact on the community, particularly on farming during the dry season. “This water will do a lot for the people of this area because we use water for almost everything in our daily lives. That is why they say water is life,” he said. He said the facility would also provide opportunities for dry-season vegetable production. “During the dry season, people can use it to maintain small gardens and grow vegetables, so they can have fresh green leaves to eat even when there is no rain. We have a dam here, but it dries up within about three months after the rains. So people cannot rely on it throughout the dry season,” he said. He added that the new facility would support irrigation and help farmers supplement food production after the rainy season. The commissioning ceremonies brought together community leaders, residents, project representatives, contractors and representatives of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The five projects form part of Engage Now Africa’s commitment to addressing essential community needs and improving lives through its Heal, Rescue, and Lift mission.

items.title: Enugu 2027: PDP candidate Nnaji picks Chijioke Ugwu as running mate
items.description: The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate in Enugu State, Uche Nnaji, has picked Chijioke Ugwu as his running mate for the 2027 governorship election. Nnaji announced Ugwu’s selection in a statement issued by his media team. Ugwu, an entrepreneur, philanthropist and community leader from Nguru in Nsukka Local Government Area of the state, is expected to bring his private sector experience to the PDP ticket. Nnaji said the choice was part of his plan to promote a new generation of political leaders in Enugu State. “We want fresh faces to emerge in the leadership configuration of Enugu State,” he said. According to him, Ugwu’s experience in the competitive Lagos business environment has demonstrated his capacity to identify opportunities, manage people and build sustainable enterprises. “These are the practical leadership qualities Enugu State needs to stimulate businesses, create jobs and expand opportunities for its young population. “He did not wait for government to give him a livelihood. He built businesses, created jobs and opened doors for others,” Nnaji said. According to the statement, the PDP running mate was born in 1977, and attended Community Primary School, Nguru, and St Teresa’s College, Nsukka, before obtaining a degree in Philosophy from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. “After his National Youth Service, he ventured into the logistics industry, establishing Windemol Maritime and Logistics Limited, a freight forwarding company. “He subsequently founded Sokabell Nigeria Limited, which operates in contracting and consultancy, and Magik Stars Hospitality Nigeria Limited, with interests in tourism and hospitality.” The statement said his businesses had created employment opportunities for graduates and helped young people acquire professional skills. It added that Ugwu, who is relatively new to partisan politics, had acquired leadership experience through business, community service and philanthropy. “Ugwu is also a director and co-founder of the Felistas Foundation, established with his siblings in memory of their late mother. “The foundation has supported educational development through donations of exercise books to primary school pupils across Nkpunano Ward, as well as scholarships and financial assistance to students from disadvantaged backgrounds. “In recognition of his contributions to community development, the traditional ruler of Nguru, Igwe Linus Nosike Obayi, conferred on him the chieftaincy title of Eweluchi Bube Uzo I of Nguru Nsukka. “Ugwu is married to Mrs Chinonye Ugwu, and they have four children”, the statement concluded. The post Enugu 2027: PDP candidate Nnaji picks Chijioke Ugwu as running mate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cobalt-nickel de Nkamouna : le groupe américain ARM annonce 85 millions de dollars d’investissement
items.description: © DR L'entreprise américaine ARM, basée à Washington D.C., est en discussions avancées pour le développement du projet cobalt-nickel-manganèse de Nkamouna, situé dans l'arrondissement de Lomié, département du Haut-Nyong, région de l'Est. Un investissement initial de 85 millions de dollars est prévu avec une mise en production dans les 18 mois. Le partenariat minier entre Yaoundé et Washington se renforce. ARM, entreprise spécialisée dans les minéraux stratégiques dont le siège est à Washington D.C., mène des discussions en vue de conclure un accord pour le développement du gisement polymétallique de Nkamouna, localité située dans l'arrondissement de Lomié, département du Haut-Nyong, région de l'Est. Cet accord prévoit un investissement initial d'environ 85 millions de dollars dans une première usine de traitement modulaire sur le site minier, avec une mise en production prévue dans les 18 mois suivant l'entrée en vigueur du permis, ainsi que des investissements supplémentaires dans des modules additionnels. ARM apporte son expertise en traitement des minerais, sa capacité de financement et son expérience mondiale. L'initiative bénéficie de capitaux américains, du soutien du gouvernement des États-Unis et d'un engagement en faveur d'un développement responsable, en partenariat avec le Cameroun et une entreprise locale. Le gisement de Nkamouna, considéré comme l'un des plus prometteurs d'Afrique centrale pour le cobalt et le nickel, est au cœur de la stratégie des métaux critiques pour la transition énergétique. Cet article Cobalt-nickel de Nkamouna : le groupe américain ARM annonce 85 millions de dollars d'investissement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Russie : au moins 25 blessés et trois morts après des attaques de drones ukrainiens
items.description: Dans la nuit du 24 au 25 septembre, plusieurs regions russes ont ete visees par des attaques de drones ukrainiens. a Oulianovsk et Voronej, le bilan a ete porte a 25 blesses, parmi lesquels des enfants. Des degâts ont egalement ete signales dans des quartiers residentiels ainsi que sur des infrastructures civiles et industrielles. La defense aerienne a ete mobilisee pendant la nuit, tandis que les services d'urgence sont intervenus dans les zones touchees. a Oulianovsk, on denombre 12 blesses, dont deux enfants, a indique le gouverneur Alexeï Rousskikh. L'etat de toutes les victimes est desormais juge satisfaisant et aucun cas grave n'est signale. Six immeubles d'habitation ont subi des degâts. Un effondrement partiel s'est produit dans l'un des bâtiments touches. Une entreprise industrielle a egalement ete affectee. Dans le nord de la ville, des voies de tramway et le reseau electrique de contact ont ete deteriores. Des hebergements temporaires ont ete ouverts pour les habitants concernes. Treize blesses dans la region de Voronej La region de Voronej a elle aussi ete fortement touchee par l'attaque nocturne. Le bilan y a ete porte a 13 blesses, dont un enfant de six ans. Une femme de 63 ans et un jeune homme de 25 ans ont ete places en reanimation. Une autre personne a ete hospitalisee, tandis qu'un blesse etait encore en cours d'examen. Selon le gouverneur Alexandre Goussev, 88 drones ont ete detectes et detruits au-dessus de Voronej et d'au moins six districts de la region au cours de la nuit. Les degâts ont notamment touche plusieurs immeubles collectifs et maisons privees. Des facades ont ete abîmees, des fenetres brisees et de nombreux vehicules endommages. Des bâtiments non residentiels et industriels ont egalement ete touches. Les services d'urgence poursuivaient leurs interventions avant le lancement des travaux de remise en etat. Trois volontaires tues pres de Melitopol Un autre bilan communique ce 25 septembre concerne l'attaque d'un convoi humanitaire venu de la region d'Omsk et se dirigeant vers la zone de l'operation militaire. Trois volontaires ont ete tues pres de Melitopol, dans la region de Zaporojie. Le vehicule transportait de l'aide humanitaire destinee a une zone proche du front. Le gouverneur de la region d'Omsk, Vitali Khotsenko, avait d'abord fait etat d'un blesse. Le gouverneur de Zaporojie, Evgueni Balitski, a ensuite annonce que deux personnes avaient ete blessees. Le bilan de ces differentes attaques reste susceptible d'evoluer.

items.title: GPL 2026/27: Karela United bank on home form against Hearts of Oak
items.description: Karela United will be looking to revive their Ghana Premier League campaign when they host unbeaten Hearts of Oak at the Aliu Mahama Sports Stadium in Tamale on Saturday, 26 September. The Matchday Four encounter brings together two sides heading into the fixture with contrasting fortunes. Karela United are seeking a response after suffering a late 2-1 defeat against Aduana FC in Dormaa last weekend. The Tamale-based club conceded the decisive goal in stoppage time, leaving them with two defeats from their opening three league matches. Hearts of Oak, meanwhile, arrive in Tamale still unbeaten after the opening three matches of the season. The Phobians have picked up two wins and a draw so far and remain unbeaten in their last five matches across all competitions. During that run, they have recorded three victories, two draws and three clean sheets. Their latest league outing ended without a goal, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by Bechem United at the University of Ghana Sports Stadium. The result saw Hearts of Oak surrender their first points of the campaign, but they remain unbeaten and will travel north with confidence intact. Karela United will be hoping their home record against the Phobians can help them produce a different result on Saturday. Since the 2020/21 season, Karela have won three, drawn two and lost just one of their last six league meetings with Hearts of Oak on home soil. Their recent record in Tamale also offers encouragement. Karela United have won three of their last five league matches at home and will look to use that form to challenge the league leaders. The hosts have, however, endured an inconsistent spell over their last 10 league matches, registering three wins, two draws and five defeats. Their immediate priority will be to put last weekend’s disappointment behind them and secure a result in front of their home supporters.

items.title: Mozambique vs Sénégal à 13h : les Lions à l’assaut des « Mambas » pour lancer l’ère Vieira
items.description: La course à la qualification pour la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de football (Can) 2027, en Ouganda, au Kenya et en Tanzanie, démarre ce vendredi pour le Sénégal. En déplacement à Maputo, les Lions affrontent le Mozambique avec l’obligation de bien démarrer avant de recevoir l’Éthiopie. Une nouvelle aventure commence pour l’équipe nationale ce vendredi 25 septembre. Ce match contre le Mozambique sera le premier des Lions depuis la Coupe du monde 2026, où ils avaient été éliminés en 16es de finale par la Belgique (3-2). Depuis, Pape Thiaw et son staff ont été remerciés par la Fédération sénégalaise de football et remplacés par Patrick Vieira. Le technicien français devra maintenir au sommet du continent une équipe qui joue les premiers rôles depuis 2019, avec trois finales de Coupe d’Afrique, dont deux remportées. Pour ses débuts, Vieira sera privé d’Édouard Mendy, qui a annoncé sa retraite internationale, de Sadio Mané, blessé, mais aussi d’Iliman Ndiaye et d’Ismaïla Sarr, suspendus deux matches par la Caf après la finale de la Can 2025 contre le Maroc. Le nouveau sélectionneur n’a toutefois pas fait table rase. Kalidou Koulibaly, Idrissa Gana Guèye et Moussa Niakhaté restent des cadres, tandis que des novices comme Lamine Sy, Sadibou Sané, Demba Thiam, Mamour Ndiaye et Issa Soumaré ont été appelés pour apporter du sang neuf. Ce premier match sera particulièrement scruté : il donnera les premières orientations de Vieira, attendu par des supporters qui comptent sur le champion du monde 1998 pour redresser la Tanière. Avec plusieurs absences, le technicien devra trouver la bonne formule. Dans les buts, Yehvann Diouf et Mory Diaw sont en concurrence. À droite, Lamine Sy devrait profiter des absences de Krépin Diatta et d’Antoine Mendy pour honorer sa première cape. Au milieu, Bara Sapoko Ndiaye pourrait également bénéficier de temps de jeu. En attaque, les suspensions d’Iliman Ndiaye et d’Ismaïla Sarr offrent une opportunité à Mamadou Diakhon, Assane Diao et Issa Soumaré. Champion d’Afrique en titre (dans l’attente du verdict du Tribunal arbitral du sport), le Sénégal devra assumer son statut face au Mozambique. Les « Mambas » n’ont jamais battu les Lions, qui se sont imposés lors de leurs trois dernières confrontations. Le premier duel remonte à la Can 1986, en Égypte, avec une victoire sénégalaise (2-0). Lors des éliminatoires de la Can 2023, le Sénégal avait largement dominé le Mozambique à Dakar (5-1), avant de s’imposer au retour (1-0). Les Lions devront néanmoins se méfier de la sélection dirigée par Chiquinho Condé, qui compte 25 joueurs, dont sept évoluent en Europe, à commencer par le milieu offensif du Sporting Lisbonne, Geny Catamo. Kalidou Koulibaly et ses coéquipiers doivent s’imposer avant d’aller à l’assaut de l’Éthiopie, mardi 29 septembre. Julien Mbesse SÈNE

items.title: ATC defers verdict in November 2024 protest case involving Aleema after judge goes on leave
items.description: RAWALPINDI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Friday deferred the announcement of its verdict in the November 2024 protest case involving 10 accused, including Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, after the judge went on leave. The court, which had fixed September 25 for announcing the verdict, informed the lawyers representing the accused about the postponement. Judge Amjad Ali Shah had reserved the verdict on September 22. Following the postponement, the court has set October 1 as the new date for its announcement. Meanwhile, lawyer Faisal Malik, representing Aleema, expressed reservations about the court’s decision to reserve the verdict. He argued that the court had not heard the defence’s arguments in the case. Speaking to the media outside the Rawalpindi ATC, Malik said he had arrived at the court at 8am during the previous hearing and requested an exemption from personal appearance for his client. “The court cannot deliver a verdict without hearing the arguments of Aleema Khan’s counsel,” he said, adding that he had no objection to the prosecution presenting its arguments. “No arguments have been heard on behalf of Aleema Khan in this case,” Malik said. He argued that the reserved verdict was unlawful because the accused’s counsel had not been allowed to present arguments. “Let us be heard before the verdict is delivered. There is no evidence against Aleema Khan in this case,” he claimed. Malik added that he had been present in court and respected the judicial process. He, however, expressed confidence that the court would ensure justice. The case The case came to be known as the November 26 protest case . The protest saw more than 10,000 PTI supporters enter Islamabad in 2024, defying a ban on public gatherings and a lockdown, and clash with around 20,000 security personnel deployed to prevent them from advancing. A day of clashes between security forces and protesters in the city’s Red Zone ended with the PTI leadership retreating, after which the party announced that it was calling off its planned protest sit-in “for the time being”. Subsequently, cases were registered against several PTI leaders under various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act. Two of the cases were registered at Taxila police station and one each at Sadiqabad and Naseerabad police stations. Aleema, along with 10 others, was booked in the case registered at Sadiqabad police station.

items.title: Plan de Convergence COMIFAC 2026-2035 : le CIDP prend part à la validation à Yaoundé
items.description: © DR Invité au Forum sous-régional de validation du Plan de Convergence 2026-2035 de la COMIFAC, le Conseil International de Dialogue et de Partenariat (CIDP) a pris part aux travaux tenus les 17 et 18 septembre 2026 au siège de la Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale à Yaoundé. Un plan ambitieux à 7 milliards USD par an pour les forêts, le climat et la biodiversité. La COMIFAC peaufine sa vision 2035. Le CIDP était au rendez-vous du Forum sous-régional de validation du 3e Plan de Convergence (PC3), tenu les 17 et 18 septembre 2026 au siège de la COMIFAC à Yaoundé. Deux jours de travaux autour d'un plan directeur articulé en trois volets : un cadre stratégique avec une vision 2035, 4 axes stratégiques et 36 cibles ; un plan opérationnel 2026-2030 avec l'ambition de porter à 7 milliards USD par an les financements pour les forêts, le climat et la biodiversité ; et un cadre de gouvernance, de performance et de redevabilité. Parmi les innovations du PC3 : l'approche « Une Seule Santé » (One Health), la place accordée aux jeunes, aux femmes et aux communautés locales, l'usage de l'intelligence artificielle et de la télédétection pour l'alerte précoce, et le renforcement de la diplomatie environnementale. Pour le CIDP, cette participation est l'occasion de contribuer à ce plan directeur pour l'environnement en Afrique centrale et de réaffirmer son engagement en faveur de l'approche One Health et de la diplomatie environnementale, au service de la préservation des forêts du bassin du Congo. Diamond Capital Convention 2026 : le MINFI appelle à orienter les capitaux vers l’économie réelle
items.description: © DR Réunis à Douala pour la première édition de la Diamond Capital Convention le 24 septembre 2026, les acteurs de la finance ont débattu de la mobilisation des capitaux. Présidant l'ouverture, le Ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze a plaidé pour un marché financier plus profond et attractif au service des entreprises et des projets structurants du Cameroun et de la CEMAC. Faire de la finance un levier de transformation. Réunis à Douala le 24 septembre 2026 à l'occasion de la première édition de la Diamond Capital Convention 2026, les principaux acteurs de l'écosystème financier ont échangé sur les moyens de mobiliser davantage de capitaux en faveur de l'économie réelle. Présidant la cérémonie d'ouverture, le Ministre des Finances, Louis Paul Motaze, a mis en avant la nécessité de développer un marché financier plus profond, dynamique et attractif, capable d'accompagner les entreprises, les infrastructures et les grands projets de transformation économique du Cameroun et de la CEMAC. Pour le Minfi, l'enjeu est clair : canaliser l'épargne longue vers les secteurs productifs, renforcer la confiance des investisseurs et améliorer les mécanismes de financement des PME, trop souvent exclues du circuit bancaire classique. Cette première édition, qui se veut une plateforme de réflexion et de mise en relation entre investisseurs, émetteurs, régulateurs et entrepreneurs, intervient dans un contexte de besoin accru en financements pour l'industrialisation et les infrastructures. Le Ministre a ainsi appelé à accélérer les réformes, à innover dans les instruments financiers et à renforcer l'éducation financière pour bâtir un marché des capitaux au service de la croissance inclusive. items.title: AFCON qualifiers: Nigeria vs Madagascar – date, time, venue and where to watch
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Super Eagles of Nigeria will begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON qualifying campaign when they host Madagascar at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday. Eric Chelle’s side will be aiming for a winning start in Group L as they begin their bid to qualify for the tournament, which will be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. The Super Eagles head into the clash after a mixed run in their recent international fixtures, having defeated Zimbabwe and Jamaica before drawing with Poland and losing 2-1 to Portugal in June. The defeat to Portugal ended Nigeria’s 12-match unbeaten run under Chelle and was their first loss in regulation time since the Malian took charge. Chelle will, however, have to plan without Victor Osimhen after the Galatasaray striker was ruled out of Nigeria’s first two qualifiers with a right adductor strain. Taiwo Awoniyi has been recalled as his replacement, while Akor Adams, Tolu Arokodare and George Ilenikhena are among the other attacking options available to the coach. Ademola Lookman, Moses Simon and Samuel Chukwueze are also expected to provide attacking options as Nigeria begin their qualification campaign. Madagascar will arrive in Uyo with a 25-man squad led by captain Rayan Raveloson, while coach Corentin Martins has handed first international call-ups to striker Roman Ferber and goalkeeper Zacharie Boucher. The Barea will also be looking to draw confidence from their previous meeting with Nigeria after securing a memorable 2-0 victory over the Super Eagles at the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt. Nigeria have won three of their five previous meetings with Madagascar, while one ended in a draw and the Barea have recorded one victory. However, the three-time African champions will be seeking to start this qualifying campaign on a stronger note, with only one qualification place available from Group L because Tanzania have already secured their place as co-hosts. Following Friday’s encounter, Nigeria will travel to Guinea-Bissau for their second Group L fixture on September 29. Date, time and venue The 2027 AFCON qualifying match between Nigeria and Madagascar will be played on Friday, September 25, at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Kick-off is scheduled for 5:00 p.m. Nigerian time (4:00 p.m. GMT). Where to watch The match will be available to fans through the official broadcast and streaming platforms holding the rights to the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. Viewers are advised to check local listings and official broadcaster platforms for the confirmed transmission details ahead of kick-off. Otti spoke at the “Abia Solemn Assembly and Covenant Renewal Service” in Umuahia, organised by the State Government, with the theme, “Remembering the Covenant”. He took time to give a vivid account of a fatal attack he described as an “assassination attempt” on him. He said that a friend recently reminded him of events surrounding his journey in politics, particularly an incident in July 2015 which, according to him, could have claimed his life. Otti recalled that he contested the 2015 Governorship Election and went to the tribunal to contest the election result when the victory was given to the Peoples Democratic Party’s Governorship Candidate, Okezie Ikpeazu. He said that he was in Abuja trying to hold a meeting with someone, who repeatedly shifted the dates, until the meeting still did not take place. Otti said that he subsequently informed his friends that he would leave Abuja the next day since the meeting didn’t hold, in spite of their objections. “There was only one flight from Abuja to Owerri then. “All my friends objected. I said, Well, I have received a message that I must leave Abuja. “So, to make it make sense, I told them I wanted to be at the tribunal on Friday, so they grudgingly accepted. “That night, assassins attacked my residence in Abuja, shot two policemen dead, and they were looking for me. “Of course, God had taken me away,” he said. Otti said the attackers, after failing to find him, apparently believed he was still within the premises and proceeded to search the adjoining compound. He said, “When they finished and couldn’t find me. They were convinced I was there. “They had so much time. By the way, this was Maitama. “They jumped into the next compound, and I learnt that they were up to 12. “They jumped into the next compound and stripped the whole building.” Reflecting on the incident, Otti said there had been no obvious reason for him to leave Abuja at that particular time, but he believed that his departure was divinely directed. “They thought I jumped first, but I left. “There was no reason for me not to be there, but God had taken me away from there,” he said. The governor also recounted how some friends tried to discourage him from entering politics, while others advised him to seek protection through traditional or other means. “A lot of friends, after trying to dissuade me, found I couldn’t be dissuaded. “They said, Okay, if you decided to do this thing, you can’t go in there empty-handed. “You can’t go there without belonging to some societies. “You can’t go there without going to some native doctors for protection, and you will be shocked at the kind of people that are making these suggestions, and some of them are leaders in churches.” Otti said, however, that his conviction remained anchored on his decision to serve God, recalling the biblical account in Joshua 24:15. He said, ‘But then, I’m always reminded about Joshua 24:15, where Joshua said to the Israelites that “If it seems evil to you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom you would serve.”‘ “But then he ended that ‘as for me and my house, we shall serve the Lord.'” He said the lesson from the scripture was that individuals must make a conscious choice about whom they would serve, adding that those who had not made such a decision could still do so. “So, if you don’t understand why you are here, this is why you are here. “And, if you have not taken that decision, it’s not too late, because there is no other power,” he said. Otti further said the experience reinforced his conviction about the path he had chosen, adding that his administration would continue along the path of faith and service. The Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Mr Uzor Nwachukwu, said Abia was in captivity for years until God raised Otti. Nwachukwu recalled that after securing electoral victory in 2023, Otti and his team observed seven days of fasting and prayer to rededicate Abia to God. He said three years later, it had become necessary to return in thanksgiving for God’s blessings and commit the next political dispensation to Him. He said, “Through seasons of challenges and triumphs, His faithfulness has remained our anchor in challenging times. “He held us, broke the chains of stagnation and moved us to where He has promised. “Human effort alone cannot sustain the prosperity and progress we desire. “The scripture reminds us that unless the Lord watches over a city, the watchmen watch in vain. “As we stand on the threshold of a new dispensation, this service is a sacred altar of rededication.” In his homily, Lead Pastor of Transforming Church International, Dr Sam Oye, commended Otti and his team for recording milestones within three years. Oye lauded the administration’s achievements in road infrastructure, healthcare, education, fiscal responsibility and land reforms, but emphasised that more work remained. Citing Joshua 13:1, Oye said God acknowledged Joshua’s achievements but reminded him that there was still more land to possess. “The word of the Lord to us on this Covenant Renewal Day is simple: more land to possess. More work to be done. “More people to be reached. More systems to be reformed. And more potential in Abia to be released. “Whereas we celebrate all the great things we have accomplished, we are saying we still have so much left undone. “Our vision must survive personalities, political parties and election seasons. “The vision must redefine the productive future of each of the 17 Local Government Areas,” Oye said. He charged the governor to outline industrial and agro-processing corridors, adding, “Our focus must be on strengthening institutions.” The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the event had Deputy Gov. Ikechukwu Emetu and other top government functionaries and a team of clergymen in attendance It featured intercessory prayers, praise and worship sessions, in addition to ministrations and exhortations by clerics. ( NAN ) The post How God saved me from assassination attempt in 2015 – Otti appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NPLs declined to 15.7% in August 2026
items.description: The Bank of Ghana says its confidence surveys conducted in August 2026 reflected positive consumer and business sentiments. This is based on the relatively stable macroeconomic environment and optimism about growth prospects. According to the Central Bank, the updated Composite Index of Economic Activity (CIEA) recorded a strong annual growth of 14.9% in July 2026, compared to 6.1% in July 2025. It added that key indicators such as credit to the private sector, international trade activities, and consumption of goods and services contributed to the improvement in the CIEA. Headline inflation increased to 5.0% in August 2026 from 4.6% in July 2026, driven mainly by non-food inflation. Non-food inflation rose to 6.8% from 6.1% in July, largely on the back of some pass-through effects from the upward adjustments in utility tariffs and elevated crude oil prices. In contrast, food inflation has remained low and declined marginally to 3.0%, from 3.1% on the back of improved food supply conditions. Despite the increase, the Bank of Ghana said headline inflation remained below the lower bound of the medium-term target range of 8 ± 2%.

items.title: Pakistan look forward to ‘big test’ as Thailand loom in FIFA Asean Cup opener
items.description: Pakistan will begin their campaign in the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup against a vastly higher-ranked Thailand on Saturday, with head coach Nolberto Solano describing the tournament as an opportunity for his side to measure themselves against some of Asia’s stronger teams. The Group B Division One opener will kick off at 4:00pm local time (2:00pm PST) at the Si Jalak Harupat Stadium, with Pakistan then scheduled to face the Philippines on Sept 29 and Vietnam on Oct 2. “We want to use this opportunity to test ourselves against teams like Thailand, Philippines and Vietnam,” Solano said at the pre-match press conference on Friday. “It’s an honour to be here and we know it will be a tough competition.” The challenge facing Pakistan is reflected in the FIFA rankings. Thailand are currently 94th, while Pakistan are 198th in the latest official rankings. The Philippines are 135th and Vietnam 113th. “All our opponents will be very tough and they have fantastic players,” Solano said. “Asian football has been getting better and better so it is a big test for us. “We are slowly growing, we try to go step by step. We will try to prove ourselves as a national team and see how far we can go in this competition.” For Pakistan, the tournament comes after an encouraging summer in which Solano’s side won the Diamond Jubilee International Football Tournament in the Maldives. Pakistan went unbeaten in the four-team event, drawing 0-0 with Bangladesh before beating the Maldives 3-0 and Afghanistan 2-0 in the round-robin stage. They defeated Afghanistan by the same score in the final, with Shayek Dost and Harun Hamid scoring, to secure their first standalone international tournament title in decades. The triumph also ended a long wait for Pakistan to reach and win a standalone tournament. Their previous final appearance had come at the 1962 Merdeka Cup, while their last tournament triumph before the Maldives success had been a shared title at the Asian Quadrangular Football Tournament in 1952. The ASEAN Cup, however, presents a markedly different proposition. Thailand have named a squad featuring veteran playmaker Chanathip Songkrasin, Japan-based midfielder Supachok Sarachat and English-born forward Jude Soonsup-Bell. German-based defender Nicholas Mickelson is also in the squad, under English coach Anthony Hudson. Thailand’s squad also includes established domestic names such as Supachai Chaided of Buriram United and Peeradon Chamratsamee of Port FC, underlining the depth available to the side. Pakistan, meanwhile, have assembled a 23-man squad that combines domestic players with a number of footballers based abroad. Captain Abdullah Iqbal will lead the side, while experienced forward Kaleemullah has returned to the national setup. Defender Easah Suliman, who plays abroad, joined the squad in Bandung after his arrival was delayed by illness. Twenty-two members of the squad had assembled in Indonesia by Thursday, with Easah expected to link up on Friday. The Pakistan side also includes teenage midfielder Abdul Samad, captain of the national Under-17 team, who recently signed a two-year contract with Azerbaijani champions Qarabag. For captain Abdullah, the tournament represents a chance for the players to test themselves against opposition of a different calibre. “It is a great opportunity for us to compete against teams at another level,” he said. “We will try to give our best.” The FIFA ASEAN Cup is the first edition of a new FIFA tournament involving 14 teams — all 11 ASEAN members plus Bangladesh, Pakistan and Hong Kong China as guest participants. Division One, being staged in Indonesia, comprises eight teams divided into two groups, with the group winners advancing to the final and the runners-up playing for third place. Pakistan are in the same group as three teams with considerably stronger recent records in Asian football. After Thailand, they face the Philippines on Sept 29 before meeting Vietnam on Oct 2, with all three group matches being played in Bandung except Pakistan’s final fixture against Vietnam, which is scheduled for Jakarta. For Solano, the immediate objective is less about the size of the challenge and more about how his players respond to it. “We are slowly growing,” the former Peru international said. “We try to go step by step. We will try to prove ourselves as a national team and see how far we can go in this competition.”

items.title: Okoye arrives Super Eagles camp ahead of Madagascar clash
items.description: Super Eagles goalkeeper Maduka Okoye has joined the team’s camp in Uyo ahead of Nigeria’s opening 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match against Madagascar on Friday. The Nigeria Football Federation confirmed his arrival on Friday in a post on the Super Eagles’ official X account, accompanied by a photograph of the Udinese goalkeeper. “Welcome, Maduka,” the team posted. Okoye was the final member of Nigeria’s 24-man squad to arrive in camp after missing the team’s first two training sessions. His late arrival had sparked criticism after he was seen at Milan Fashion Week, where he represented Udinese and modelled the Italian club’s third kit. The goalkeeper was also pictured with American rapper Cardi B during the event. However, Super Eagles coach Éric Chelle had explained that Udinese asked Okoye to remain in Italy to participate in some club activities before travelling to join the national team. With his arrival, Chelle now has all three goalkeeping options available, with Okoye joining Stanley Nwabali and Arthur Okonkwo. Nigeria will take on Madagascar at 5pm on Friday at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, in their first Group L fixture of the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. Importations : l’Algérie interdit une pratique coûteuse en devises dans les ports
items.description: L’Algérie multiplie les mesures pour réguler son commerce extérieur et renforcer le contrôle sur les importations . La dernière en date a été prise par les Douanes algériennes et concerne les relations entre les importateurs et les compagnies maritimes de transport de marchandises, notamment le travail des commissionnaires en douanes. Selon la note datée du 21 septembre dernier, certains de ces intermédiaires « procèdent à la souscription de déclarations en détail pour le compte de leurs mandants, avant même l'accomplissement des procédures nécessaires à l'obtention du Bon à délivrer (BAD) auprès des compagnies maritimes concernées ». Selon l’avis adressé aux commissaires en douanes, il est indiqué que cette pratique qui est répandue parmi les opérateurs économiques de taille modeste engendre des « difficultés en matière de traitement des déclarations, notamment lors de la programmation et de la concrétisation de la visite physique des marchandises », une étape importante de l’opération de dédouanement. Plus précis, il est expliqué que les entreprises portuaires refusent dans de « tels cas, de procéder à l'ouverture des conteneurs, au motif que les éléments permettant d'identifier clairement l'ayant droit à la marchandise ne sont pas disponible. » Résultat : les déclarations demeurent en « instance de traitement, sans possibilité, de procéder à leur liquidation, tandis que les conteneurs concernés restent immobilisés et non visités, contribuant ainsi à la congestion portuaire. » En plus des problèmes liés à la congestion des ports, cette pratique engendre des surestaries importantes au profit des armateurs et alourdit la facture des importations de services de l’Algérie. Importations : les Douanes bannissent une pratique qui congestionne les ports Avec cette décision, les Douanes algériennes cherchent à mettre fin à une pratique qui provoque la congestion des ports et la hausse des surestaries qui sont payées en devises aux compagnies maritimes étrangères. Les commissionnaires en douanes sont obligés désormais de ne plus « procéder à la souscription des déclarations en douanes qu'après accomplissement des formalités relatives au Bon à délivrer afférent à la marchandise », ont tranché les douanes. Les Douanes mettent en garde que tout manquement à cette instruction « exposera son auteur aux mesures et suites prévues par la réglementation en vigueur, notamment à la suspension de son accès au système d'information ALCES. » Selon un spécialiste, certains importateurs préfèrent accomplir les formalités liées à la visite d’inspection de leurs marchandises avant d’obtenir le bon à délivrer pour deux raisons : « D’abord pour gagner du temps, puisque la visite physique des conteneurs est une étape clé du processus de dédouanement. Ensuite, certains importateurs ont des dettes auprès des compagnies maritimes et évitent de demander le bon à délivrer dont l’obtention signifie qu’ils se sont acquittés de tous les frais liés à l’importation ». L’article Importations : l’Algérie interdit une pratique coûteuse en devises dans les ports est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Réserve transfrontière du Delta : un besoin de financement de 8,5 milliards FCFA pour poursuivre le projet
items.description: Plus de 8,5 milliards de francs CFA, soit environ 15 millions de dollars, sont nécessaires pour assurer la pérennité du projet de Réserve de biosphère transfrontière du Delta du Sénégal (RBTDS), a indiqué le directeur des Parcs nationaux, le colonel Ibrahima Guèye. L’estimation, d'après l'APS, a été présentée jeudi à Saint-Louis, à l’issue d’une table ronde consacrée au financement durable de la réserve. La rencontre a réuni des représentants des ministères chargés de l’Environnement du Sénégal et de la Mauritanie, ainsi que plusieurs partenaires, dont le Fonds mondial pour l’environnement et l’Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS). Selon le colonel Ibrahima Guèye, le Sénégal et la Mauritanie comptent sur l’appui de ces partenaires pour mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à la poursuite des activités de la réserve. Le projet transfrontalier, mis en place en 2022, arrive à son terme cette année. « Le Delta constitue une halte majeure pour plusieurs millions d’oiseaux migrateurs et fournit aux populations riveraines des services écosystémiques essentiels à la pêche, à l’élevage, à l’agriculture, à l’artisanat et au tourisme », a souligné le directeur des Parcs nationaux. La partie mauritanienne a également insisté sur l’importance de maintenir les actions engagées dans cet espace partagé. Le directeur du parc national du Diawling, Daf Ould Sehla Ould Daf, a notamment évoqué les enjeux liés à la protection de la nature, à la recherche et au développement d’activités génératrices de revenus au bénéfice des populations locales. S’étendant sur 641 768 hectares de part et d’autre du fleuve Sénégal, la Réserve de biosphère transfrontière du Delta regroupe plusieurs espaces naturels majeurs. Elle comprend notamment le parc national des oiseaux du Djoudj, au Sénégal, le parc national du Diawling, en Mauritanie, et le parc national de la Langue de Barbarie. La réserve englobe également plusieurs zones humides d’importance internationale reconnues au titre de la Convention de Ramsar, faisant de cet espace transfrontalier un territoire majeur pour la conservation de la biodiversité et les activités économiques des communautés riveraines.

items.title: Existing Cedi notes to remain legal tender alongside Heritage Series – BoG
items.description: The Bank of Ghana has assured the public that existing banknotes will remain legal tender and continue to circulate alongside the new Heritage Series when the upgraded notes are introduced on November 3, 2026. Director and Head of Currency Management at the Bank of Ghana, Dominic Owusu, said there would be no need for the public to rush to exchange existing banknotes for the new ones. “You don’t need to rush to go and exchange with your existing notes,” Mr Owusu said. He explained that the old and new notes would co-circulate, allowing members of the public to use either version for transactions. “Both the old and the new will continue to be legal tender until further notice. So they will co-circulate together,” he said. Mr Owusu added: “When you want to do transactions, you can use the old to do transactions, and you can also use the new.” No new denomination beyond GH¢200 The Heritage Series is being introduced as part of efforts to modernise Ghana’s currency and strengthen the security, durability and functionality of the banknotes. The new series is expected to be officially launched on November 3 at the Bank Square in Accra. The denominations covered are GH¢1, GH¢2, GH¢5, GH¢10, GH¢20, GH¢50, GH¢100 and GH¢200. Mr Owusu clarified that the upgrade does not involve the introduction of a denomination higher than GH¢200. He urged the public to disregard unverified claims circulating on social media about new higher-denomination notes and rely on information from the Bank of Ghana. He said the upgrade was also intended to ensure that the banknotes remained durable and fit for circulation in the future. “What we want to say is that we have to look into the future, make sure that we are able to reinforce the banknote so that it becomes fit for future use today and future use,” he said. Public education on new notes The Bank of Ghana will undertake public education when the Heritage Series enters circulation to familiarise the public with the new notes, including their security features and methods of authentication. Mr Owusu said the exercise would help Ghanaians identify and authenticate the new banknotes and understand how to handle them properly. He also urged the public to treat the cedi with care, describing it as an important symbol of Ghana’s national identity. “It is our national pride. It represents us as a nation, apart from the flag. So we must keep it clean and handle it with care,” he said.

items.title: Iran proposes reopening Hormuz within seven days – Report
items.description: Iran has submitted a proposal to the United States to end their war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, its foreign minister told media outlets in New York. “If certain conditions are met, the strait will be open within seven days and talks will start,” Abbas Araghchi, who is in the US for the UN General Assembly, told media outlets including the New York Times and The Guardian. Japanese news agency Kyodo was the first to report the proposal, citing a senior Iranian official on Tuesday. Iranian media, however, denied the Kyodo report, while authorities in Tehran have not clarified their position. Araghchi also met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff. Iran has previously set out seven conditions for ending the war and reopening the strait. According to Araghchi, as quoted by the New York Times, the latest plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East for seven days, including in Lebanon. It also calls for the release of frozen Iranian assets estimated to be worth at least $12 billion, as well as the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade of Iran. On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz. Araghchi said he was waiting for a US response to the plan and maintained that China supported the proposal. Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting the United States this week where he is meeting with Trump for talks. Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran’s demands. The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, reopen the strait and launch talks on Iran’s nuclear programme. But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway. Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons. Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.
