items.title: Ghana’s Liquidity Paradox: Why capital is not reaching productive businesses
items.description: Ghana has liquidity, institutions seeking returns and businesses seeking capital. The missing link is an effective system for converting savings into appropriately structured finance for investment-ready enterprises. Ghana’s financial system presents an important economic paradox. There is substantial liquidity in the system. Commercial banks are actively looking for credible opportunities to grow their loan portfolios, while pension funds, insurance companies, asset managers and collective investment schemes continue to mobilise savings. Yet many businesses still struggle to obtain the patient, affordable and appropriately structured capital required to expand production, acquire equipment, enter new markets and create employment. Meanwhile, significant amounts of money are held in deposits, invested in government securities or absorbed by the Bank of Ghana through its open-market operations. In September 2026, the central bank reportedly absorbed more than GH¢21 billion from the financial system in one week through 14-day Bank of Ghana bills at an annualised rate of approximately 10.5 percent. This is occurring at a time when year-on-year inflation stood at 5 percent in August 2026 and government Treasury-bill rates declined significantly. At its September 2026 meeting, the Bank of Ghana’s Monetary Policy Committee maintained the policy rate at 14 percent. Although the Ghana Reference Rate declined to 10.18 percent in September, the Bank of Ghana reported an average lending rate of 15.94 percent for August. The rate offered to an individual business may be higher or lower, depending on its risk profile and the terms of the facility. The situation raises an important question: If Ghana has liquidity, banks want to lend and investors are looking for attractive returns, why is the private sector not expanding in line with the capital available? Figure 1. Selected rates as at August-September 2026. The instruments have different maturities and policy purposes. Actual lending rates may exceed the GRR after risk premiums and charges. From my observation across banking, treasury and financial markets, the problem is not simply an absence of money. It is the absence of sufficient structures for moving available capital into businesses capable of using it productively. Ghana does not merely have a lending gap. It has a capital-allocation, business-readiness and financial-intermediation gap. Liquidity is not the same as productive capital Liquidity refers to the availability of funds within the financial system. Productive capital is funding that reaches a viable business in the right form, at an appropriate cost and for a period consistent with the purpose for which it is required. A business seeking short-term working capital may need an overdraft or revolving credit facility. A company purchasing machinery may require medium-term debt or leasing. A growing enterprise with irregular cash flows may need equity rather than a loan. A large, established company may be able to issue commercial paper or a corporate bond. The challenge is therefore not merely to make money available. It is to connect each credible business opportunity with the appropriate source and structure of capital. Banks want to lend but businesses must absorb the credit Commercial banks are an important part of this discussion. Many are actively searching for credible borrowers to grow their loan portfolios. However, banks cannot lend solely because they have liquidity or ambitious growth targets. Every loan must satisfy credit, profitability, capital and regulatory requirements. A bank must establish that the borrower can repay, that the proposed investment is commercially viable and that the associated risks can be managed. This explains why banks can be aggressively looking for lending opportunities while businesses simultaneously complain about inadequate access to credit. In practice, financial institutions may be competing for the same relatively small group of established corporates, multinational companies and well-structured local businesses. Many other enterprises remain outside the acceptable credit space because of inadequate financial information, uncertain cash flows, weak governance, insufficient collateral or high exposure to economic shocks. The real constraint is therefore not always the availability of credit. It is the availability of businesses capable of absorbing credit without becoming financially distressed. Why businesses struggle to absorb capital The cost of doing business remains high. A decline in inflation or Treasury-bill rates does not automatically make every expansion profitable. Companies continue to face costs associated with electricity, transport, imported inputs, taxation, regulatory compliance, technology and skilled labour. A manufacturer will not borrow merely because a bank has money available. It will borrow when management is confident that the company can produce competitively, sell the additional output and generate sufficient cash flow to service the facility. Where operating costs are high and demand is uncertain, businesses may rationally postpone expansion. Many businesses are also not investment-ready. Ghana has enterprises with viable products and committed founders, but many do not maintain reliable financial records, separate the owners’ finances from those of the company, or have audited accounts and effective governance structures. An entrepreneur may know that the business is profitable; unless that profitability can be independently demonstrated, a lender or investor may be unable to rely on it. The enabling environment remains another constraint. Businesses require reliable electricity, efficient logistics, predictable taxation, stable regulation, prompt payment for government contracts and an effective system for resolving commercial disputes. If the operating environment does not allow companies to produce competitively, increasing the supply of credit alone could result in excessive indebtedness rather than sustainable expansion. Not every business needs another loan One weakness in Ghana’s financing system is the tendency to treat bank credit as the primary solution to every business-financing problem. Some companies are already highly leveraged. Others have seasonal cash flows or require several years to complete an expansion before earning sufficient income. Such companies may require equity, quasi-equity or another form of patient capital. Consider an agro-processing company that has secured demand for its products but needs a new processing plant, additional working capital, storage facilities and distribution capacity. A bank could finance part of the working-capital requirement. Equipment could be acquired through leasing. A private-equity investor could finance part of the plant and strengthen the company’s governance. A development-finance institution could provide a guarantee, while export-finance facilities could support regional sales. Attempting to finance the entire expansion through a short-term bank loan would place unnecessary pressure on the company’s cash flow. Businesses need financing structures, not isolated financial products. The problem goes beyond commercial banks Responsibility for converting Ghana’s savings into productive investment cannot be placed entirely on banks. The country also has pension funds, insurance companies, asset managers, collective investment schemes, the Ghana Stock Exchange, venture-capital firms, private-equity funds, private-credit providers and development-finance institutions. Together, these institutions should provide a spectrum of capital suited to different stages of business development and different levels of risk. The broader question is therefore not simply why banks are not lending more. It is why Ghana’s entire financial system is not allocating more capital to productive private-sector opportunities. Pension funds and insurance companies control long-term pools of money that could support infrastructure, housing, agriculture, manufacturing and export-oriented businesses. These investments, however, require properly regulated and professionally managed vehicles that protect contributors while offering competitive risk-adjusted returns. Asset managers and collective investment schemes can aggregate savings and channel them into corporate securities. Yet Ghana’s corporate-bond and commercial-paper markets remain relatively shallow, limiting the number of private-sector instruments available to institutional investors. This creates a circular problem: investors see too few well-structured businesses, while businesses see too little patient capital to help them grow. The stock market and private capital must play a greater role The Ghana Stock Exchange should become a more important channel for mobilising long-term capital. Listing allows a business to raise equity without assuming fixed repayment obligations. It can also improve governance, transparency, visibility and access to future capital. Many Ghanaian businesses are reluctant to list because owners fear losing control, disclosing financial information or becoming accountable to external shareholders. Others may not yet meet the required governance and reporting standards. The solution is not merely to encourage businesses to list; it is to prepare them. The Ghana Stock Exchange, investment banks, accounting firms, business associations and government agencies could jointly identify promising enterprises and prepare them for private placements, corporate-bond issuance or eventual listing. Venture capital and private equity must also help fill the risk-capital gap. These investors can share commercial risk and support businesses in strengthening strategy, governance, reporting and operations. Private-credit funds can complement both banks and equity investors by providing flexible financing to viable businesses that may not satisfy standard bank-lending requirements. Connecting capital to the 24 Hour Economy The 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme seeks to increase production, deepen industrialisation, expand exports and create employment through more efficient use of Ghana’s productive capacity. A company moving from one shift to two or three shifts may require additional machinery, inventory, working capital, transport, storage facilities, technology and employees. These are precisely the productive activities that Ghana’s available liquidity should finance. However, operating additional shifts will be commercially beneficial only if the company has reliable electricity, adequate inputs, productive labour, efficient logistics and a market for its increased output. The programme should therefore be deliberately connected to the entire financial system. A qualifying company may require an overdraft for working capital, leasing for machinery, private equity for a factory expansion and trade-finance facilities to support exports. A larger project may require a corporate bond or infrastructure fund. No single financial institution can provide every component. AfCFTA provides the market but businesses must compete The African Continental Free Trade Area gives Ghanaian businesses potential access to a continental market of approximately 1.4 billion people with a combined gross domestic product of about US$3.4 trillion. This should fundamentally change how Ghanaian businesses assess market size and expansion opportunities. A company with a credible export contract or regional distribution agreement presents a stronger financing proposition than one seeking to expand without an identified market. However, market access on paper does not automatically translate into sales. Ghanaian companies must compete on price, quality, volume, standards and delivery time. They require certification, reliable transport, efficient customs procedures, market intelligence, cross-border payment systems and trade finance. The fact that the AfCFTA Secretariat is headquartered in Accra gives Ghana strategic visibility. But location alone will not create continental champions. Ghana must deliberately build businesses capable of producing at scale and serving regional markets. Three actions to close the gap First, Ghana should establish a coordinated national investment-readiness pipeline linked to the 24-Hour Economy and AfCFTA. Promising businesses should receive support to improve governance, financial reporting, operational systems and investment proposals before being connected to the most appropriate capital provider. Second, Ghana should develop more credit-enhancement and co-investment structures. Government and development-finance institutions can provide targeted guarantees, first-loss protection and risk-sharing facilities to crowd private capital into priority sectors. These arrangements must support commercially viable projects rather than replace proper investment appraisal. Third, the country should deepen its corporate capital markets and private-fund industry. Pension funds, insurers, asset managers, family offices and qualified investors should have access to properly regulated vehicles through which they can invest in diversified portfolios of corporate bonds, private credit, infrastructure, private equity and venture capital. From liquidity to productive transformation Ghana’s challenge is not simply that banks are failing to lend. Many banks want to grow their loan portfolios. Investors are searching for competitive returns, and businesses are looking for capital. What is missing is a sufficiently strong bridge connecting these pools of capital to enterprises capable of deploying them productively. The 24-Hour Economy can create opportunities for businesses to expand production and employment. AfCFTA can provide access to a much larger market. But these opportunities will generate economic transformation only when businesses are competitive, properly structured and supported by suitable forms of finance. The next stage of Ghana’s financial-sector development must move beyond asking whether money is available. We must ask whether businesses are prepared to absorb it, whether the operating environment allows them to invest it profitably and whether the financial instruments available are aligned with their actual needs. Ghana has capital. Banks have an appetite to lend. Institutional investors are mobilising long-term savings. Entrepreneurs have ideas, while government has introduced policies intended to stimulate production and exports. The task now is to connect these elements deliberately and convert financial liquidity into factories, technology, competitive businesses, exports and sustainable jobs. The writer, Ernestina Mensah, is a treasury, financial markets and risk-management professional with experience in banking, asset and liability management, market risk, business development and financial-sector strategy. The views expressed are personal. items.title: LHC seeks Punjab home secretary's reply on plea against Aleema's detention
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday sought a reply from the Punjab home secretary on a petition challenging the detention of PTI founder Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. Aleema was detained by authorities on Sept 20, after the office of Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days. The DC’s order cited a letter by the Lahore capital city police officer, which referred to police reports that Aleema and Ameer “are prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”. Justice Abher Gul Khan has been holding hearings on the petition. In the previous hearing, Justice Abher had sought arguments on the plea’s maintainability. As the hearing resumed on Friday, a Punjab government law officer asked the court to dispose of the petition, arguing that the home secretary had already fixed a hearing to review the detention order issued by the Lahore DC on Sept 28. The judge, however, issued a notice to the home secretary for submission of a reply to the petition. Barrister Taimur Malik submitted that his client, Aleema, was facing difficulties in receiving her medicines and other essentials in jail. The judge directed the counsel to file a separate application on this issue. Aleema’s detention took place amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. Shahraiz Khan, Aleema’s son, filed a petition through Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention orders issued by the Lahore DC against his mother and two aunts. Following Aleema’s detention, her two sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were also detained under MPO. A day earlier, the LHC turned down a request to immediately suspend the preventive detention notifications issued against Noreen and Dr Uzma. The petition contends that the DC unlawfully issued the detention orders and failed to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance. It further argues that the orders contain no specific allegations and demonstrate no application of mind. The petition also says that ordinary criminal law and less restrictive measures were not considered and contends that the grounds for detention were not communicated within the required period, alleging that the detention orders were issued after the arrests. It asks the court to set aside the detention orders issued by the Lahore DC and declare them unlawful.

items.title: After 50,000 km, British round-the-world walker faces final hurdle
items.description: After 28 years and 50,000 km, a British adventurer is facing one last hurdle in his bid to trek home from South America without using any form of transport — the Channel. “We thought we got permission to swim from the coast of France. Turned out that is not the case,” Karl Bushby, a former paratrooper, told AFP as he walked towards Cap Blanc-Nez in northern France, within sight of the white cliffs of the English coast. “There was some internal confusion. So, right now we’re scrambling in kind of semi-panicked state.” The 57-year-old had originally hoped to use a service corridor in the Channel Tunnel on foot, but he said the authorities seemed “set against” this idea. So he resigned himself to swimming from Calais, even though he “hates” it. “I say I swim like a cat dropped in a bathtub. It’s not funny. It’s bad. “But you just do what you’ve got to do,” he said. At an earlier stage of the journey he took 30 days to cross the Caspian Sea with a mixture of swimming and floating, resting — but not advancing — on a boat. He hopes to get permission to swim across the Channel, one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, before October 1, after which the winter weather would make the crossing too risky. When he set off in November 1998 , Bushby set himself two rules: not to use any form of transport to advance, and not to return home — near Hull in northern England — except on foot. As he travels he pushes a cart containing all his belongings, nicknamed “the Beast”. Over three decades, he has paused his journey several times. Moscow refused him a visa for a long time, unhappy that he had crossed the Bering Strait separating Alaska from far eastern Russia on foot — something he says no one had ever done before. Between them, visa woes, the 2008 financial crisis, and then the Covid-19 pandemic have accounted for about 14 of his 28 years on the road, he estimates. At those times, he stepped away from the journey, living notably in Mexico, then once the situation cleared, he would resume his journey at the exact spot where he had left off. As he nears England, Bushby looks back nostalgically on the very start of the adventure, on his trek up through the Andes and the difficult crossing of the Darien jungle between Colombia and Panama. “Then slowly but surely it becomes a job. You get older, it gets harder,” he said. Bushby is the subject of a documentary currently in preparation, and once the journey is complete he plans to devote himself to the film and to giving talks. “I’ve got to try and get established in the grown up world again, because I’m going to arrive home with nothing,” he said. But first there is the Channel to cross, and despite the challenge, Bushby is optimistic. “I think we can work it out. If not, I’m living in France for the rest of my life!” he said.

items.title: À quoi ressemble le quotidien d’une femme enceinte à Gaza?
items.description: Alors que la guerre à Gaza entame sa quatrième année, le journal britannique The Guardian a décidé de donner la parole à cinq Palestiniens ordinaires de Gaza pour raconter leur quotidien. Chacun raconte sa journée, révélant le terrible tribut imposé par le conflit qui se poursuit en dépit du cessez-le-feu du président américain Donald Trump. Parmi ces Palestiniens figure une femme qui a perdu ses trois enfants durant la guerre et qui a raconté sa nouvelle grossesse dans les terribles conditions endurées par la population gazaouie. Un témoignage précieux qui doit être connu par les personnes qui vivent cette époque et qui doit rester pour la postérité car la banalisation de la souffrance et l’oubli sont les meilleurs alliés de l’idéologie génocidaire sioniste. Imed Bahri Alaa Hessi gravit les marches avec précaution. Elle lève le pied pour le poser lourdement sur la marche supérieure, reprend son souffle et fait glisser sa main le long de la rampe. Posé sur un amas de décombres irrégulier, l’escalier en bois tremble à chacun de ses mouvements. Sa progression est ralentie par le volume imposant de son ventre de femme enceinte. Arrivée en haut, elle s’arrête pour reprendre son souffle puis s’avance sur la plateforme qui constituait autrefois l’étage de la maison familiale. Une tente est dressée là où se trouvait la maison. Sous ses pieds gisent les ruines du foyer où elle a élevé ses trois enfants: Waseem, 10 ans, Mohannad, 7 ans, et Khawla, 5 ans. C’est aussi là qu’ils ont péri, tous trois tués par une frappe aérienne israélienne qui a rasé la maison. Dans environ un mois*, Alaa donnera de nouveau la vie. Elle raconte sa journée… Au lever du jour Le bruit qui me réveille le matin, c’est le bourdonnement des mouches à l’intérieur de la tente et le vacarme de nos voisins. Dans les tentes, l’intimité est inexistante, tout comme la sécurité. Ici, tout le monde connaît les secrets des autres. Nous entendons les gens lorsqu’ils vont aux toilettes. Nous pouvons même les entendre respirer. La fenêtre de ma tente donne directement sur la ligne jaune**. D’ici, on aperçoit les positions de l’armée israélienne et il leur arrive de tirer sur nous. Mon mari et moi adorons boire du thé le matin mais le préparer est devenu un défi car Israël empêche le gaz d’entrer à Gaza et cette ressource est extrêmement rare. Nous dépendons toujours du bois de chauffage et des feux ouverts pour cuisiner et préparer des boissons chaudes. Ramasser du bois et allumer un feu suffit à m’épuiser. Après avoir bu mon thé, je range la tente et j’essaie de cuisiner le plus tôt possible, avant que le soleil ne devienne trop ardent. Je lave aussi à la main les vêtements de mon mari et les miens, une tâche physiquement éprouvante maintenant que je suis enceinte de huit mois. Le matin Alaa ouvre la fenêtre en l’occurrence un pan de bâche sur le côté de la tente. Une ouverture donnant sur l’extérieur. À mesure que ses yeux s’habituent à la lumière, elle constate que tout, à perte de vue, est détruit. Le paysage n’est qu’un amas de béton fracassé et d’acier tordu. Aujourd’hui, j’ai un rendez-vous prénatal pour suivre l’évolution de la grossesse. Le lieu est éloigné et je m’y rends à pied, généralement, aucun véhicule ne peut m’y conduire. Il fait 34°C, et marcher dans les rues bombardées, jonchées de décombres et grouillantes d’insectes, en pleine chaleur, est une épreuve épuisante. Le centre où je reçois mes soins prénataux est une tente et non un véritable établissement de santé. Les médecins m’ont prescrit des compléments nutritionnels pour ma grossesse. J’ai déjà été enceinte par le passé mais je sens que cette grossesse est différente. Malgré tous mes efforts pour compenser les carences nutritionnelles et les privations alimentaires subies pendant la guerre, mon corps reste épuisé. La nourriture se fait rare. Mon mari m’achète des fruits et des légumes mais refuse d’en manger lui-même car il n’a les moyens d’en acheter qu’en petite quantité. Lorsque j’ai appris que j’étais enceinte, j’ai ressenti deux émotions totalement contradictoires. J’étais heureuse d’attendre un enfant mais je pleurais aussi sans cesse car mes enfants –Waseem, Mohannad et Khawla– me manquaient. Tout me les rappelle. Quand j’ai envie de manger certains aliments, je pense à Waseem car j’aimais beaucoup en manger quand j’étais enceinte de lui. Je ne parle pas aux infirmières de ma situation ni de mes enfants décédés car le personnel soignant est lui aussi émotionnellement épuisé. Ils ne sont pas en mesure d’offrir du réconfort ou un soutien psychologique. Mon histoire n’a rien d’exceptionnel à Gaza. Beaucoup de femmes ici ont perdu leurs enfants. Après le rendez-vous avec le nutritionniste, j’ai également une consultation avec le psychologue de la maternité. On me conseille de me concentrer sur ma respiration: inspirer profondément, retenir mon souffle puis expirer lentement. Ensuite, je rentre chez moi à pied. L’après-midi S’attaquant à nouveau aux marches, Alaa hisse un sac à dos bleu jusqu’à la tente. Il contient quelques vêtements de ses enfants disparus, qu’elle espère voir portés un jour par le bébé à naître. Beaucoup d’entre eux ont été abîmés par le souffle de l’explosion: déchirés, les bords brûlés, mais encore portables. Elle déplie avec précaution un T-shirt Snoopy et un bonnet à deux pompons duveteux puis en sort une écharpe aux couleurs du Castleview AFC —un petit club de football de Cork— que son fils Waseem chérissait. «Il la portait tout le temps, même en été. Je lui disais: Waseem, il fait trop chaud, enlève-la! Et il répondait: Non, je l’adore.» Je passe l’après-midi avec mon frère à réfléchir à la manière de ranger les vêtements pour le bébé à venir. Il suggère une boîte solide en carton ou en bois. Ce qui nous inquiète, ce sont les rats, ils sont partout. Nous les entendons chaque nuit et ils finissent toujours par s’introduire dans la tente. J’avais recousu l’endroit par lequel ils entraient, mais ils en ont rongé un nouveau. Aujourd’hui, nous avons découvert un autre trou dans la paroi de la tente. Je me demande si nous pourrions utiliser de la mort-aux-rats mais mon frère craint que les rongeurs ne meurent ici, dans la tente, et ne propagent des maladies. Pour le bébé qui va naître, tout ce que je veux, c’est un endroit sûr, hors de portée des rats. Le bébé sera si petit et je suis terrifiée pour lui. J’aimerais avoir un vrai berceau pour lui mais il est difficile d’en trouver à Gaza en ce moment et la tente est déjà surpeuplée. Ce que j’aimerais que le monde extérieur comprenne, c’est à quel point la vie sous une tente est humiliante. C’est une existence difficile, avilissante et profondément inhumaine. La mort nous entoure encore de toutes parts. La soirée Alors que la fin de l’après-midi approche, Alaa fait défiler les photos de ses enfants décédés sur son téléphone. L’appareil qui les contient —comme tant d’autres à Gaza— est vétuste et son écran est fissuré. Après un long blocus, de nouveaux smartphones arrivent désormais mais ils sont chers et beaucoup de familles n’ont pas les moyens de se les offrir. Dans une vidéo, les voix des enfants s’élèvent, ténues, du haut-parleur du téléphone. Khawla et son frère aîné se taquinent: «Maman, c’est moi la plus gentille!» , crie Khawla. Mohannad rit et répond: «Non, c’est moi le plus gentil!» . Je ne parle vraiment de mes enfants qu’avec mon mari. C’est la seule personne qui partage la même douleur et qui comprend vraiment ce que je ressens au fond de moi. Quand je faiblis, il me donne de la force. Quand il traverse des moments difficiles, j’essaie de le réconforter et de le soutenir émotionnellement. Nous passons des heures à parler de nos enfants, de leur personnalité, de ce qu’ils aimaient et de leur façon d’être. Nous nous rendons même ensemble sur leurs tombes. Cet endroit garde encore les souvenirs de mes enfants. Il me rappelle la belle vie que nous avions autrefois. En regardant ces décombres, je pense à mes enfants, à la vie que j’ai partagée avec eux, les élever, leur préparer à manger et à les enseigner. Tout ce qui était beau a disparu après leur départ. Parfois, la peur m’envahit car j’ai perdu mes enfants et je crains de perdre aussi mon bébé. J’espère que mon nouveau-né connaîtra une vie meilleure que celle de ses frères et de sa sœur et qu’il sera en sécurité. *Peu après le recueil de ce témoignage, Alaa a donné naissance à un petit garçon en bonne santé. Elle l’a prénommé Waseem, en hommage à son frère aîné. **La « ligne jaune » à Gaza est une ligne de cessez-le-feu et de déploiement militaire établie en octobre 2025 dans le cadre du plan de paix. Matérialisée sur le terrain par de grands blocs de béton peints en jaune, elle divise la bande de Gaza en deux zones distinctes: l’ouest, sous contrôle palestinien et l’est/sud, sous contrôle de l’armée israélienne. L’article À quoi ressemble le quotidien d’une femme enceinte à Gaza? est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: How Trump's diplomatic week exposed the limits of his power
items.description: From his high-profile address to the UN General Assembly to his high-stakes White House summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping , US President Donald Trump this week was looking to reassert himself on the world stage. But Trump’s diplomatic flurry has done little to dispel the view among many analysts of a president beset by problems at home and abroad. Those include a widening Iran war that has driven up US gasoline prices and cratered his approval ratings, while his relations with allies worsen and the AI challenge from China intensifies. With the limits of his power exposed, Trump has begun facing pushback from world leaders on issues ranging from the crisis in the Middle East to Russia’s war in Ukraine , leaving the impression of a foreign policy agenda that has stalled. This comes as Trump’s Republican Party faces midterm elections in November that could further constrain him politically. Even so, Trump’s speech to the United Nations on Tuesday was a stark reminder of how, since returning to the White House last year, he has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped to create from the ashes of World War Two. Standing atop the rostrum of a world body dedicated to peacemaking, he issued a fresh threat to annihilate Iran if it did not agree to a deal, defended his coercive approach to OPEC member Venezuela by asserting to the victor belong the spoils, and signaled he may not be done deploying the US military to achieve his international aims. Despite that strident stance, Trump’s talks with Xi on Thursday put the US president up against a Chinese counterpart who appeared to be in stronger position, overseeing a surge in his country’s trade with the world while the US grapples with the economic fallout from the Iran conflict. Limited results from Xi summit That was the backdrop for a state visit by Xi that was heavy on pomp and ceremony but light on substance, despite a host of thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and Iran. The most tangible outcome appeared limited to a two-month extension of a trade truce, originally due to expire in November, between the world’s two biggest economies. While Trump showed little interest in publicly airing any differences between the two powers, Chinese state media reported that behind closed doors Xi urged him to oppose independence for Taiwan. The democratically governed island claimed by China remains the most contentious topic in relations between Washington and Beijing. China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump pose on the North Portico steps of the White House ahead of a State Dinner in Washington, DC, on September 24, 2026. —AFP Trump’s seemingly non-confrontational attitude was a far cry from his previously hawkish, tariffs-driven approach, which has been tempered by Beijing’s control over rare earth minerals, a key input for technology and auto manufacturing that Beijing has shown the ability to withhold in retaliation. “Trump sees himself taking us back to a world where might makes right,” said Brett Bruen, who was a foreign policy adviser in the Obama administration and now heads the Global Situation Room strategic consultancy. “But its noteworthy that he goes all wobbly when it comes to Xi Jinping and ascendant Chinese power.” Responding to Reuters questions, a White House official rejected the notion that Trump’s foreign policy had hit a wall and said his UN remarks “highlighted his various wins in advancing US interests around the world,” including preventing Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. Tehran has always said its nuclear program is for peaceful purposes. Iran war stalemate Looming over Trump’s packed week of diplomacy was the war with Iran, which he started alongside Israel on February 28. It has dragged on for nearly seven months, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region most recently to Yemen and the Red Sea shipping corridor. Iran’s defiance, despite the economic and military beating it has taken, has become the most intractable foreign policy challenge of Trump’s second term. Trump used his address at the UN to defend his attack on Iran and to declare that America is back, stronger than ever. But after a string of early foreign policy achievements, including a Gaza ceasefire and the capture of Venezuela’s leader , Trump’s record in his second term in office is increasingly defined by stalemates. Pro-Palestinian demonstrators protest against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, in Times Square, New York, US on September 24, 2026.—Reuters With the Iran war deeply unpopular and dividing Trump’s political base, he could pay a price in the midterm congressional elections when his Republican Party’s control of Congress is at risk. World leaders appear to be preparing for a time when the US president’s influence could begin to wane following the midterms, and with less than two-and-a-half years left in office. Most European and Asian allies have already spurned Trump’s demands for assistance in an Iran conflict he launched without consulting them. At this year’s UN gathering , some US partners took aim at Trump, though mostly without mentioning him by name. France’s President Emmanuel Macron warned against a global “return to the law of the jungle,” saying countries faced a choice between a world governed by power and coercion, and a “civilised international society.” In a rebuke to Trump, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva decried foreign interference in his country’s October election and insisted that “we do not need aircraft carriers patrolling our waters, we need cooperation to stem the flow of weapons and money that fuel crime”. The White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that Trump was “not concerned with posturing but about results” and that some leaders’ public comments did not match what they told the president in private. Resisting Trump In another sign of diminished clout, Trump’s effort to pressure Ukraine and Russia to agree to even a limited energy ceasefire failed to gain much traction. And while Trump touted a deal with Denmark and Greenland for an expanded US military presence in the vast Arctic island, it fell short of his initial demand to own the territory and his threat, if necessary, to take it by force from a fellow Nato member. US President Donald Trump makes a toast during a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House in Washington, DC, US on September 24, 2026. —Reuters A year ago, few countries dared cross Trump, Ian Bremmer, president of the Eurasia Group, wrote on X. Now Canada, Europe, China, Iran, Russia and others are all more willing to say no. At one point, Trump himself seemed to wonder how much international sway he actually possessed. In his speech, he told world leaders he wanted to rebrand AI as super intelligence. “Let’s see if I have any power,” he said. “Maybe I do and maybe I don’t. We’re going to find out pretty soon.” Header image: US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US on September 22, 2026. —Reuters

items.title: Transferts de devises d’Algérie vers la Turquie : des commerçants risquent de lourdes peines
items.description: En Algérie, louer son registre de commerce peut rapporter et mener en prison. Plusieurs individus se sont retrouvés mêlés à une affaire de transfert de devises vers l’étranger. L'affaire est jugée devant le pôle pénal économique et financier de Sidi M'hamed (Alger). Le principal accusé est un importateur de vêtements de Turquie. Le parquet a requis de lourdes peines contre le mis en cause et plusieurs autres accusés, dont plusieurs personnes qui ont loué leurs registre de commerce. Il promettait 10 millions sur chaque milliard de bénéfice Selon un compte-rendu d’Ennahar, le principal accusé, désigné sous les initiales B.A., possède dix sociétés spécialisées dans l’importation de vêtements de Turquie. Dans l'acte d'accusation, il est indiqué que l’importateur a effectué des opérations d’importation illégales de Turquie, blanchi et transféré des sommes colossales en devises vers ce pays où il réside, avec la complicité de plusieurs commerçants qui lui ont loué leurs registres de commerce moyennant une commission de 10 millions de centimes sur chaque milliard de centimes de bénéfice réalisé. Les mis en cause sont poursuivis pour blanchiment d'argent, infraction à la législation de change et du mouvement de capitaux de et vers l'étranger, faux et usage de faux dans les écritures commerciales et bancaires, abus de fonction et octroi d'indus avantages à des tiers. Le parquet requiert 12 ans de prison À l'audience, les commerçants mis en cause ont nié les faits, déclarant qu’ils ne connaissaient pas l’accusé principal. Ils ont reconnu avoir loué leurs registres de commerce, mais pas à l’importateur mis en cause dans cette affaire. Devant la gravité des faits, le représentant du parquet a requis de lourdes peines contre les accusés, allant jusqu'à 12 ans de prison ferme. Le représentant du Trésor public a réclamé 300 millions de centimes de dédommagement à chacun des mis en cause. L’article Transferts de devises d’Algérie vers la Turquie : des commerçants risquent de lourdes peines est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: NBA G League United's visits to China strengthen basketball exchanges
items.description: NBA G League United made two trips to China in less than a month, competing against Chinese Basketball Association teams in Shanghai and Beijing while also taking part in exchanges with some of the country's professional players and young prospects. The developmental club made its China debut in Shanghai in late August, facing reigning CBA champions the Shanghai Sharks in two exhibition games at the inaugural NBA Shanghai Basketball Festival on August 28th and 30th. NBA G League United then returned to China for the 2026 FIBA Intercontinental Cup in Beijing, where they beat the Beijing Royal Fighters 119-89 at the National Indoor Stadium on Wednesday. Formed in 2024 to represent the NBA's developmental league in international competition, NBA G League United's roster also featured a player with recent connections to Chinese basketball. Guard Lester Quinones played for the CBA's Qingdao Eagles last season, before joining the select team for its latest international campaign. There were familiar faces on the other side of the court as well. Beijing guards Grant Riller and Daishen Nix both previously competed in the NBA G League, with Riller having played for the CBA's Royal Fighters since 2023. The visits provided opportunities for players from both countries to exchange ideas and experience different styles of basketball. Shanghai guard Li Tianrong said his team learned from NBA G League United's pace at both ends of the court and picked up on various details of the American players' individual skills. Sharks coach Lu Wei also welcomed cross-Pacific basketball exchanges, saying Chinese teams can benefit whether they travel to the United States or host American clubs at home. The interaction extended beyond professional competition. On their first trip, the NBA G League United players visited the Bund and met young players from the Shanghai Guangming High School basketball team. From exhibition games in Shanghai to international competition in Beijing and meetings with young players, the two visits served as the latest platform for basketball exchanges between China and the United States.

items.title: Full text: Toast by Xi at state dinner hosted by Trump
items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered remarks at a state dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C. on Thursday. The following is the full text of Xi's toast at the banquet: Honorable President Donald J. Trump and Mrs. Melania Trump, Ladies and gentlemen, Dear friends, Thank you, Mr. President and Mrs. Trump, for extending to my wife and me your gracious hospitality and thoughtful arrangements. You and Mrs. Trump have made many special arrangements for our visit, all prepared with meticulous care and consideration in every detail. You make us feel truly at home. I would also like to extend my sincere greetings to Americans from all sectors of society who care about China-US relations and support the further growth of our bilateral ties. As I speak, my compatriots in China are celebrating the Mid-Autumn Festival – a cherished occasion for family reunion in Chinese tradition. I wish you all a very happy Mid-Autumn Festival, and my best wishes to you and your families. In May this year, President Trump paid a successful visit to China at my invitation. We agreed to build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability. During the visit, President Trump warmly invited me to visit the United States, and I have come as promised. In less than half a year, the Chinese and American presidents have exchanged state visits, making history in our bilateral engagement. Today, President Trump and I had sincere and in-depth exchanges and reached common understanding on many issues. This has added new substance to the constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, and provided new strategic guidance for China-US relations. Not long ago, the United States celebrated the 250th anniversary of its independence. On that occasion, I sent my congratulations on behalf of the Chinese government and people. The past 200-plus years have also witnessed friendly exchanges between China and the United States. Over 200 years ago, soon after its independence, the United States turned its eyes to China. Our two countries started trading with each other, exchanging goods to meet each other's needs and draw on our complementary strengths. In fact, President George Washington had personally acquired a large collection of Chinese porcelain. Over 80 years ago, the Chinese and American people stood shoulder to shoulder in the fight against Japanese militarist aggressors. Together we opened the famous Hump air route over the Himalayas. During the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, Chinese soldiers and civilians rescued hundreds of American pilots at the cost of hundreds of thousands of Chinese lives. Such a friendship, forged in blood and fire, will surely live on through the generations. Over 50 years ago, Ping-Pong diplomacy between China and the United States reopened the door to bilateral exchanges that had been closed for years. With the political wisdom embodied in "a small ball moving the globe," the older generation of Chinese and American statesmen, led by Chairman Mao Zedong and President Richard Nixon, set in motion the historic process of normalizing relations between our two countries. The redwood trees that President Nixon had presented as a special state gift have taken root in Zhejiang Province where I worked for several years. Over 20 years ago, an American named Ronald Sakolsky gave financial support to Yin Yuzhen, a Chinese desert control worker, for her tree-planting effort. Just recently, Ronald, now an elderly man, returned to China. He saw with his own eyes that the desert back then had turned into a lush forest. This story touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between our two peoples. Exchanges have helped promote heart-to-heart communication between our people and cemented public support for Sino-US friendship and cooperation. Ladies and gentlemen, Dear friends, Reviewing the past gives us new perspectives. Today, we have come to another historic juncture for China-US relations. President Trump has pledged to make America great again and led the American people in making significant strides. China is committed to achieving great national rejuvenation, and Chinese modernization has kept breaking new ground. These two goals are both ambitious and can surely be mutually reinforcing. China and the United States must act as responsible major countries, meet the expectations of our peoples, keep pace with the trend of our times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other. Like a river that never stops flowing, history never stands still. The friendship between the two peoples is a worthy cause that holds great promise. Let us join hands and move forward side by side. Together, let us nurture the beautiful flowers of Sino-US friendship. Together, let us write a new chapter in our friendly relations. Now, I would like to propose a toast: To the health of President and Mrs. Trump; To the prosperity and progress of China and the United States; and To the friendship between our two peoples. Cheers!

items.title: Security forces kill several Afghan Taliban fighters in retaliatory action along Balochistan border: sources
items.description: Pakistani troops responded to an act of aggression along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Balochistan and killed several Afghan Taliban on Thursday, state media reported, citing sources. State-run APP reported, citing sources, that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter the Pakistani territory in Balochistan’s Gulistan sector and carry out an act of aggression. Meanwhile, officials also reported attacks on some border posts in Pakistan. The APP report said in retaliatory action, several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed. Intermittent exchange of fire between security forces and Afghan Taliban was ongoing after midnight, according the sources cited in the report. There has been an uptick in tensions at the Pak-Afghan border lately. Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said earlier in the day. The response came after eight drones, launched from Afghanistan, entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat on Wednesday. Security sources said they were subsequently shot down. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan. On Sept 21, Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations. A statement from the information ministry on Monday said that over 28 terrorists were eliminated in the strikes. “It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” the ministry said at the time, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”. The airstrikes had come after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area. Ghazab lil-Haq Tarar described Pakistan’s action as part of its ongoing counter-terrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq. On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts. Pakistan also carried out strikes in the border region with Afghanistan in late June , with the government saying they were in response to a wave of terrorist attacks, including one on a Rangers camp in Karachi . At the time, Tarar said that 25 terrorists were killed in those strikes in Paktia, Paktika and Kunar. Pakistan had carried out similar strikes on terrorist hideouts along its border with Afghanistan earlier that month, killing 26 terrorists. In July, security forces responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban at border posts in Kurram, security sources had said. In the same month, the Afghan Taliban regime launched four rudimentary drones across the border into Balochistan, which were shot down by security forces. Two drones were also shot down in June in Qila Abdullah and Chagai districts. Pak-Afghan ties As clashes continue, tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have remained high. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. Earlier this week, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he called for steps towards concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan. Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional and international peace and security. Last week, Pakistan also told the UN Security Council that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law. Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory. It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure. According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from December 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group. The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA). Additional input from Saleem Shahid

items.title: La Chine et les États-Unis peuvent-ils s’accorder sur la sécurité de l’IA ?
items.description: L’IA est désormais au cœur de la confrontation sino-américaine. La manière dont les deux puissances pourraient s’accorder pour continuer à développer la technologie tout en délimitant un cadre pour en gérer les risques est l’une des questions clefs de la visite d’État de Xi aux États-Unis qui s’achève aujourd’hui, vendredi 25. Si leurs motivations diffèrent, Pékin et Washington tendent à reléguer la sécurité au second plan. L'administration Trump a tendance à considérer la course à l'IA comme une question de sécurité nationale : une victoire chinoise donnerait à Pékin un avantage stratégique considérable. En Chine, certains chercheurs estiment que la sécurité des modèles les plus avancés est moins urgente, puisque les laboratoires chinois accusent un retard sur leurs concurrents américains China Also Thinks AI Could Kill Us. But First, It Wants to Match the U.S. », The Wall Street Journal , 14 septembre 2026.[/note ]. Dans les deux cas, ralentir le développement de l'IA au profit de la sécurité relèverait d'un choix qu'aucune des deux puissances ne pense pouvoir assumer. Pour Cheryl Wu, doctorante en économie à Yale, l'idée que le retard chinois permettrait de différer les questions de sécurité repose sur une prémisse fragile : un retard en capacités ne garantirait pas un retard en incidents. Elle avance ainsi trois hypothèses 1 Cheryl Wu, China’s AI-safety trajectory is not necessarily a delayed version of America’s , 23 septembre 2026.'> 2 : Tout d'abord, les incidents pourraient survenir à un niveau de capacité plus faible pour les modèles chinois, notamment en raison de la diffusion de modèles open-weight. Leur nature et leur gravité pourraient aussi varier en fonction de la manière dont les modèles sont exploités par les utilisateurs. Les modèles américains pourraient notamment plus souvent entreprendre des actions sans autorisation, tandis que les modèles chinois pourraient exploiter des failles dans leur système de récompense plutôt que d'accomplir la tâche donnée. Il faut également prendre en compte la manière dont les deux pays peuvent traiter la divulgation des incidents de sécurité. Contrairement aux États-Unis, où METR a notamment pu tester les systèmes de surveillance d'Anthropic, il n’y a aucun cas d'intégration d'évaluateurs tiers au sein d'entreprises chinoises. Moins d'incidents signalés ne signifierait donc pas moins d'incidents. Enfin, il reste à savoir comment réagirait la Chine face à un incident d'ampleur lié à un modèle d'IA, et notamment quel serait le seuil à partir duquel le pouvoir chinois considérerait qu'un « problème » mérite une intervention. https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/66ziA Au-delà des questions économiques, le Parti communiste s’inquiète des conséquences que pourrait faire peser l’IA sur sa maîtrise du processus politique. Dans un article publié le 13 septembre, le secrétaire du Parti et ministre du Département de la Sécurité d’État, Chen Yixin, évoque notamment le risque que des « individus aux intentions malveillantes » utilisent la technologie pour « inventer des rumeurs politiques, diffuser des informations malveillantes, inciter au conflit et attiser les tensions dans l’opinion publique », et cela « dans des proportions importantes et à des coûts très faibles ». L’article La Chine et les États-Unis peuvent-ils s’accorder sur la sécurité de l’IA ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Senate body orders probe into ‘overcharging’ by telco
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Com­mittee on Information Technology and Tele­c­ommunication has constituted a subcommittee to investigate allegations that a leading telecom firm had charged customers Rs5.83 billion in excess of tariffs approved by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA). The subcommittee, headed by Senator Dr Afnanullah Khan, will examine the alleged overcharging by Jazz and the regulatory action taken by the PTA in the matter. The decision was taken following a heated debate between PTA officials and representatives of the Auditor General of Pakistan (AGP). Committee Chairperson Senator Palwasha Khan intervened to pacify the situation when the PTA chairman threatened to resign if any allegation of corruption was levelled against him. Meanwhile, a Jazz spokesperson said the matter concerned two government entities and that Jazz would present its point of view if called before any relevant forum. The matter relates to the audit of the PTA for 2024. The audit objection stated that the telecom regulator had allowed a 15 per cent tariff increase for Jazz against a permissible limit of 3pc. The audit also suggested seeking the opinion of the Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP) on the tariff policy. PTA Chairman retired Maj Gen Hafeezur Rehman questioned the proposal, saying that if tariffs were to be decided by the CCP, the PTA should not be held responsible for ensuring quality of service. “Let them take the whole responsibility,” he said. He maintained that the regulator had acted with complete transparency in allowing the 15pc tariff increase for Jazz and offered to have the matter subjected to a forensic audit. The PTA chairman categorically stated that he would resign if even one rupee of overcharging by the telecom operator was established in violation of the authority’s approved tariffs. He explained that the PTA examined mobile packages before their launch and monitored compliance with the approved tariff structure. However, audit officials had raised certain queries regarding the matter. Senator Palwasha Khan subsequently decided to constitute the subcommittee. It will examine the relevant tariff approvals, packages and billing details to determine whether customers were charged amounts beyond the rates approved by the regulator. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: Govt limits public disclosure of bureaucrats’ assets
items.description: • Selected asset information of BS-17, above officers to be made public • Government cites security concerns for withholding full asset declarations ISLAMABAD: The government will not fully disclose the assets of civil servants due to security concerns and will instead publish selected information by December this year to meet requirem­ents of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal told the National Assembly Stan­ding Committee on Finance and Revenue on Thursday. However, parliamentarians questioned why full details would not be made public when politicians, including the president and prime minister, were required to disclose their assets. They questioned why public servants should be treated differently when parliamentarians and politicians were required to make full asset declarations. Mr Bosal did not directly respond to the objection but said a lot of technical work had been undertaken by the Establishment Division and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). Under the mechanism, the FBR would assess the data and report its findings to the Establishment Division, which would have the power to initiate disciplinary action in case of any discrepancy. The fi­­nance secretary said civil servants’ asse­­ts would be declared under prescribed gui­delines but would not be published in full. The government has already moved to digitise declarations of income and assets of all federal civil servants in BS-17 and above, replacing the existing manual submission process with a dedicated FBR online portal. The declarations will undergo risk-based verification, while selected non-sensitive information will be made public. Soon afterwards, the Ministry of Fin­a­nce published on its website an office me­­morandum issued by the Establishment Division last week regarding the “digitisation of declaration of assets under Section 15-A of the Civil Servants Act, 1973”. According to the memorandum, the Establishment Division, in collaboration with the FBR, has launched a digitised system for the submission, verification and publication of declarations of income and assets under Section 15-A of the Civil Servants Act, 1973, and Rule 12 of the Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules, 2026. All officers in BS-17 and above are required to submit their declarations of income and assets for financial year 2025-26 through the dedicated FBR portal instead of the existing manual process. The deadline for digital filing has been set at Oct 30, 2026, in accordance with Rule 12(6) of the Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules, 2026. Under the new mechanism, officers will first have to provide their name, designation, personal active email address, mobile number and CNIC to their respective cadre administrator for creation of an account on the FBR portal. The cadre administrator will forward the officers’ details to the FBR, which will notify them about account creation through email, SMS or other prescribed means. Officers will then activate their accounts using their CNIC and a one-time password to set their own password. Once logged in, officers will find a “Declaration” option on the FBR portal dashboard. By selecting this option, they will be required to enter the requisite information through subsequent screens, with the details specified in Annex-I of the Establishment Division’s memorandum. The information submitted by officers will subsequently be subjected to risk-based verification checks by the FBR, which will communicate the results to the relevant cadre administrator. Establishment Division said selected non-sensitive sections of the declarations would be published on the FBR website for information of the general public. The declarations must be filed within the prescribed deadline, while any rectification of errors on the portal will be permissible up to Nov 30, 2026, subject to approval or authorisation of the cadre administrator concerned. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: La deuda de la justicia con Dolores Vázquez: 25 años sin reparar los 519 días de cárcel de una inocente
items.description: Pocos días antes de jubilarse, el juez Fernando González Zubieta citó en su despacho de la Audiencia de Málaga al penalista Pedro Apalategui. “Por favor, dile a Dolores Vázquez que le tengo cariño y deseo que sea feliz”. No solo hay cordialidad en ese mensaje. Ahí adentro se puede intuir un pesar rocoso cimentado durante años, los que habían pasado desde que el magistrado condenó en 2001 a Dolores Vázquez a 15 años y un día de prisión por un asesinato que no cometió. “Que me dijera aquello le honra. Le vi dolido. Fue el único”, afirma Apalategui en su casa de Málaga, a pocas semanas de que se cumplan los 25 años de un juicio que le marcó la vida. Nadie más de los que levantaron aquella pira en la que ardió Dolores Vázquez le mostró arrepentimiento . La vista había sido un espectáculo, concluida con el público aplaudiendo el veredicto como en un teatro mientras Apalategui cubría con su toga a la acusada para impedir que las cámaras grabaran para la eternidad su desmoronamiento. Vázquez se había sentido protegida tras su inocencia e insistió en ella en su alegato final: “Busquen a los culpables, que están ahí fuera. Nunca han tenido nada contra mí y no lo tendrán porque soy inocente”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Negociar con el hombre que asesinó a tu madre: “La descuartizó y tuvimos que pactar para que no saliera de la cárcel”
items.description: La abogada había citado a Ferran Montón junto a sus hijas Thais y Thania a una videollamada urgente para revelarles la peor de las noticias: “Van a soltar al asesino”. Cuando las hermanas escucharon estas palabras, sintieron que el suelo desaparecía bajo sus pies. No entendían cómo la justicia iba a dejar libre al hombre que a finales de 2021 ahogó, quemó y descuartizó a su madre, Carmen Ortiz, de 57 años. Su letrada, Nuria Milà, les explicó la crudeza de la ley: una persona no puede pasar más de cuatro años en prisión preventiva y el procedimiento judicial para aclarar el asesinato se había dilatado tanto que ese límite estaba a escasas semanas de cumplirse. items.title: ‘La bola negra’: estética e hipersensible
items.description: Pocas veces he constatado un grado tan alto de expectación no ya entre la cinefilia, sino también en gente de la calle que quiere saber mi opinión sobre una película titulada La bola negra . Viene avalada por premios lujosos en festivales, en la tantas veces falsa suposición de que esos galardones han sido bendecidos por la infalible gracia de Dios, y por una espectacular campaña de marketing cultural y apoteosis de lo woke . Y uno es proclive a las manías y a los prejuicios. Pero estoy dispuesto a creerme la excelencia cinematográfica de Javier Ambrossi y de Javier Calvo (el público y los profesionales deberían prescindir de ese colegueo tan moderno de identificarlos todo el rato como Los Javis), después de haber quedado fascinado con su talento visual y expresivo, con su capacidad para inventarse un universo tan siniestro como mágico, con su poder para transmitir una atmósfera entre misteriosa y lírica como hicieron en su admirable serie La Mesías . Seguir leyendo La bola negra Dirección: Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo. Intérpretes: Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Lola Dueñas, Penélope Cruz, Glenn Close. En el momento en el que su nombre empezó a ocupar titulares por su papel protagonista en la serie Riverdale (2017-2023), en la que interpretó a Betty Cooper, el control sobre lo que quería —y lo que no— en su vida pareció escaparse de sus manos. Al mismo tiempo que su fama iba creciendo, también tuvo que enfrentarse a sus inseguridades y a la exposición constante de una vida que, de repente, pertenecía también al público.
